Edited by Hu Shengyou of Huan’an in Xiangshui;
the fifth-generation successor of Dajian (Mazu) in the lineage of Yaoshan Yan.
Chan Master Decheng of Huating in Xiuzhou was of lofty character and peerless capacity.
Having received the seal of his mind from Yaoshan, he shared the path with Daowu and Yunyan.
Upon departing from Yaoshan, he said to his two companions, "You two should each occupy a region and establish the school of Yaoshan; as for me, my nature is by disposition indolent."
He lived in the wilds, fond only of mountains and rivers, seeking to dispel his emotions through pleasure; he was skilled in nothing else.

Later, learning of my place of residence, he sent a man upon encountering a spiritually sharp *zhu-zu* (abbot) who might be capable of refinement, so that I could transmit what I had acquired throughout my life to repay the kindness of my former teacher.
Thereupon we parted ways. Arriving at Huating in Xiuzhou, I took a small boat and followed along.
Because he crossed the waters daily to receive those coming and going from the four quarters, people of the time did not know of his lofty conduct;
thus he was called the Boatman Monk. One day, while mooring his boat by the shore and sitting idly, an official asked, "What is the Master’s daily practice?
The Master held up his oar and said, "Do you understand? The official said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The oar strokes."
In the clear waves, golden scales are rarely encountered. The Master had a verse that said: For thirty years I have sat upon the fishing platform;

From time to time, I catch the *huangneng* fish on my hook. Failing to meet the golden-scaled one, my efforts are in vain; I gather up my line and return home. A thousand feet of line hang straight down;
As soon as a single wave stirs, ten thousand follow. The night is still and the water cold; the fish do not bite. Full [is the boat].
The boat returns empty under the bright moon. For thirty years I have roamed upon the sea; when the water is clear, the fish appear but do not swallow the hook.
The fishing rods have been cut down and bamboo has been planted anew; I do not calculate the time or effort, for I rest as soon as the opportunity arises.

There is a fish, magnificent beyond measure; its harmonious fusion and all-encompassing nature are truly marvelous. It can transform and breathe forth wind and thunder; yet though the line is cast, how could it ever be caught?
Come! Others merely gaze at the plucking of lotuses; their fragrance clings long to the wind around their fingers.
On both banks, a single boat reflects crimson. How could it ever stain the void? When asked about my livelihood, I say it is simply this boat;
sons and grandsons each gamble for their own karmic conditions. It depends neither on earth nor heaven; aside from the raincoat, there is nothing to pass down. Later, Daowu arrived in the capital.
[The Master] went to meet Jiaoshan as he was ascending the hall. A monk asked, "What is the Dharma-body? Jiaoshan said, "The Dharma-body has no form.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Dharma-eye? Jiaoshan said, "The Dharma-eye has no flaw. Daowu could not help but let out a laugh.
Jiaoshan immediately descended from his seat and asked Daowu, "In my response to that monk just now, there must have been something incorrect, which caused you to—"
The Elder laughed. Hoping that the Elder would not withhold his compassion, I said, "Venerable Sir, you are equally one who has transcended the world, yet you still have no teacher.
Zhaozhou said, "In what way am I at fault? I hope you will explain it to me. I said, "I shall certainly not say anything.
I ask that you instead go to Shipin at Huating. Zhaozhou asked, "What is this man like?"
I said, "This man has not a single tile above him and not the space for a锥 (chui) to rest upon below him. If you, Master, are going there, you must change your attire before you go.
Deshan then dismissed his assembly and, having packed his belongings, went straight to Huating. As soon as Chuanshi saw him, he asked, "Virtuous One, in what monastery do you reside?
Deshan replied, "As for a monastery, I do not reside in one; were I to reside in one, it would not be like this. The Master [Chuanshi] asked, "What is it that is not like this?"
Mao asked, "Is it not the Dharma before one's eyes? Shan said, "It is not something reached by the ears or the eyes.
The Master said, "A single phrase that fits the head is a tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas. The Master asked again, "With a line lowered a thousand feet, the intent lies in the deep pool.
When you are three inches away from the hook, why do you not speak? As Shan prepared to open his mouth, the Master struck him once.

He struck him with the oar, knocking him into the water. As soon as Shanshan climbed back onto the boat, the Master said again, "Speak! Speak! Just as Shanshan was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him once more.
Shanshan attained a sudden, great enlightenment and nodded his head three times. The Master said, "The line on the tip of the pole is for you to handle as you please."
"Without violating the clear waves, the intent is naturally distinct. Yaoshan then asked, "Regarding casting the line and throwing the hook—what is your intention, Master?

The Master said, "The line hangs in the green water; floating, it holds the meaning of both existence and non-existence. Yaoshan said, "The words carry the profound yet there is no path; the tongue speaks, yet it does not speak.

The Master said, "When the river's waves have been fished dry, only then is the golden-scaled fish encountered. Yaoshan then covered his ears. The Master said: *Note: This passage is from the *Wudeng Huiyuan* (Jewel Source of the Five Lamps), a collection of Zen records. The dialogue concerns the art of fishing as a metaphor for the pursuit of awakening.*
"So it is, so it is. He then instructed him, saying: "In going forth, you must vanish where there is no trace;
do not hide yourself where there is no trace. For thirty years I was at Yaoshan, and I clarified only this matter. You have now attained it."
"In the future, do not dwell in cities or villages. Go instead into the deep mountains, by the side of your mattock, and seek out one or two [disciples];
continue this lineage so that it is never severed. When Shanshan took his leave, he looked back again and again. The Master then called out, "Śrāmaṇera! Shanshan turned his head.
The Master held up his oar and said, "You thought there was something else; here is the overturning of the boat. He then entered [the mountain].
He departed by way of water.
A monk asked Master Jinsha, the Dharma heir of Linji Xuanshi, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Listen. The monk said, "In that case..."
The great assembly listened intently. The Master said, "One hundred and eight thousand.
Later, a monk asked Yizhou Yingtian Wenheshang, the Dharma heir of Guishan Lingyou: "Everyone possesses Buddha-nature; what is the Buddha-nature of the Master?"
Xing asked, "Master, what do you call 'Buddha-nature'? The Master said, "If that were so, then you, Reverend, would have no Buddha-nature.
The Master then cried out, "What joy! What joy!"
The Sixth Generation under Dajian [Huairang]:
Chan Master Baishui of Jiashan Hui, a successor of the lineage, was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The four oceans have no lair."
The Dwelling: A single drop moistens heaven and earth. When asked, "What do you discuss on the single path of Caoxi? the Master said: "A thousand-year-old pine by the mountain stream gathers cranes;
the fragrant cassia in the moonlight welcomes the phoenix. When asked, "What is this sutra? the Master said:
"The shuttle-thrown stone woman echoes across the vast void; the mud-ox at the bottom of the sea cries out frequently at night."
Xiangyan Xian was the dharma heir of Chan Master Wuran of Nanchan in Yizhou. A monk asked, "Regarding the phrase that has no phrase, does the Master still have an answer?
The Master said, "From the beginning, I have only clarified this very matter. The monk asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "Just ask and see."
A monk asked the Monk of Changping Mountain in Yizhou, "What is it like at the point where even a blink of an eye is impossible?
The Master said, "I do not even have the leisure to blink. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch? The Master said, "Coming from India, going to Tang China."
A monk asked Chan Master Yongjia Chengfu Yanjiao of Yizhou, “What are words that are vast and expansive?
The Master said, “To speak without a mouth. The monk asked, “What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, “Today and tomorrow.”
Touzi, a Dharma successor of Xichuan Qingcheng Xiangshan Chengzhao Chan Master, was asked by a monk: "When the Buddhas encounter difficulties, they hide their bodies within the flames.
I wonder, when a patch-robed monk encounters difficulties, where does he hide his body? The Master replied: "Inside a crystal jar."
While staying at Bosi, he was asked, "What is the newly risen moon? The Master said, "Too many people do not see it.
A monk asked Zen Master Zhungu of Zhongliang Mountain in Xingyuan Prefecture, "In the empty kalpa, there was no one who could ask about the Dharma;
now that there is someone asking about the Dharma, how can you rest in peace? The Master said, "The Bodhisattva of Great Compassion sits inside a jar. He was further asked, "What is the Patriarch?"
[The monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Master’s coming from the West? The Master said: "A Daoist carries a leaking cup.
Dongshan Jia’s Dharma heir, Chan Master Tong of Beiyuan in Yizhou, first visited Jiashan and asked: "There is no dharma before one's eyes; where does the intent lie?"
"It is not a thing of the present moment; it is not within the reach of the ears or eyes. Is this not the Master’s own teaching? Dongshan replied, "It is.
The Master then overturned the meditation seat and stood with his hands folded. Dongshan rose and struck him once with his staff;
the Master then descended. Next, he visited Dongshan. Dongshan ascended the hall and said: "Cut off the host and do not fall into a secondary view."
The Master stepped forward from the assembly and said, "One must know that there is one person who does not join the company. Baizhang said, "That is still the second view.
The Master then overturned the meditation seat. Baizhang asked, "What about you, elder brother? The Master replied, "Wait until my tongue rots away."
He then spoke to the Abbot. Later, when he was taking his leave of Dongshan and intended to enter the mountain passes, Dongshan said, "Be careful;

Feiyuan Ridge is steep and you must look out. The Master remained silent for a long time. Dongshan called out, "Disciple Dao! The Master responded, "Yes? Dongshan said, "Why do you not go into the pass?"

The Master attained realization thereupon and never again entered the mountain pass. Later, while presiding over an assembly, he ascended the hall and said: "Venerable elders, what matters are there? Come forth and discuss them!

If you possess the capacity of the highest root, it need not be like this. But as for those of middling or inferior capacity, you must strip away the thresholds and foundations of the gate until they are bare and empty;
do not let them enter the mud and water. First and foremost, you must act with haste."
Simplify matters. You must simply proceed without mind. Even if you learn a thousand or ten thousand things, they will only result in intellectual understanding;
what connection does that have with the school of the patch-robed monks? A monk asked, "If one must study without mind, how is it? The Master said, "Do not concern yourself with it.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A sheer cliff has no moss; ink is splashed to create mottled patterns. [Question: ...asked.
"Two dragons contend for a pearl; who is the one that obtains it? The Master said, "The one who obtains it loses. [The monk] asked, "What of the one who does not obtain it?
The Master said, "Return me my pearl! [The monk] asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, "Without defilement. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when one cannot turn [the wheel]?
The Master said, "Merit has not yet arrived. [The monk] asked, "What is a person of great wealth and nobility? The Master said—
[The monk] asked, "It is like the treasure-store of a Wheel-Turning King. [The monk] asked, "What is it like for one who is utterly destitute? The Master said, "It is like the belt of a wine shop.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when water cannot be sprinkled? The Master said, "Dry and parched. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when everything is accomplished with a single blow?
The Master said, "It is not a mere coincidence. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:
On the wall above him was painted a withered pine tree; wandering bees vied with one another to gather medicinal herbs. After his passing, he was posthumously titled Chan Master Zhengzhen.
He was the seventh-generation descendant of Dajian and the dharma heir of Yungai Yuan.
A monk asked Zen Master Deng of Tiantai in Pengzhou, “Where has the ancient Buddha gone?
The Master said, “The central mansion is lofty; year after year, numinous sprouts emerge. The monk asked, “What is it like when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished?
The Master said, “No effort is applied. The monk asked, “What is it like after it has been polished? The Master said, “It does not shine. The monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Red.”
No celestial crown is seen upon the lotus seat.
When Anfa, the Dharma heir of Luopu, was at Jiazhou Dongxi, he asked Meditation Master Jieding: "The moon-tree has no branches, yet it provides long-lasting shade. I pray—"
The Master directly pointed to the wondrous, profound, and subtle. Pu said, "In the place where the myriad phenomena flourish, things do not rely on one another;

the thousand waves of the green water and the solitary peak are each distinct. Thereupon, the Master understood the intent. Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "Why was the snake charmer swallowed by the snake?
The Master said, "How many times did he knock at the door before being invited out? He entered straight in to see what was inside. A government official was present.
Question: "Since this is a pure monastery, why is the fish-drum being beaten? The Master said:
"One must beat it right out beyond the azure heavens, so as to avoid seeing those who fail to pass through the Dragon Gate."
Caoshan Ji was a Dharma heir of the Venerable Master Bushuiyan of Yizhou. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the West?

The Master said, "Every time I think of it, my heart is wounded. The monk asked, "How is it when the precious sword has not yet been polished? The Master said, "It cannot be used. [The monk] asked, "After it has been polished..."
"How is it? The Master said, "It cannot be touched.
A monk asked West Chan Worthy of Shu Province, "The Buddha was born from Māyā; I wonder, Worthy, whose son are you?
The Master said, "A red banner planted upon the water. [Another] asked, "Of the thirty-six paths, which one is the most wondrous?"

The Master said, “It does not go beyond the first move. [The student] asked, “What if one suddenly encounters the moment it is made? The Master said, “It is no more difficult than having one’s back touch the ground.
Baima Ru was his dharma heir.
Chan Master Ruguan of Mount Qingcuo in Xingyuan Prefecture was asked by a monk, “What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, “Picking wild greens with a bottomless basket. The monk asked, “What is the realm of Qingcuo? The Master said, “In the three months of winter, the trees flourish;
in the nine months of summer, snow and frost fly.”
Yantou Huo was a dharma successor of Chan Master Xuankan Yan of Mount Yungting. A monk asked, "What is it like to be one on the Way?

The Master said, "The sun has set; he has sought lodging at a solitary inn. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The three sons of the Zhang family. The monk said, "I do not understand."
The Master said, "Meng, Zhong, and Ji do not understand. [The student] asked, "What is the one phrase before the sound? The Master said, "HŪṂ.
[The student] asked, "How is it after the turning? The Master said, "What is it?"
Longya Dun was the dharma heir of Chan Master Xichuan Cun.
A monk asked, "The student understands how to pose a paradoxical question; I request the Master to bring forth a response that startles people's faculties.
The Master said, "Chao Fu did not lead an ox; Xu You did not wash his ears. [The monk] asked, "What about when a person who is fully endowed comes? The Master—
"Will you accept it? The Master then struck him.
Chan Master Puming of Puyong Mountain in Yizhou, a Dharma heir of Xuefeng Cunen, was asked by a monk: "What is Buddha-nature? The Master said: "You have none."
[The student] asked about Buddha-nature. [The Master] said, "All that stirs and contains spirit possesses Buddha-nature.

Why then do you, as a student of the Way, lack it? The Master said, "It is because you seek it outwardly. [The student] asked, "What is the pearl of the profound mystery? The Master said, "This is not it.
[The student] asked, "Then what is the pearl of the profound mystery? The Master said, "It has been lost."
When the Venerable Fu of Taiyuan was first at Guangxiao Temple in Yangzhou, he was lecturing on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*.

A practitioner of Chan, who had been stranded by the snow, went there to listen to the lecture. On the third day, as the Master was extensively discussing the subtle principle of the *dharmakāya* in relation to the Buddha-nature and the three virtues, the Chan practitioner could not help but laugh.
After the lecture concluded, the Master invited the Chan practitioner for tea and said to him, "My own aspirations have always been narrow."
"Inferior! To explain the meaning based merely on the words has just earned me your laughter. I hope you will instruct me.

The Chan practitioner said, "I truly laugh at you, Master of Commentaries, for not recognizing the Dharma-body. The Master said, "If this is liberation, where is it not so? The practitioner said, "Please, Master, explain it once more.
The Master said, "The principle of the Dharma-body is like the great void: vertically it exhausts the three periods of time; horizontally it spans the ten directions."
It encompasses the eight extremities and includes the two polarities of heaven and earth; responding to conditions and meeting with stimuli, there is nowhere it does not pervade.

[The Master] said, "It is not that you, the Master of Dharma (*dharmācārya*), are wrong in what you say, but you have only described the boundaries of the *dharmakāya*. You truly do not yet recognize the *dharmakāya* within.
The Master said, "Since this is so, you, Virtuous One of Chan, should explain it for me. [The other] said, "Master of Dharma, do you believe it? The Master said, "How could I not?"
"How could I dare not believe it? If it is as you say," [the master] said, "I shall suspend my lectures for ten days and sit upright in quiet meditation within my chamber.
I will withdraw my mind and gather my thoughts, letting go of all conditions of good and evil at once. The teacher followed these instructions exactly;

from the first watch of the night until the fifth watch, upon hearing the sound of drums and horns, he suddenly attained realization. He then went to knock on the door. The meditator asked, "Who is it?"
The Master said, "I am so-and-so. The Chan practitioner exclaimed, "You were told to transmit and uphold the Great Teaching and to preach the Dharma in place of the Buddha.

Why did you come back last night drunk and lying in the street? The Master said, "Virtuous Chan practitioner, since I began lecturing on the sutras, I have been twisting the nostrils of my biological parents.
From this day forward, I shall never dare to act like this again. The Chan practitioner said, "Go for now; we shall speak again tomorrow."
Upon meeting him, the Master consequently ceased his lectures and traveled extensively throughout all regions, his fame spreading across the land.
Once, while traveling through the region of Xi, he attended a dharma assembly at Mount Jing. One day, before the Great Buddha Hall, a monk asked him, "Have you ever been to Wutai?"
The Master said, "I have been there. The monk asked, "Did you see Mañjuśrī? The Master said, "I saw him.
The monk asked, "Where did you see him? The Master replied, "I saw him in front of the Buddha Hall at Mount Jing. Later, when that monk traveled to Minchuan, he recounted this to Xuefeng.

Xuefeng said, "Why did you not tell him to come over the mountain ridge? Upon hearing this, the Master packed his bags and set out. When he first arrived at Xuefeng, he stayed his staff at the guest house.
He gave some tangerines to the monks. Changqing asked, "Where did you bring these from? The Master said, "From beyond the ridges.
Changqing said, "It was no easy matter to travel such a long distance; how did you manage to carry them here? The Master replied, "Tangerines, tangerines. The next day he went up the mountain.
When Xuefeng heard of this, he assembled the community. Upon arriving at the Dharma Hall, the Master looked back toward Xuefeng and then went down to inspect the administrative affairs. Ming.
The next day, as the Master was ascending to pay his respects, he said, "I offended you, Master, yesterday. Feng said, "Since you know it was such a matter, let it rest.
One day, seeing the Master, Feng pointed at the sun and showed it to him. The Master shook his hand and went out. Feng said, "Do you not agree with me?
The Master replied, "When you, Master, shake your head, I wag my tail. Where is there any disagreement?"
Feng said, "One must avoid it everywhere. One day, during the evening assembly, Feng was lying in the central courtyard.
The Master said, "Within the jurisdiction of the five provinces, there is only this old monk who is slightly superior. Feng then rose and departed.
Feng once asked the Master, "I have heard it said that Linji has three phrases; is this true? The Master replied, "Yes. Feng asked, "What is the first?"
"One phrase. The Master raised his eyes and looked at him. Fēng said, "This is still the second phrase. What is the first phrase? The Master folded his hands and withdrew.

From then on, Xuěfēng held him in deep esteem; they reached a mutual understanding within the master's quarters, and their spiritual bond as teacher and disciple was so perfect that he no longer traveled elsewhere, but remained to attend to the bathhouse.
One day, Xuánshā went up to inquire after Xuěfēng’s health. Xuěfēng said:
"There is a little mouse here; it is currently in the bathhouse," said Xuefeng. Yunju Sha said, "I shall wait to examine him with you, Master.
Having finished speaking, he went to the bathhouse and encountered the Master (Xuefeng) pouring water. Sha said, "I have come to see the Senior Monk.
The Master said, "We have already met. Sha said, "In which kalpa did we ever meet? The Master said, "Why are you dozing off? Sha then entered the washroom.
Zhàng Bai Xuefeng said, “I have already investigated and resolved this. Fēng asked, “How did you investigate him? Shā recounted the previous dialogue.

He refused. Deshan asked, "How so? The Master said, "Bring me the fan in your hand. Deshan gave him the fan and again posed the previous question.
The Master shook the fan and did not answer. Deshan, unable to fathom this, struck the Master with a single punch.

When Gushan went to attend a banquet invited by the Great King, Xuefeng saw him off at the gate. Upon returning to the Dharma Hall, Gushan said, "A single holy arrow shot straight through nine [layers of armor]."
“[He] has gone into the innermost city. The Master said, “He is not yet there. Feng said, “He is a man who has reached the very bottom.

Shan said, “I am going into the nine-layered city. The Master said, “Suppose you suddenly encounter an encirclement by a threefold army—what then?”
"What? Shan said, "His house has its own path that reaches the heavens. The Master said, "If that is so, then he has left the palace and lost the hall.
Shan said, "Where would he not be called Honored One? The Master shook his sleeves and turned back. Feng asked, "How was it? The Master said, "A fine divine arrow;
it was broken mid-course. He then recounted the previous conversation. Feng then said, "The slave still has his words."
The Master said, "This old, frozen scum still has some local sentiment left. The Master stood before the storehouse; a monk asked, "What is Bodhi as it meets the eye?
The Master kicked a puppy, which ran off making a noise. The monk had no reply. The Master said, "That little puppy does not deserve more than a single kick.
While Baofu was selecting melons, the Master arrived. Baofu said, "If you can say something, I will give you a melon to eat."

The Master said, "Bring it here. Fudu gave him a piece. The Master took it and departed. As he did not appear in the world [as a formal teacher], those of all quarters referred to him as "Venerable Fu of Taiyuan.
Later, he returned to Weiyang, where Minister Chen invited him to stay at his residence and provided for him.
One day he said to the Minister, “Tomorrow I shall lecture on the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* once.

When the Minister had completed his offerings of tea and incense for the purification ceremony, the Master ascended the seat. After a long silence, he struck the sounding board once and said, “Thus have I heard.
He then called to the Minister; the Minister responded, “Yes. The Master said, “At one time, it was swept away,” and immediately passed away.
National Teacher Shenyi Xingsheng of Gushan in Fuzhou was the son of the Li clan of the Great Liang dynasty.

From his youth, he loathed the smell of meat and pungent spices and delighted in hearing the sounds of bells and sutras. At the age of twelve, he visited Xueling, where their karmic affinity was instantly realized. One day he went to consult Xuefeng;
knowing that his conditions were ripe, Xuefeng suddenly rose and seized him, asking, "What is this? The Master attained sudden and complete enlightenment, yet even forgot that he had attained it.
[The Master] simply raised his hand and waved it back and forth. Xuefeng asked, "Are you applying intellectual reasoning? The Master replied, "What reasoning would there be?

Xuefeng scrutinized his profound understanding and patted him in confirmation. Later, when the Military Governor of Min frequently inquired about the essentials of the Dharma and established the Drum Mountain (Gushan) Chan monastery, he invited [the Master] to propagate the fundamental tenets.
Ascending the hall, after a long silence, he said, "In Nanquan’s day, there was also someone..."
[The Master] raised [the case]: "In short, you do not recognize Nanquan. Is there anyone here now who recognizes Nanquan?
Come forward and let us test you before the assembly. At that time, a monk stepped forward; as soon as he had prostrated and risen, the Master said, "How is it? The monk stepped closer and said:

He addressed the Master, saying, "Venerable One. The Master replied, "I am without talent; please withdraw. He then said, "The Sūtras have Sūtra masters, the Śāstras have Śāstra masters, and the Vinaya has Vinaya masters;
each has its own keepers. Furthermore, the Buddha-dharma is the establishment of the teachings, whereas the Way of Chan is but a device to stop a child's crying.
That other sages appeared in the world was because the minds of people were not uniform; they skillfully opened up expedient means, resulting in many [diverse paths]."

The gateways [of teaching] differ according to the illnesses received, and the prescriptions vary accordingly. Those who dwell in existence refute existence; those who abide in emptiness revile emptiness.

Once these two afflictions are removed, the Middle Way itself must be discarded. Thus Mount Gu said: "Phrases do not meet the occasion; words do not unfold the reality. He who receives the words perishes; he who clings to the phrases is deluded.
If one does not sing before the words, how could one discuss what follows the phrases? This leads directly to Śākyamuni closing his room."
Vimalakīrti kept his mouth shut; the Great Being was a youth during the Liang dynasty. On that day, he asked once, twice, and thrice, yet everyone has already understood.
"How should you all act? At that time, a monk came forward and bowed. The Master said, "Ask with a loud voice.
The monk said, "I, this student, inquire of the Master. The Master shouted, "Get out! The monk said, "Since my own matter is not yet clear, what shall I do?"
Yan examined him. The Master raised his voice and said, "Have you not heard? The monk asked again. The Master said, "A single drop follows the current;
though one eats salt, it is not heavy. [The monk] asked, "What is the phrase that encompasses all of heaven and earth? The Master said, "Come closer.
When the monk approached, the Master said, "This will surely leave people frustrated."
The Eighth Generation under Dajian [Huineng]:
Qingfeng Chu’s Successor, Chan Master Lingkan of Xichuan.
A monk asked: “What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? The Master said: “The place of emergence.”

"It is not the Buddha’s doing; when spring comes, the grass turns green of its own accord. A monk asked, "What is it like when one is in a state of mere mundanity? The Master said, "Try taking one step forward and see.
A monk asked Chan Master Guixin of Jingzhong Monastery in Yizhou, "What is it like before the lotus flower has emerged from the water? The Master—
[The student] said, "The lotuses fill the flowing pond. [The Master] asked, "After they emerge from the water, what then? The Master said, "The leaves fall, yet one knows not autumn.
[The student] asked, "If one does not rely on a life-raft, how is it when ascending the vast ocean? The Master said, "The red-beaked bird flies beyond the three realms."
Lümao also understood how to brew tea. [A monk] asked, "What is a person who is autonomous?
The Master said, "When the sword-trees and frosty forests appear, he goes immediately. [The monk] asked, "What is a person who is not autonomous? The Master said, "Śākyamuni is behind you, O layman."
A monk asked the Second Generation Master of Xuánquán in Huáizhōu, the Dharma heir of Xuánquán Yàn, "What is it like when words are exhausted and principles are fully realized?

The Master said, "If one does not enter into principle, how can it be said that [words] are exhausted? The monk asked, "The wondrous, profound pearl exists—how can it be obtained? The Master said, "It is not like a *maṇi* jewel."
"Exquisite and shadowless brilliance—how could a blue-eyed barbarian ever perceive it? [The student] asked: "When there is a mouth but one cannot speak, what then? The Master said:
"Three inches cannot keep pace with the rhythm of the drum; the mute man understands how to sing the song of the wooden man."
Xichuan Dinghui Chanshi was a successor of Luoshan Xian.
When he first visited Luoshan, the Master asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have traveled far from Xichuan and have recently departed from Kaiyuan.
He then stepped forward and asked, "As for the matter at hand right now, what is it? Luoshan made a gesture of invitation and said, "Eat."
"Tea is served. The Master hesitated. Deshan said, "The autumn air is somewhat warm; go.

The Master went out to the Dharma Hall and sighed, saying, "While I was at Mount Emei in Western Sichuan, I picked up a single arrow made of tares and thistles, intending to use it to settle the chaos of the world."

Today I am dismantling the mountain fortress; the bow is broken and the arrows exhausted—enough, enough! He then descended from his seat to join the assembly. On the following day, he ascended the hall.
The Master came forward and asked, "The doors and windows are flung wide open; who stands before the hall? Mountan (Shanshan) gave a shout. The Master remained speechless.

Mountan said, "Your feathers and wings are not yet complete; go for now. Thereupon, the Master tucked up his robes and departed. Having long since received his seal of approval, he later went to visit Taizhou.
Prabhūtaratna (Shengguang) was seated. As the Master entered directly by his side and stood with hands joined in *añjali*, Prabhūtaratna asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master said, "I am still waiting for an answer to my words," and he immediately departed. Prabhūtaratna took up his whisk and pursued him to the front of the Sangha Hall, where he saw the Master.
He then raised the whisk and asked, "What do you call this, *ācārya*? The Master replied, "Dare one who is about to die continue to breathe? Prabhūtaratna [laughed].
He bowed his head and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
A monk asked Master Lingyan of Guanzhou, "What is the treasure within the Way? The Master replied, "The earth slopes toward the southeast."
"The heavens are high to the northwest. [The student] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The setting sun before one's face is unique.

Regarding his verse on Shigong receiving Sanping, he said: "He understood how to split the arrow aimed at his chest; why then did he remain only half a person? Because he was enlightened while still on the path, he therefore failed to preserve his whole body."
Chan Master Ciquo of Chengtian Monastery in Pengzhou was a dharma successor of Bājī Qīng. A monk asked him, "I, this student, have an arrow.
Shall I shoot it, or shall I not? The Master said, "What is your arrow, lay brother? The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "This..."
"This is the grass arrow. [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s arrow? The Master said, "When restraining forgetfulness, one must count on the fingers;
when offering prayers, one immediately knocks the teeth. He asked, "The mind turns following the myriad objects; which one is that mind that turns the myriad objects? The Master said:
Regarding the "Great Image of Jiazhou" (Jiazhou Daxiang), an ancient master once asked the assembly: "Sins are like frost and dew; how can the sun of wisdom eliminate them? The Master said:
"Rain on the pavilions in the deep night; the bell in stillness at the towers. He asked again: "Why is it that when causes and conditions meet, the retribution is received by oneself?
The Master said: "The pen and brush can write; the tongue can speak. On the day he opened the hall: [He recited: "The pen and brush can write; the tongue can speak."

Addressing the assembly: To uphold the true command and grasp the essential principles is still to fabricate a nest and create a counterfeit. To provide a formal response regarding the Buddha-dharma is, in itself, a deliberate mockery of those of superior caliber.
When questioned, they are inconsistent; when answered, they are contradictory. Where, O Virtuous Ones, do you intend to set your teeth?
Nevertheless, it is thus: matters are not one-sided. The authority rests in my hands; I grant or withhold according to the immediate occasion. If you have doubts, please ask.
Question: A monk asked, "What is the primary meaning? The Master said, "The myriad peaks pierce through to the sea; a drop of water descends from the cliff.
Question: "Whose song do you sing, Master? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? The Master said, "He who understands the beginning knows the end; he who raises his intention knows the mind."
A monk asked Zen Master Jing of Mount Niutou in Xingyuan Prefecture, “What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas?

The Master said, “Bubbles on the Eastern Sea. The monk asked, “How should one comprehend this? The Master said, “The scale-weight falls into the well. Another asked, “Who is it that dwells neither among the ordinary nor the sagely?
The Master said, “Fu Dashi of the Liang Dynasty. The monk asked, “What is the principle of this? The Master said, “Meng [Zi] of the State of Chu.”
While serving as attendant to the Master, a monk from Juecheng Monastery in Yizhou asked Zen Master Xin, "What is the single path for emerging [into the world]?
The Master said, "In front of the triple gate. The monk asked, "How should one understand this? The Master said, "Tie your straw sandals tight."
Chan Master Chengyuan of Xianglin Monastery in Qingcheng, Yizhou, was a Dharma successor of Yunmen Wenyan. He was a native of Mianzhu, Hanzhou.
During the early days of his tenure among the assembly, while he was engaged in communal labor weeding, a monk said, "Look, there is a fire at a layperson's house. The Master replied, "Where?"
Huo said, "I do not see it. The Master said, "I do not see it. Huo said, "You blind fellow! At that time, the entire assembly remarked that Elder Yuan had failed.
Later, when Mingjiao Kuan heard this account, he sighed and said, "It must have been my elder brother Yuan who achieved this.
After [the Master] took up residence there, a monk asked, "Why does the delicious flavor of *amṛta* turn into poison? The Master said, "The paper in Daojiang has become expensive."
A questioner asked, "When one sees form, how is it that one sees the mind? The Master said, "Where did you just come from?

The questioner asked, "What is it like when both mind and objects are forgotten? The Master said, "Sitting and dozing with eyes open. A questioner asked, "What is the meaning of 'hiding one's body within the Big Dipper'?
The Master said, "The moon is like a drawn bow; there is little rain and much wind. A questioner asked, "What is the mind of all Buddhas? The Master said—
[The monk] said, "If it is pure, it is pure from beginning to end. [The Master] asked, "How do you understand this? The Master said, "Do not let others deceive you.
[The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Who is it that steps forward? [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s wondrous medicine?

The Master said, "It is not apart from the various flavors. [The monk] asked, "And what of those who consume it? The Master said, "Look at how they swallow and devour. [The monk] asked, "What about... (The text ends here).
"This is a single bowl of lamp-light within the room. The Master said: "Three people have taken a tortoise and turned it into a turtle. He asked: "What is the matter beneath the patched robe?
The Master said: "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains. He asked: "The great assembly has gathered; we request the Master to provide instruction. The Master said:
"Three do not depend on two. A questioner asked, "What is the matter for a student during their time [of practice]? The Master said, "Precisely. He asked, "What is the profound (xuan)?
The Master said, "Coming today and going tomorrow. He asked, "What is the profound within the profound? The Master said, "On the long continuous bed.
He asked, "What is the single stream of spring at Xianglin? The Master said, "Thoughts are uninterrupted. He asked, "To drink [from it]..."
"How is this so? The Master said, "It is like the bushel and the scale according to the region. The monk asked, "What is the true eye of a patch-robed monk?
The Master said, "Non-discrimination. The monk asked, "How are illumination and function? The Master said, "A traveler loses his footing.

The monk asked, "When all myriad activities have vanished and one recognizes the person of original nature, what then? The Master said, "The clear faculty manifests of itself. The monk said, "If that is so, then it is not..."

By the time he was one year old, his memory and questioning were as they had been before. When he reached the age of three, Chan Master Băizhūn Duān arrived at their home; this was when he first met him.

Yun asked, "Where did we part? He replied, "At Bailian Village. Yun asked, "What is the proof?
He said, "Tomorrow my father and mother will invite the Master for a meal. Suddenly I heard the sound of a cart being pushed. Yun asked, "Is that outside the gate?"
"What sound? Yun made a gesture with his hand as if pushing a cart. Yun asked, "What about after it has passed? [Baizhang] said, "Two channels across level ground.
Indeed, six weeks later, he passed away without illness.

"Acting. When people come here, do they still understand thoroughly? After a long silence, he said:
"Constantly walking without lifting his feet from the human path, he wears fur and horns, mixing with the dust and mud. A monk asked, "What was it like before Ox Head saw the Fourth Patriarch?

One day, while being taught the text, upon reaching the passage, "By nature humans are nearly alike; by practice they become far apart," he suddenly said, "Ordinary people and sages are fundamentally one."
"Regarding the essence, it is differentiated by habituation; I understand this. Thereupon, the Master went straight to the Qingtai Hermitage at the Deer Park.

At the age of nineteen, he shaved his head, received the precepts, and ascended to full ordination. When Master Tai ordered him to listen to the *Awakening of Faith*, the Master simply returned to lie down.

Master Tai questioned him about this, and the Master replied: "Since you call this the 'correct faith' of the Mahāyāna, how could it be fully understood through mere words? He then withdrew to roam with an open mind.

Fang then went to visit Fuyong at Dahuangong. Once, while sitting in the night on the gallery, a violent wind and snow were blowing. Hearing the watchmen calling out as they passed by to alert against thieves, Fang followed them for a short distance before turning back. During the Daguan era, when Fuyong was embroiled in trouble, the Master intended to head toward Yishui from the Three Wu regions. He then composed a verse: "The dog has no Buddha-nature; The Buddha has no dog. In the midst of the three realms, There is nothing to be sought. The Great Matter is right here; Why seek it elsewhere? When the Jin dynasty fell and the Song rose, he moved to the Xiangguo Cloister in Yangzhou. During the early Shaoxing era, he resided at the Chongfu Cloister in Suzhou. Among them, the most prominent were the Chan masters Zhenxie Qingliao, Zhenjing Kezhen, and Wuzu Fayan. His teachings were compiled into the *Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wuxin*. This concludes the biography of Chan Master Wuxin.

Chan Master Fadingeng of Lumén in Xiangzhou was the son of the Liu family of Chengdu. He took ordination as a monk under Daci Baofan.
He was sent to listen to the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* so that he might grasp its essentials; he then went to visit Furuong. Furuong asked, "What is the self prior to the empty kalpa?
At these words, the traces of the Master's mind vanished. He replied with composure, "A single phrase, spiritually resonant, transcends all phenomena;
it stands far beyond the Three Vehicles and requires no cultivation. Furuong patted him and certified his realization. He subsequently propagated the Dharma at Lumen. A monk asked:
"How is it when the profound void is unassailable and the light of the precious mirror is cold? The Master said, "Dig a deep hole and bury it.

Chan Master Shousui of Dahuang, a successor of the Great Hong’en lineage and a native of the Zhang clan of Suining, addressed the assembly from the high seat, calling out to them:

He replied, "I dare not. Yantou raised his fist and said, "What teaching is this? He replied, "It is the provisional teaching (expedient teaching).
Yantou said, "How tragic! If I were to ask you with my legs extended, you could not say it is the 'leg-teaching'!"
The Master said: "How extraordinary! These two venerable elders possess the 'knife that kills' and the 'sword that gives life.

One turn of phrase is like planting flowers upon a stone; another turn of phrase is like hanging a sword in mid-air. Had there not been their subsequent words at that time, the entire school of Bodhidharma would have been wiped out.
Do you wish to see these two venerable elders? It would be better to cut out one's own tongue than to offend the state."
His taboo name was Yue Dao.

A lay practitioner (*upāsaka*), he was the dharma heir of Master Quan of Mount Jiangshan and the Qingxian Gong, Zhao Bian. When he was over forty years of age, he cast aside sounds and colors and fixed his mind [upon the Way].
Regarding religion: when Huìfó came to reside at Nanchan in Quzhou, the Duke visited him daily. Huìfó never once permitted him to utter a single word.

Later, while serving as the administrator of Qingzhou, he often sat in meditation during his leisure from official affairs. Suddenly, a great thunderclap struck with such force that he attained immediate enlightenment.
He composed a verse, saying: "Sitting silently in the public hall, leaning back on a vacant rest; The source of the mind is unmoving, as still as water. A single sound—"
"The thunderclap opens the crown of the head; it awakens that which belongs to one's own self from of old. When Huiwen heard this, he said with a smile, "Zhao Yuedao has merely struck lucky.
When Duke Zhengfu was initially not yet inclined toward the School of the Lineage (Zongmen), the Duke exhorted him with a letter, saying:

"I humbly observe that your official duties have reached such an extreme of nobility and wealth; your virtue and character are so flourishing; and your blessings, longevity, health, and tranquility are likewise [in such abundance]."
His preparations for retirement were as grand as this. Yet, that which he had not yet paid much attention to was nothing other than the Tathāgata’s Great Cause and Condition.
If you can seek with single-minded sincerity that which is to be realized and awakened, I shall congratulate you on your achievement in the future.
You, sir, at the age of seventy-two, have retired from office as Grand Master of the Household (Taizi Shaobao) and returned home. Your relatives, old friends, and the local villagers—
He treated him as he had before. He built a lofty study for his own comfort and composed a verse to express his intent, saying:

"Golden girdle fastened at the waist, now retired and hidden; The message within this state is simply ordinary. If people of the world wish to know the old man of Gaozhai, He is none other than Zhao Sili of Ke Village.
He further said, "Be careful not to mistake him. When he was about to pass away, he wrote a letter to Fohui, saying: "This is not [the work] of my usual self..."
At this point, admonitions will surely fail to exert their influence. Hui-dao expressed his sentiments in verse: In office, he was an omen of blessing for the state;
Returning home, he serves as a model for the world. The Golden Grain has departed from the human realm; The Jade Tower is now completed in heaven. His sword of wisdom is without the slightest flaw;
His crystal pitcher is pure to its very depths. On the waters of the Hui River in the spring breeze, A solitary moon shines brightly through the clouds.
Fayun Xiu’s successor, Chan Master Cijie Cong of Xingyuan Prefecture, was asked by a monk: “What is the Way? The Master said: “Thirty stages from here to Chang’an.
The monk asked: “What is one who is on the Way? The Master said: “Bumping heads and knocking foreheads. [Another monk] asked: “It is not the wind...”
[The wind] moves. It is not the banner that moves; I wonder, what is it that moves? The Master said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice.
[A monk asked: "What is the mani-jewel that reflects all colors? The Master said, "The lush green bamboo; the dense yellow flowers.

[The Master] acted as their leader. The Master said, "Even an iron ox must break into a sweat. [The monk] asked, "Is it not that this is the very point of acting for others?
The Master said, "Look closely at the previous statement. He asked, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? The Master said, "The iron ox of Shanfu. Entering the hall, he said:
"The scriptures of the Three Vehicles are not the true exposition; pointing directly to one's own mind is not yet the ultimate principle."
If there were a man of universal capacity and high standing, a liberated and eminent figure, to come forth and meet him, he would look at the assembly and say, "Enough.
He ascended the hall and said: "All day long we have been diligently striving for one another’s sake, yet it is just like trying to lead an ox up a wall.

Why is it that the assembly is like this? 'Greedy for life, you toil busily chasing after each day; when called back, you do not turn—what can be done? He ascended the hall and said: "One is precisely one."
"Two is indeed two. He firmly grasps the essential ford. "Where does one breathe out? Holding up his staff, he said, "He has no wound himself;
do not injure him. With a thump, he struck it once and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Changzong Zhaojue of Donglin Xinglong Temple in Jiangzhou was a dharma successor of Huanglong Nan. He was the son of the Shi family of Jianzhou.

Having long relied upon Huanglong, he received the secret transmission of the Great Dharma’s essential meaning. He subsequently resided at Letan and later moved to Donglin, both of which fulfilled prophetic records.
A monk asked, "Within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the universe, there is a treasure hidden within the mountain of form. What is this treasure?
The Master said, "The white moon appears; the black moon hides. The monk said, "I have not merely heard its name; today I have seen it face to face.
The Master said, "But tell me, where does the treasure reside? The monk said, "The doors of the ancient hall stand open, radiating brilliant light, by the side of the white lotus pond."
A man from the monastery stepped forward. The Master said, "One who discerns jewels returns them to the blue-eyed barbarian.

Then another monk came forth from the assembly, held up his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*), and said, "I ask the Master to answer this question. The Master said, "Put it down. The monk made a gesture as if to spread it out.
The Master said, "Withdraw it. The monk said, "In years past I was a seeker of the sword; today I have met a master craftsman. The Master said, "What kind of place is this? The monk then...
"Ha! The Master said, "What about me, the old monk? The monk shouted again. The Master said, "Even if you let it go, how could you have won?
He then struck him. Ascending the hall, he said: "The heavens and earth constantly proclaim the perfect sound; the sun, moon, and stars always discourse upon the true mark (*dharmatā*).
I am reminded of the former Huanglong, who said: 'The autumn rain pours down, continuing from night until dawn; every drop is impartial, falling nowhere else. He then added: "Furthermore..."
[The Master] said: "Drops will pierce your eyes; they will soak and rot your nostrils. Donglin, however, was not like this: "In the end, they return to the great ocean to become waves and billows.

[He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it. [On another occasion, he gave] a formal lecture: "Old Lu did not know how to read, yet he suddenly realized the Buddha’s intent. This is because the Buddha’s intent is beyond words and ink.
Baizhao did not know how to write, yet he fully awakened to the lineage of the school. This is because the lineage of the school is not something conveyed by speech."

With such a grandmotherly heart, I have clearly entered the mud and water. People of the present day still cling to the bridge pillar to wash themselves, or hold the mooring rope while releasing the boat.
After a long while, he said: "How can you blame this old monk?"

Chan Master Weisheng Zhenjue of Huangbo in Ruizhou was the son of the Luo family of Tongchuan. While he was living among a community of lecturers, he happened to strike a window lattice with his fan, causing it to ring.
Suddenly, he recalled a passage from the teachings which states: "When the drums are struck throughout the ten directions, they are heard simultaneously in ten places.

Because of this, he attained great enlightenment. He informed his lecturer, who instructed him to seek out a teacher through formal inquiry. The Master went directly to Huanglong; later, because of Ruizhou...

The Prefectural Governor appointed Longlin to select the master for Huangbo. Long gathered the assembly and delivered this instruction: "Reciting hymns atop the bell tower; planting vegetables beneath the bedframe. If anyone can explain this, they shall go to serve as abbot.

The Master stepped forward and replied, "A fierce tiger sits blocking the road. Long was greatly pleased and immediately sent him there. Consequently, he was revered by the various schools. He ascended the hall and said: [He ascended the hall and said: "The great Way is not difficult to understand; it only avoids picking and choosing. When you see forms, do not grasp at them; when you hear sounds, do not cling to them. If you can act thus, you will naturally accord with the Way.

But if you still harbor doubts and hesitate, you will never attain liberation. Therefore, I say to you all: 'If you wish to enter the Buddha’s Way, first you must cut off the root of doubt. He struck the meditation seat once and descended.
Linji’s shout and Deshan’s staff are left for practitioners as models.
Guizong’s grinding and Xuefeng’s ball—this kind of teaching style is for receiving those of superior capacity. If it were Huangbo, however, it would not be so;
there would be no shout and no staff, nor would he grind, nor would he roll a ball. Before you is the front mountain, behind you is the main mountain—they block you up.
The eyes: they crush open your face-gate. If you can see into this, you will attain the stage of non-retrogression and, until the end of the future, seek nothing from others.
If you cannot see into it, the supreme flavor of *amṛta* (clarified butter) turns instead into a poisonous drug. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Silent and desolate—the moon shines brightly down into the empty valley. Vast and expansive—the brilliant light of the sun streams across the four seas."
On the road to Caoqi, the passage of people is cut off; before the Many-Son Stupa, the crowds are as dense as at a marketplace.
Even if you can realize it here with such clarity and decisiveness, that is not yet the livelihood of a patch-robed monk.

A true man of great capacity must strike the shackles and break the chains within the dark prison; he must set fire to the ranks of hungry ghosts to seize their gruel, and topple the Tower of Maitreya.
"Demolish the Palace of the Empty King! Uproot the auspicious sprouts and lucky grasses by their very roots! Let thorns grow everywhere as they please.
This was the Dharma Hall discourse of Chan Master Cigan of Nanyue Fuyan, a descendant of the Du clan of Tongchuan. He said: "The mind of the ancient Buddhas is right here now.
If you do not understand it, you will suffer in deep hesitation. The autumn rain falls lightly; the autumn wind blows briskly. From here to there, from that to this—"
In response: On the sandy shore, the reeds and flowers are intermingled in shades of green and yellow; on what does the Chan practitioner rely? After a long silence, he said: "Zha!
Chan Master Shouzhi of Yungai in Tanzhou was a native of the Chen family of Jianzhou. While traveling, he arrived at Dajian in Yuzhang.
At that time, Chan Master Farchang was sequestered in the Western Mountains. Hearing that the Master had completed his extensive training, Farchang went to visit him.
Farchang asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Daining. He asked again, "The main gate collapsed last night;
were you aware of it? The Master was startled and said, "I was not aware. Farchang said, "In Wuzhong, there is a stone Buddha that many people have never seen. The Master was left bewildered.

He immediately performed prostrations. Chang sent him to pay his respects to Chan Master Zhen of Cuiyan; although he practiced there for a long time, he had no realization, yet he did not waste even a moment of time.
Upon visiting Huanglong at Jicui, he finally resolved all his doubts. Later, he led the assembly at Shishuang and subsequently established the Dharma lineage at Dagui.
He later moved to Yungai. A monk asked: "There is a stringless zither that is not made of worldly wood; today it is carried upon one's back."
"Come! Please ask the Master to play a melody. The Master tapped his knee once. The monk said, "The golden wind rustles in harmony with the pure tones;
we pray the Master will use his skillful means to grant us further sound. The Master said, "An iron ox emerges from Shanfu. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:
"Tightly laced water-repelling boots tread upon the moon of Lake Xiang. Grasping an iron caltrop in hand, he breaks through the dragon and tiger’s lair, turning his body upside down and ascending."
The Tree: For the first time seeing that there is neither birth nor extinction, he laughs at the old Gautama, who snaps his fingers and surpasses Maitreya.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Yesterday, I watched for fish from a high mountain; walking while riding a horse, I lost my donkey. Someone picked up the camel and went off; though a thousand pieces of gold were offered as a reward, not even one was found. If you can realize this point here, I will not charge you for the straw sandals. Ascending the hall, [he said again]: "Yesterday, I watched for fish from a high mountain; walking while riding a horse, I lost my donkey. Someone picked up the camel and went off;

though a thousand pieces of gold were offered as a reward, not even one was found. If you can realize this point here, I will not charge you for the straw sandals. If you cannot realize it here, I shall still demand the money for the straw sandals. Ascending the hall.
[The Master] cited the case of Zhaozhou asking a monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to pick tea. Zhaozhou said, "Idle. The Master [Xuedou] said:
"To speak or not to speak—where can one search for it? Scales on the dragon’s back behind; donkey’s feet before the face. A somersaulting flip;
a solitary cloud and wild crane. A-he-he! He addressed the assembly: "Without leaving this very place, it is ever serene. If you seek it, I know you will not find it."
It can be seen. Although the ancient sages spoke thus, they merely fashioned a mold to cast [the truth]. If you cannot emerge from it, you will only be clutching the ancients' leftovers;
if you can emerge from it, only then will there be some slight correspondence. Yun’gai, however, was not like this:
"Riding a fine horse around Mount Sumeru, passing over mountains to seek the tracks of ants—how many people could possibly know? The Master resided [there].
In the East Hall of the monastery was the abbot of Lingyin in Sushong County, Shuzhou, named Dezhi, a native of Shu. He had served as the head of the monastery for twenty years.
Every day he would ascend the hall alone; morning after morning it was the same, day after day it was the same hall. "This very thing is it—do not seek it elsewhere."

On the fourth day of the tenth month in the sixth year of the Yuanfeng era, he ascended the hall to assemble the congregation. After a long silence, he asked, "Do you understand? The assembly remained silent.
He then passed away in solemn stillness.
Jingfu was a native of Xishu. He received the Dharma from Hui Nan, yet his karmic conditions were meager; all the monasteries where he resided were small establishments in remote regions.
When students passed through his gate, there was no room for them. Jingfu, however, remained transcendent and self-contented, regarding the mundane world as flying dust passing before one’s eyes.
At over eighty years of age, he passed away while seated at Mount Xiangcheng.
The Chan Master Zhijing of Fule in Mianzhou was a dharma successor of the Arhat Zu Lin. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Six ears do not share a secret. The monk asked, "What is the intent of this? The Master said, "When you meet someone, simply speak of it thus."
The Fourteenth Generation after Dajian (Baizhang),
Chan Master Wuzu Fayan of Qizhou,
a successor of Baiyun Tian, was the son of the Deng family from Mianzhou. At thirty-five, he first renounced his home and received the precepts.
Having shaved his hair and received full ordination, he went to Chengdu to study the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra* (The Treatise on the Hundred Dharmas).

There, he heard that when a Bodhisattva enters the Path of Vision (*darśana-mārga*), wisdom merges with principle and the object merges with the spirit; thus, the means of realization and the object realized are not distinguished.

Once, a non-Buddhist from the Western Regions challenged a Bhikṣu, saying: "If you do not distinguish between the means of realization and the object realized, then by what means is there realization? No one was able to answer him. The non-Buddhist—
The Master of the Way disparaged him, ordering that he not strike the bells and drums and instead wear his *kāṣāya* robe backward.
When the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang arrived there, he resolved this point, saying, "It is like a person drinking water; whether it is cold or warm, they know it for themselves.

The Master said, "Cold and warmth may indeed be known, but what is this matter of 'knowing for oneself'? He then questioned the original lecturer, who replied, "I do not know what it means to 'know for oneself.'"

"What is the principle behind this? He lectured on it without neglecting the question, but merely guided him, saying: "If you wish to clarify this, you should go to the South and seek out those who have transmitted the Buddha-mind school.
The Master immediately took his book-bundle and left the pass. Whichever venerable masters he encountered, he consulted them all regarding this matter;
yet his doubts remained unresolved. Eventually, upon visiting Chan Master Yuanzhao Ben, the causes and conditions of past and present were fully resolved.
Only [Yunmen] did not join the assembly when he was asked by Xinghua, "How is it when they come from the four quarters and eight directions?
Xinghua said, "Strike the one in the middle. The monk bowed; Xinghua said, "Yesterday I attended a village feast.
On the way, I encountered a sudden storm of wind and rain, but I managed to take shelter inside an old temple. He requested further instruction from Wuben. Wuben said, "This is the lineage of Linji."
"The causal conditions must be sought by questioning the descendants of that house.
The Master then visited Chan Master Fushan Yuan and requested instruction on the previous dialogue. Yuan said, "I have a parable to tell you:
you are like a firewood seller from a village of three households who, carrying his yoke, stands at a crossroads and asks people about the Secretariat."
"What matter is the Master discussing today? The Master thought to himself, "If it is so, there is still much that remains to be done.
One day, Yuan said to the Master, "I am old; I fear you will let your time pass in vain. You should go and rely upon Baiyun.
Although this old man is younger than I, I have not yet met him in person, but I have seen his verse on the story of Linji’s three blows of the staff, and it possesses a quality beyond my own."
"Once you have reached the human realm, you will surely be able to resolve the great matter. The Master bowed in tears and took his leave.

Upon arriving at Baiyun, he brought up the dialogue concerning the *maṇi* jewel asked of Nanquan for inquiry. Baiyun rebuked him. The Master attained realization and offered this verse of karmic resonance:
"A plot of vacant land before the mountain; With palms joined, I earnestly questioned the patriarch: How many times have I sold it only to buy it back again?"

"Out of pity for the pines and bamboos, he draws in the pure wind. Yun granted him formal approval (*inka*) and appointed him to oversee the grinding of ink-sticks. Not long after, Yun came to the Master and said:
"There are several Zen guests who have come from Mount Lu; all of them possess a point of awakening. If you ask them to speak, they can explain it with its proper origins.
If you present them with a *nidāna* (causal occasion) to test them, they understand it clearly. If you instruct them to offer a response, they are able to do so as well. However—"
"Not yet. At this, the Master was greatly perplexed and thought to himself: "If he has already attained awakening, then he can certainly speak it and clarify it; how is it that he says 'not yet'?
He then spent several days investigating this matter until he suddenly attained realization.
All that he had previously cherished was cast aside at once, and he went to see Baiyun. Baiyun danced for joy with hands and feet, and the Master also smiled.
Later, the Master said: "Because of this, I broke into a cold sweat and thereby clearly realized the pure breeze of ten thousand loads.
One day, Yun said to the assembly: "An ancient said: 'It is like casting an image in a mirror. Once the image is formed, where is the mirror?'"
The assembly’s responses were not in accord with his intent, so he brought the matter to the Master for questioning. The Master stepped forward and greeted him, saying, "It is not much.
Yun smiled and said, "One must be a true practitioner to achieve this. He then ordered Yun to share his seat and instruct those who would come after. Yun first resided at Sishian.
Qian Baiyun later resided at Mount Dongshan. A monk asked, "Carrying your staff and leading the assembly, you carry out the Patriarchal Command;
sitting and cutting off the vital ford, what is your meaning, Master? The Master said, "The autumn wind blows over the Wei River; fallen leaves fill Chang'an.
The monk said, "With no gates on all four sides, the mountains and peaks are magnificent; today the master has finally returned home. The Master said, "Where do you think the roadhead is?"
[The monk] asked, "Where [is it]? The Master said, "Why do we not recognize each other face-to-face? The Master said, "Fortunately, you have arrived.

[The monk] asked, "Are the intent of the Patriarchs and the intent of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "When a person is poor, their wisdom is short; when a horse is lean, its hair is long.
[The monk] asked, "What is the point where Baiyun’s help for people is most intimate? The Master said, "Twist their nostrils around. [The monk] said, "If one goes in this very way..."

"What? the Master said. "A fellow who does not know pain or itch. [The monk asked: "What was the meaning of Bodhidharma’s facing the wall? The Master said: "The calculation has not yet been completed.

[The monk asked: "What about when the Second Patriarch stood in the snow? The Master said: "Taking a mistake and following it through. [The monk asked: "As for cutting off one's arm to find peace of mind, what then?

The Master said: "Emperor Yang opens the Bian Canal. [The monk asked: "What about 'the hundred-foot pole'?"* *Note: This refers to the famous Zen kōan concerning the limit of spiritual progress. The Master’s response implies that even at such a height, there is still work to be done.*
"How does one make progress? The Master said, "Only by walking fast will you succeed. "Question: What is the matter under the Linji lineage?

The Master said, "The five heinous crimes [are heard] upon the thunderclap. "Question: What is the matter under the Yunmen lineage? The Master said, "The red banner flashes. "Question: What is the matter under the Caodong lineage?
The Master said, "The letter is sent, but it does not reach home. "Question: What is the matter under the Guiyang lineage?"
[The monk] presented the matter. The Master said, "A broken stele lies across the ancient road. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Why do you not ask about the matter of the Fayan lineage?
[The monk] replied, "I leave it to you, Master. The Master said, "The patrolman has committed a night-time offense. [The monk] asked, "What is the single drop of water from White Clouds?"
The Master said, "Pounding the mortar, grinding the mill. [A monk] asked, "What about those who drink? The Master said, "I will give you no place to put your face.
[Another] asked, "The tongues of all people in the world have been completely cut off by Baiyun; who can cut off the tongue of Baiyun?"
The Master said, "The great elder of East Village. The Master then said, "Just now I thought of a kōan (a causal condition), but I have already forgotten it this morning.
It is actually my staff that remembers. He then picked up the staff and said, "Even the staff has forgotten.
He then struck the ground once and said, "In the same pit, there is no different soil. Tsk! He ascended the hall [to give a formal sermon]. Fortunately, there was not one...
Matters: When traveling on pilgrimage, one must practice Zen; yet one is instead vexed by the appearances of Zen. If one does not penetrate the Patriarch’s Barrier, what is the Patriarch’s Barrier?
"Carrying fire into the cowpen. [The Master] ascended the hall and said: "In this way, in that way—crabs cannot leap out of the bucket.
Not in this way, not in that way—cleverness turns into clumsiness. Soft as iron, hard as mud. The diamond eye is twelve..."
Two. In the hands of the patch-robed monk, the scale-pan head is low; there is a price, yet no room for deliberation.

For one who lacks nostrils, with what shall they smell the fragrance? He ascended the hall and said: "Difficult, difficult! How many kinds! Easy, easy! No handle to grasp. Truly good at urging one toward old age."
Silently, from this, one attains it. Having passed through the four heavy barriers, the people of Sizhou see the Great Sage. [End of] the *can*.

Chan Master Zhenxie Qingliao of Changlu in Zhenzhou, a successor of Danxia Chun, was the son of the Lady of the Yong clan from Zuoyuan in Mian. From the time he was in his swaddling clothes, he entered the temple and saw...
The Buddha’s eyebrows and eyelashes moved with joy, and everyone marveled at this. At the age of eighteen, he underwent the ritual for ordination by testing his mastery of the *Lotus Sūtra*.
He went to Daci Monastery in Chengdu to study the sūtras and śāstras, grasping their essential meaning. Leaving Sichuan, he traveled to Mian and Han, where he sought out Danxia’s quarters.
Danxia asked, "What is your original self prior to the empty kalpa? As the Master was about to respond, Danxia said, "You are making a fuss; go away for now. One day—

He ascended Mount Bōyú (Bowl Basin Peak) and attained sudden, profound enlightenment. He returned directly to stand in attendance upon Master Xiázhăng. Xiázhăng said, "I thought you already knew. The Master bowed joyfully.
The following day, Xiázhăng ascended the hall and said, "The sun shines upon the solitary peak’s emerald heights; the moon descends upon the mountain stream’s chill waters.
The mysterious and wondrous secret of the Patriarchs—do not seek it within a single inch of the mind. He then descended from his seat. The Master stepped straight forward and said, "Today..."
He ascended the seat and said, "You cannot deceive me any longer. Xiang said, "Try to present your case for today’s ascent of the seat and see. The Master remained silent for a long while.

Xiang said, "I thought you had suddenly awakened. The Master then stepped down from the seat. Later, he traveled to Mount Wutai and then to the capital. Floating down the Bian River, he arrived directly at Changlu to pay his respects to Zu Zhao.
