The Master struck him again and said: *The Transmission of the Lamp*, Volume 12, Case 109: "Seeing the Buddha" (Jianfo) **Case 109: Seeing the Buddha** When the Master was at Mount Huangbo, he would often see the Buddha and not bow. One day, a monk asked, "Why do you not bow when you see the Buddha? The Master struck him with his palm and said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master struck him again and said: "The Buddha is right here before your eyes; why do you seek him elsewhere? Since you have encountered the Buddha, why do you not bow?

If you can see the Buddha within yourself, you will naturally be free from the duality of subject and object. If you seek him outside, you are merely chasing shadows. Do not mistake the finger pointing at the moon for the moon itself. This case illustrates that the true Buddha is not an external object to be worshipped, but the enlightened nature inherent within one's own mind. To see the Buddha is to realize this innate wisdom; to bow to an external image is to remain deluded by form. The Master’s striking of the monk was a direct, non-conceptual teaching intended to awaken him to this reality. As the *Platform Sutra* states, "The Way does not consist in words; it consists in seeing into one's own nature. When the monk failed to grasp this, the Master struck him once more, emphasizing that the truth cannot be captured through intellectual understanding alone, but must be realized through direct experience. This encounter remains a classic example of the Chan school’s pedagogical method of using sudden, physical action to shatter conceptual barriers and reveal the luminous mind.
"A household has no two masters. In the winter of the Gengshen year of the Xiangshi era, he constructed a large basin, pierced it with holes, and then plugged them.
He wrote a letter to Chan Master Chi of Xuedou, saying: "I am about to undergo a water burial. In the Renxu year, Chi arrived and saw that [Xingkong] was still alive;
he composed a verse to mock him, saying: "Alas, old Xingkong! You stubbornly insist on feeding the fish and turtles. If you were going, you should have gone properly; instead, you merely—"

He told this to others. The Master read the verse and said with a smile, "I shall wait for my elder brother to come and provide testimony. He then ordered that it be announced throughout the fourfold assembly.
When the assembly had gathered, the Master expounded the essentials of the Dharma and spoke this verse: "To die while sitting or standing is not as good as a water burial;
First, it saves the need for firewood; second, it saves the digging of a grave. To cast off one's hands and go forth—how unimpeded and exhilarating! Who is the one who knows this sound? A boat."
Master Zi’s lofty style was difficult to emulate for a thousand years. Few could sing his single verse of fisherman’s song.
He then sat cross-legged in a basin and drifted downstream with the tide. The assembly followed him all the way to the seashore, watching until their eyes grew weary.
The Master took a plug to stop the water and returned; the crowd pressed forward to observe, yet no water entered the basin. He then rode the current away once more, singing: "The Boatman..."

He returned to his hometown in the year [blank]. His traces having vanished, his wondrousness is difficult to measure. The true wind is universally entrusted to those who understand; he plays the iron flute crosswise as the performance concludes. The sound of that flute was mournful; shortly thereafter, amidst the vast expanse, he was seen throwing the flute into the air and vanishing.

The multitude sighed with longing and worshipped him by painting his image. Three days later, he appeared on the sand sitting in the lotus posture as if alive. Thus it was said: *The year he returned to his native land, his traces were lost and his wonder immeasurable. The true wind is sent everywhere to those who know; he plays the iron flute crosswise to end the scene. The sound of that flute was choked with grief;

a moment later, amidst the desolate void, He was seen casting the flute into the sky and vanishing. The crowd wailed in admiration, And they venerated him by portraying his likeness. Three days later, upon the sands, He sat in the lotus posture as if living.* The Way... [text ends]
The common people vied with one another to go and welcome him back. He remained for five days before his body was cremated. Relics as large as soybeans were beyond counting.
Two cranes circled in the air and only departed once the fire had been extinguished. The multitude enshrined the relics and sacred bones, constructing a stupa at Qinglong.

Qingyuan Xinfu was a successor of Chan Master Zhengfa Ximing of Chengdu Prefecture; he was a native of Hanzhou. On the occasion of the lifting of the retreat restrictions, he ascended the hall and said:

"Leaves fall in profusion from the forest trees; heaven and earth announce the early autumn. This is clearly the meaning of the Western Patriarch—what need is there to seek it further? If you understand it in this way..."

One attains [realization]. Only then does one come to believe that the Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is fundamentally level and even; that the Great Gate of Liberation has never had a lock or key;
and that it encompasses the universe and fills all of space, its measure being inexhaustible and its wisdom unfathomable.

If one has not yet clarified this principle and reached its source, then regardless of how many hundreds of kalpas of cultivation or thousands of lifetimes of refining practice one may undertake, it will merely lead to weariness and suffering in vain.

There is no interaction. If one deeply clarifies this principle and penetrates its source, one will know that in movement and stillness, in action and response, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, every instance accords with the Way and every thought flows toward the ultimate source.
As the Patriarch said: "Delusion gives rise to stillness and turmoil; awakening is free from likes and dislikes.
Let gain and loss, right and wrong, be cast off all at once. Thus, who is deluded and who is awakened? Who is this and who is that?
It is not so. It is simply that these people alone have given rise to divergent views. They observe the great as small and cling to existence and non-existence.

Their own spirit shines in isolation, yet they refuse to accept their responsibility; the moon of their mind is solitary and full, yet they themselves create opposition to it. How is this different from abandoning one’s father within the family or forgetting the pearl within one's clothing?
This causes thorns to form a forest upon the path to Bodhi, and clouds of delusion to shroud the sky of liberation.

Today, this mountain monk is fortunate to encounter the *pravāraṇā* ceremony of the assembly of monks. As the patron has returned to the mountain and these various virtuous friends have taken the trouble to visit me, I cannot remain silent.
I shall offer some idle talk according to my capacity, bending it to suit the present age and opening a small measure of expedient means.
You must all open your eyes and observe closely for yourselves. If you further hesitate or engage in discursive thought, there will be ten thousand miles of white clouds.
He then took up his staff and said: "If you can understand this, the assembly on Vulture Peak is as if standing right before you.
If it is not yet so, wait for tomorrow morning for further instruction."

Doushuai Yuefa was the successor to the Chancellor Zhang Shangying, a lay practitioner whose courtesy name was Tianjue and whose sobriquet was Wujin. At the age of nineteen, while traveling to the capital to take the imperial examinations, his route passed by the home of the Xiang family.
Prior to this, the Xiangs had received a dream in which a divine being announced, "Tomorrow, you shall receive the Excellency. At dawn, the Excellency arrived.

When he arrived, Xiang treated him with particular distinction, greeting him with great courtesy and hospitality. He then said, "Since you, a scholar-official, are not yet married, I shall offer my daughter to serve as your attendant.

Gong declined repeatedly and humbly; however, Xiang said, "If this journey of yours does not result in success, I shall not fail to fulfill our prior agreement. Later, Gong indeed passed the imperial examination and took her as his wife.
Upon his first appointment as a District Magistrate (Zhubù), he entered a Buddhist monastery and saw the golden Sanskrit manuscripts of the Tripitaka.
When the characters were written in even rows, he became indignant and said, "The books of our Sage Confucius are not equal to the teachings of these barbarians, which people look up to and revere.
Sitting in his study at night, he ground ink, took up his brush, and composed long verses upon paper, remaining awake until the middle of the night.
Lady Xiang called out to him, saying, "It is late at night, sir; why do you not go to sleep? The official informed her of his intentions, stating that he was currently engaged in this composition.
Regarding the "Treatise on the Non-existence of the Buddha," [Huiyuan] replied with a voice directed toward him: "If there is no Buddha, what would there be to discuss?

One must first establish the existence of the Buddha before one can discuss it. The official doubted his words and consequently desisted. Later, he visited a colleague and saw a scripture before a Buddha niche.
He asked, "What book is this? His colleague replied, "The *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa Sūtra*. The official then reached out his hand...

He opened the scroll and read it. Upon reaching the passage stating that "sickness is neither the element of earth nor yet separate from the element of earth," he sighed and remarked, "Can the language of the Hu people also be so?
He asked how many fascicles this sutra contained; the answer was three. He then borrowed it and returned home to read it.
Later, when Master Xiang asked him what book he had been reading, the Master replied, "The Vimalakīrtinirdeśa Sūtra. Master Xiang said, "You should read this sutra thoroughly."

Later, he composed the *Wufo lun* (Treatise on the Non-existence of the Buddha). The Duke was struck with awe and marveled at his words; from this, he developed deep faith in the Buddha Vehicle and devoted himself to the Way of the Patriarchs.
In the sixth year of the Yuanyou era, while serving as the Provincial Commissioner for Jiangxi, he first visited Chan Master Donglin Zhaojue Zong.

Zhaojue interrogated him regarding his realization, and finding it to be in perfect accord with his own, he granted him formal certification (*yinke*). Zhaojue said, "I have a disciple who has attained the Dharma and resides at..."

Yuxi was the "Compassionate Ancient Mirror" (Cigu Jing); he could indeed engage in conversation. When the Duke traveled through the region on official inspection and arrived at Fenning, the various Chan masters went out to welcome him.
Upon his arrival, the Duke first paid his respects to Yuxi Ci, and only at the very end did he inquire after Chan Master Doushuai Yue.
Chan Master Yue was short in stature; having heard that Gong Dezhuang once remarked that Yue was highly intelligent, the Duke said, "I have heard that you are skilled in literary composition."
Chongyue laughed loudly and said, "The Commissioner has lost one of his eyes. Chongyue was the ninth-generation descendant of Linji;
his discussing literary composition with the Commissioner was exactly like the Commissioner’s discussing Chan with him.

The Commissioner did not agree with these words, so he insisted on counting on his fingers and said, "It is the ninth generation. He asked, "How far is Yuxi from here? Chongyue replied, "Thirty [li]."

[The Master] said, "Five *li*. [The monk] asked, "Is that the Tuṣita Heaven? He replied, "Five *li*. The Master then passed through Tuṣita. Previously, he had dreamed of grasping the sun's orb with his hand;
upon waking, he told the Head Seat, "This is a sign of the sun's movement. I have heard that Commissioner Zhang is passing through here. I shall give him a deep thrust and a painful prick.
If he is willing to turn his head, it will be a fortunate event for our school. The Head Seat said, "The scholar-officials of today..."

He received the offerings of others, yet he was habitually fearful that their evil might manifest and give rise to further trouble. Yuè said, "Even if they cause affliction, it will merely result in my being driven from this monastery;
there is nothing else to fear. While the Duke was conversing with Yuè, he praised Dōnglín.

Yuè was not yet convinced by his words, so the Duke composed a poem for the "Imitating Waterfall Pavilion" behind the temple. Its opening lines read: "I shall not seek the traces of [the Master] on Mount Lú..."
[The Master] said: "The elephant king’s nostrils mock the vastness of the sky. This was intended as a rebuke that Donglin was not [fit for such a position].
The Master and Yue conversed until late at night, and their discussion turned to matters of the Chan school.

Yue asked, "Since Donglin has already certified you, Master, do you have even the slightest doubt regarding the teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs? The Master replied, "I do. Yue asked, "What words do you doubt? The Master said, "I doubt..."
Regarding the Verse of Xiangyan’s “Single Foot” and the Anecdote of Deshan Carrying the Alms Bowl, Yue said, "If you have doubts about this, how could you possibly be without them regarding the rest?
Take, for instance, Yantou’s statement concerning the 'Final Word'—does it exist or not? Gong replied, "It exists."
Yue laughed heartily and returned to his quarters, closing the door behind him. That night, Gong could not sleep peacefully; at the fifth watch, he rose from his bed and overturned the urinal.
At that moment, he attained great enlightenment and suddenly realized the meaning of the previous conversation. He then composed this verse: "The drum falls silent and the bell has ceased;
the bowl is carried back. A single thrust from Yantou was like thunder. Indeed, it seems he will have but three years left to live. "Is this not [the consequence]? he asked.
He came to receive his prediction [of enlightenment]. He then knocked on the door of the abbot’s quarters and said, "I have already caught the thief.
Yunyue asked, "Where is the stolen goods? The official was speechless. Yunyue said, "Commissioner, please leave for now; let us meet tomorrow. The next day, the official recited the previous verse.
Yunyue then said to him, "The reason one studies Chan is precisely because the life-root has not been severed and one generates interpretations based on words. It is like this..."
"You have already deeply realized this teaching. However, when it comes to the most subtle points, they cause people to fall into the mundane realm without even realizing or knowing it.
He then composed a verse to certify this, saying: "In ordinary conduct, every step is as it should be; though one dwells amidst sound and form,"

It is better to remain suspended between existence and non-existence; let the single mind be without differentiation and the myriad dharmas without distinction. Cease dividing essence from function, and do not select between the refined and the coarse.

Unimpeded when facing critical moments, free from constraint when responding to phenomena, all sentiments of right and wrong are exhausted, and both ordinary and sage are eliminated. Who gains and who loses?
What is near and what is distant? To take the head as the tail; to point to reality as being empty.

Turning one’s back on the realm of demons, turning one’s feet toward the path of heterodoxy—there is nothing of opposition or compliance, yet no lapse in one's practice. You invited Yue to Jianchang, observing him step by step along the way.
There were ten verses that recounted these events, to which Yue also responded with ten verses. This was in the eighth month of the eighth year of the Yuanyou era.
[This was written by] Fayaun Gao, a dharma successor.

Master Luan of Xishu was well-versed in both Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna teachings. When Fozhao retired from his duties and resided at Jingde Monastery, Master Luan asked him, "Why is it that the Chan school’s discourse often lacks a firm foundation?
Fozhao replied, "What sūtras and śāstras have you studied? Luan said, "I have a rough understanding of various sūtras."
[The Master] was somewhat proficient in the *Śata-dharma-śāstra*. Zhao said, "Just as it rained yesterday and is sunny today—into which dharma is this included?
The Master was bewildered. Zhao raised his *yǎnghézi* (itching-comb) and struck him, saying, "Do not say that what the Chan school speaks of lacks a foundation.
The Master said indignantly, "Ultimately, into which dharma is 'it rained yesterday and it is sunny today' included? Zhao said, "The second [dharma]."
[The Master] was included among the fourteen types of phenomena that do not correspond [to the nature of mind]. The Teacher was suddenly enlightened and immediately prostrated in gratitude.

Later, he returned to Shu and resided at a lecture hall, where he instructed his disciples with straightforward principles, refusing to be mired in names and forms; consequently, many followers departed. He then recited a verse and concluded his lectures, saying:
"The multitude sell flowers, while I alone sell pines; Though their green hue is fine, it does not match the red. When calculated, in the end it is not..."
In harmony with the times, he returned to the midst of the verdant mists. Thus, he lived in seclusion for twenty years.

As both monastics and laypeople pursued him with longing, he was requested once more to expound the Dharma. He replied with a verse, saying: "I have hidden my traces on the high peak, yet even the high peak will not contain me.

It is better to return to Jinli and, as before, sell my green pines. The assembly prostrated themselves in repentance, and lecturers from the two river provinces vied with one another to rely upon him.

...[he] did so. Lëtán Zuǎn was a Dharma heir of the Chan Master Tiānyóu (also known as Diānniú) of Yúnyán in Lóngxīng Prefecture. He was the son of Zhèng [family] from Chéngdū. Initially, he took the examination at the local prefectural school.
He went again to take the examination in Zizhou; he was placed on the official register for both locations, yet the Master did not dare accept it and fled through the frontier passes.

It happened that a mountain-dweller from the Valley was returning westward, and seeing that his physical bearing was extraordinary and his discourse transcendent, [the Master] traveled down the river with him in the same boat and eventually went to Mount Lu to seek out the Master [Tianyi Yihuai] and shave his head. He did not change his original name and first attended upon Sishin (Huqiu).
Qie subsequently relied upon Zhantang at Letan. One day, during a general discourse, Letan said, "Everyone is struggling so hard to seek the Buddha-dharma from me, Elder Zhuan.
He then tapped his knee and asked, "Do you understand? "Adding frost to snow," he replied.
Again tapping his knee, he said, "If you still do not understand, have you not seen Qianfeng’s address to the assembly? 'When one is raised, two must not be raised; let one pass.'"
"Attached! You have fallen into the second [category]. Upon hearing this, the Master attained sudden, penetrating enlightenment. He emerged into the world at Yungai, and subsequently moved to Yunyan.
He once composed a verse on "Tending the Ox" in response to Zhong Daozhe, which says: "Two horns point to heaven; four hooves tread the earth. Having snapped the nose-rope,"
Mushi was very foul-smelling with flatulence. When Zhang Wujin saw this, he struck his palm-boards in great admiration. Later, Mushi retired to Yunyan.
Passing through Qixian on Mount Lu, he encountered the master of the house, who was unwilling to take him in, saying, "Old and decrepit as you are, you are truly a cow pledged in a pawnshop.
Upon hearing this, the Master composed a verse and departed, saying: "How could a pawnshop ever understand pledging a cow? It is simply because the price..."
A heavy debt is difficult to repay; I imagine your original capacity was not much, and ultimately you could not withstand this one head of cattle.
Because of this, he stayed at Wuning Hermitage and named it "Tianniu" (The Cow Keeper); he never left for the rest of his life. Tudu saw him when he was already ninety-three years old.
Ascending the hall, he struck the meditation staff and said, "A long rain has not cleared; a note! The golden crow flies upon the corner of the bell tower.
He struck once more and said, "It is still in the husk. Striking again, he said, "Let the monks name it as they please.
Ascending the hall, [he said]: "When Mazu gave that one call, Baizhang missed it. Linji, that little fellow, picked up a broken [shoe] from a heap of refuse."
“Straw sandals! ‘Huh-he! ‘Huh-he! The Master roared with a shout and said, “Can it be called ‘huh-he’ and ‘huh-he’?
Ascending the hall, he said: “Xianggu’s rolling the ball has exhausted its skill; Xuansha’s chopping the plaque has also reached its limit. Do you know? A spark enters the hem of the trousers;
the matter arises from within the family. Ascending the hall, he said: “Three hundred, five hundred—copper heads and iron jaws, wooden flutes.”
[The Master] plays the flute horizontally. Whose tune does it follow? At that moment, a monk stepped forward. The Master said, "This too is drawing the bow after the thief has fled.

He ascended the hall and said: "Baofeng has a secret method; I shall explain it clearly before the assembly. Last night before the third watch, a tortoise swallowed a turtle. At the winter solstice, he ascended the hall and said:
"The movement of the sun's shadow shifts; today is the longest day of the year. My cotton trousers have not been washed, as there is no one to come and exchange them."
Zan said: "At both the Great and Small Yuquan, though there was no wind, waves arose. Yunyan saw injustice on the road and brought it down with a single blow, smashing it to pieces.
Then he cried out in a loud voice: 'Look beneath your feet!'"
Daming Yancheng’s Dharma heir was Chan Master Hui mu Yuneng of Zhongyan in Meizhou, a native of the Lü clan of that prefecture.

At the age of twenty-two, while serving as a copyist for a wealthy household in a rural village, he happened to visit a mountain temple and read a collection of Chan records; it seemed as though he had attained some realization.
He immediately tore his ceremonial cap and received full ordination. Carrying a single bowl, he traveled to various regions, first visiting Chan Master Baosheng Chengfu;
his direction of practice was quite distinct from the norm. Upon reaching Jinghu, he called upon Yong’an Xi, Zhenru Zhe, and Deshan Hui, and his realization grew even more profound.

Eventually, he arrived at Daguang Miao, where Miao asked, "Where is your home district, Senior Seat? The Master replied, "Western Sichuan. Miao said, "I have heard that in Western Sichuan there is..."

"Is it Samantabhadra Bodhisattva who has manifested? The Master said, "Today I have been able to behold your compassionate countenance. [Samantabhadra] asked, "Where is the white elephant? The Master said, "Its claws and tusks are already complete. [Samantabhadra] asked, "Do you know how to turn around? The Master took up his sitting cloth, circled the meditation seat once, and stepped out. One day, when Guishan was conducting a private interview with the assembly, [Samantabhadra] appeared. The Master said, "It is not this principle. The Master then hurried out. One day, Guishan was receiving visitors in the inner quarters for the assembly. Guishan asked, "What is the meaning of 'The mind-ground is vast and boundless'? [Samantabhadra] replied, "The sky is blue. Guishan said, "I do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The earth is yellow. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The sun and moon are bright. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The four seas are vast. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The five mountains are high. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The myriad phenomena are all here. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The Great Way is open and unobstructed. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The ten directions are empty. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The three realms are like a dream. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The six paths are like an illusion. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The eight winds cannot shake it. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The four demons cannot disturb it. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The hundred grasses are all green. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The thousand flowers are all blooming. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The spring breeze is gentle and mild. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The autumn moon is bright and clear. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The summer sun is hot and fierce. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The winter snow is cold and biting. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The morning mist is thick and heavy. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The evening clouds are thin and sparse. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The mountain peaks are steep and precipitous. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The valley streams flow deep and far. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great earth is level and even. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small path is narrow and winding. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great ocean is vast and deep. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small pond is shallow and narrow. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great tree is tall and majestic. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small shrub is low and humble. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great palace is magnificent and grand. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small hut is simple and modest. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great vehicle is broad and spacious. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small cart is cramped and confined. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great assembly is harmonious and joyful. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small group is scattered and disordered. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great drum is loud and resonant. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small bell is faint and soft. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great fire is blazing and bright. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small lamp is dim and weak. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great river flows swiftly and continuously. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small stream is slow and intermittent. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great wind blows everywhere. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small breeze stirs gently. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great rain falls heavily. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small drizzle falls lightly. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great sun rises in the east. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small moon sets in the west. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great wisdom is penetrating and clear. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small ignorance is dark and obscured. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great compassion is vast and impartial. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small affliction is narrow and limited. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great vow is firm and enduring. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small aspiration is fragile and fleeting. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great practice is constant and unwavering. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small deed is sporadic and inconsistent. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great fruit is ripe and full. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small seed is tiny and undeveloped. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great teaching is profound and subtle. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small doctrine is shallow and superficial. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great Dharma is universal and all-encompassing. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small method is partial and restricted. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The great liberation is free and unimpeded. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said, "The small bondage is tight and constricting. Guishan said, "I still do not understand. [Samantabhadra] said
He asked a monk, "After Huang Chao passed through here, was there anyone who managed to recover his sword? The monk held up his fist. Baizhang said, "A kitchen knife.
The monk replied, "But it is still of inexhaustible use. Baizhang shouted and sent him out. He then asked the Master, "After Huang Chao passed through here..."
"Is there anyone who can retrieve this sword? The Master also raised his fist. Guishan said, "That too is merely a kitchen knife.

The Master said, "If you can kill someone, then stop. He then stepped forward and struck him across the chest. Guishan said, "For thirty years I have been riding a horse, yet today I have been thrown by a donkey.
Later, he returned to Shu and, at the request of the fourfold assembly, rebuilt the site of his former hermitage.

Emerging from his quarters to dwell in gratitude for kindness, he ascended the hall. Longji said, "The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are nothing but the awakening of nature.

Originally there is no person who is deluded or awakened; it simply requires realization today. The Master said, "If there is neither delusion nor awakening, what is there to realize? *Du!* (A shout of rebuke)."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an example: One day, while Xuefeng was working together with the community to carry firewood, he saw a monk on the road and threw down a piece of wood, saying, "The entire Tripitaka speaks only of this.
Later, Zhenru Zhe said, "The entire Tripitaka does not speak of this.
Based on the words of these two venerable masters, are they the same or different? As for me, the mountain monk, I do not...
However, he held up his whisk and said: "To lift it up is 'Thus have I heard'; to let it drop is 'faithfully received and practiced.
In the room, he questioned Chongzhen Zhan-tou: "What is your parent from before the empty kalpa?

Chongzhen attained realization and said: "Venerable Sir, please lower your voice. He then offered this verse of spontaneous resonance: "In the Myriad-Year Granary, there was once famine; the Great..."

Dwelling in the midst of the sea, one’s thirst grows ever greater. At first, when seeking it, one could not find it; now, when trying to avoid it, one cannot escape it. The Master granted him formal approval (*inka*).
One day, while playing *xiqi* (chess) with Huang, the Judicial Commissioner, Huang asked: "Among all these games, not a single one is the same.
Though there are thousands and tens of thousands of moves, they are all as they are. What is that one move? The Master picked up a chess piece.
The Master showed it to him. Huang stood there lost in thought. The Master said, "Have you not heard it said: 'Of the nineteen paths from of old, how many have been driven to distraction?
The Master presided over the monastery for more than thirty years. Whenever he preached the Dharma, he did not permit his words to be recorded.
At the time of his death, he wrote a verse, sat cross-legged, and passed away. When his body was cremated, a violent wind suddenly arose; wherever the smoke reached, śarīras rained down. His Way—
The laity dug into the ground and found them all; the heart and tongue remained undecayed. They were enshrined in a stupa at the original mountain.
Chan Master Yunzhong Baojue Zongyin of Huai’an Commandery ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said: 'Recognize the bench.'"
It was more than a full circuit. He further said, "To recognize a bench is as far removed from the truth as heaven is from earth. I, this mountain monk, do not think so;
to recognize a bench—what kind of trivial furniture is that? One day, after finishing his general discourse, the Master said, "Sons, do not disperse yet.
Listen to one more verse," and he said: Forty-nine years, A scene of heated clamor. Eighty-seven...
"Spring! The old man plays alone. Who is few? Who is many? All alike are dreaming. Return! Return! The snow falls heavy upon the plum branches.
Having finished speaking, he descended from his seat, leaned on his staff, and passed away.

Chan Master Chengjue Zongxian Zhengjue of Xinsiang Monastery in Chengdu was a dharma heir of Zhaojue Chunbai. He was a native of the Wang clan of Tongchuan. In his youth, he was renowned as a successful candidate for the jinshi examination.
Once, while playing by scooping up mountain stream water during the day, he thought about it at night; consequently, he saw the water filling the room with a shimmering clarity.
He tried to draw it up but could not; yet the dusty world of phenomena was naturally empty. He said, "The net of worldly existence has been torn asunder.

He went to rely on Zhaojue for his ordination, receiving the full precepts. Later, he followed the assembly in seeking instruction. One day, Zhaojue asked the Master, "Standing atop the highest peak, walking upon the deepest ocean floor—how do you understand this?
At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment and said, "Nailed down! (Dingsha).
"Also the heels. Jue picked up his whisk and asked, "What about this one? The Master smiled and departed. He served [Jue] diligently for seven years.
Later, he traveled south to the capital and passed through Huai and Zhejiang. In his later years, he met Master Wuzu Yan at Haihui, where he went forth and asked:
"I do not yet know the pivotal point: who crosses the Zhaozhou Bridge? I shall not ask about the Zhaozhou Bridge itself."
"What is the pivotal catch? The Patriarch said, "Stay outside the door for now. The Master stepped forward, gave a kick, and withdrew.
The Patriarch said, "For so long, it turns out there has been someone who knows the flavor of this tea and rice. The next day, he entered the room.
The Patriarch said, "Are you the monk who questioned me yesterday? I certainly know where your understanding lies;
it is simply that you have not yet passed the White Cloud Barrier. The Master said, "I take my leave," and departed. At that time, Yuanwu was serving as attendant.
The Master inquired of him regarding the meaning of the White Cloud Barrier. Yuanwu said, "You must simply realize it directly. The Master smiled and said, "It is not I."
"Not so; it is simply that he is not yet familiar with it. Wait until I see this old fellow, and we shall settle the matter together.
The next day, Linji went to Shucheng, followed by the Master and Wujue. They happened to meet at Xinghua. Linji asked the Master, "Do you remember meeting me in the prefectural seat?
The Master replied, "I have been waiting for you all along. Linji looked at Wujue and said, "This fellow talks too much. From then on, he was known as "Talkative Wujue."

This was a meeting of minds. Upon returning from his travels at Mount Lu, the Master recounted to the Fifth Patriarch the words he had received while "standing atop the highest peak and walking on the bottom of the deepest sea.
The Patriarch said, "I once questioned my late master about this matter. My late master said, 'I once asked Master Yuan;
Yuan replied, "A cat has the merit of drinking blood; a tiger has the power to raise the dead. "
Virtue. Without having fundamentally mastered the source, one cannot reach it. The Master had served the Patriarch for a long time, and the Patriarch held him in great affection.

Later, when he took his leave to return westward, the Patriarch gave a small discourse (*xiao can*) and further sent him off with a verse, saying: "For over forty years I have been away from my hometown, And for a time I forgot the dialect of Shu.
When you, O Chan practitioner, return to Chengdu, You must take care to remember the dialect of Lu. At that time, Huairang was still in good health.
The Master again attended him, and his reputation became widely renowned. He subsequently went forth to reside at Changsong, and later moved to Baofu Xinsiang.
A monk asked, "The Buddhas of the three periods and the patriarchs of the six generations all fail to escape this circle.
What is this circle? The Master replied, "The rim of a well. Entering the hall, he raised the case of Yangshan asking Zhongyi, "What is the meaning of Buddha-nature?"
Yi said, "I shall give you a parable; you will understand it immediately. For example, suppose there is a room with six windows and a monkey inside.
Outside, a person calls 'Singing' from the eastern window, and the monkey responds. Likewise, he calls from all six windows and the monkey responds to each.
Then [the person] bows in worship. Having just received the Master’s instruction, I have attained something."
Doubting, Yangshan said, "What is it that you doubt? Nanquan replied, "Suppose the inner monkey has fallen asleep while the outer monkey wishes to meet him;
what then? Nanquan stepped down from his meditation seat, took Yangshan by the hand, and said, "The *xingxing* [gibbon] has already met you.
The Master said, "Do you all wish to see these two elders? I shall tell you as well."
There is an analogy. Zhongyi was much like a goldsmith. Yangshan brought him a piece of gold and asked the goldsmith to appraise its value.
The goldsmith also offered his full price in return. As they were about to finalize the transaction, the seller added extra weight to the scales.
Although the goldsmith was inwardly pleased, he could not help but harbor secret doubts in his heart. Why? "If this is not a spy, it must certainly be stolen goods.
Having said this, he descended from his seat.
The Head Seat Yan was a dharma successor of Chan Master Ze of T’ongchuan Tianning. He had originally studied Confucianism, and his literary compositions were elegant and refined.

Having entered the Buddhist order, he received the Dharma from Head Seat Yan and became a grandson of Huangbo Xingshan. He composed a "Song on Herding the Ox" (Muniu song) set to the tune of "Man Ting Fang."
He said: "Ho! You ox, though your body is strong and your vigor great, how many can truly manage to lead or ride you?
For the sake of greedily craving the lush, tender green grass upon the plains, you run hither and thither in pursuit of fragrances and verdant hues, heedless of impending peril.

Who knows that the mountains are remote and the waters far, so that when you turn your head to reach home, it will be late? Now the cowherd possesses wisdom; he holds you fast with a long rope and wields a short staff."
Gao Di enters the mud and the water, yet he never grows weary; he waits only until his mind is harmonized and his steps are steady.
Under the green pines, he plays his solitary flute crosswise as he prepares to return home. When neither man nor ox is seen, it is precisely at this time of bright moonlight.

The world takes these Chan expressions as lyrics; in their meaning and phrasing, none are more perfectly beautiful than these. Some may mock them for using unconventional sounds, but they are mixed [with the sublime].
This harms the [true] religion. Nevertheless, for those who delight in chanting and singing, they may thereby perceive the Way;
this is also not lost as one aspect of skillful means (upāya-kauśalya) established according to the capacities of beings.
Fushan Zhenfa was the dharma successor of Emei Lingyan Weicun. A monk asked, "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas;
I wonder who is Mañjuśrī’s teacher? The Master replied, "The horseherd’s wife at the sands of Jinsha."
Xinxiang Xianfa succeeded Chan Master Jinchunwen of Chengdu Prefecture. A monk asked, "What is the source of the Great Way?

The Master said, "The Yellow River has nine bends. The monk asked, "What is the command that cannot be transgressed? The Master said, "An iron snake cannot penetrate it. The monk was about to speak when—
The Master struck him.
Wuzu Yan was a dharma successor of Chan Master Foguo Keqin of Zhaojue Monastery in Chengdu; he was the son of the Luo family of Pengzhou and followed the Confucian tradition in his youth.

When the Master was a child, he could memorize a thousand words a day. Once, while visiting Miaoji Temple, he saw a Buddhist scripture; after reading it three times, he felt a sense of profound longing, as if he had recovered an old possession.
He immediately left home to follow Zizheng for his tonsure and followed Wenzhao to master the exegesis of the lectures. He further studied the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* under Minxing.
Suddenly, he fell ill and was on the verge of death, whereupon he sighed, saying: "The true path to the Nirvana of all Buddhas does not reside in the text."
"Within these words, I wished to seek form through sound; it was only natural that I should have died without success.

He then departed and went to the seat of Chan Master Zhengjue Sheng. At that time, Sheng had just wounded his arm and shed blood, pointing to it and saying to the Master, "This is a single drop from Caoxi.
The Master stared at it in awe for a long while and said, "Is the Way truly like this? He immediately set out on foot and left Sichuan, first visiting...
Yuquan Hao followed in succession under Jinluan Xin, Damingque Zhe, Huanglong Xin, and Donglin Du; all of them designated him as a vessel of the Dharma.
Yet Huitang remarked, "In days to come, the single lineage of Linji shall belong to you. Finally, he went to see Wuzu.
He exhausted all his skillful means, but the Patriarch would not grant him permission. He then accused the Patriarch of attempting to force a change of people and spoke insolent words;
departing in a fit of rage, the Patriarch said, "Wait until you are struck by a severe fever, and only then will you think of me.

Later, when the Master arrived at Mount Jin, he contracted a case of smallpox and was extremely ill. He tested [his realization] against what he had previously understood, but nothing proved effective. He sent someone to pursue...

Reflecting on the words of the Fifth Patriarch, he made a vow to himself, saying, "When my illness has slightly abated, I shall return to the Fifth Patriarch. Once his illness was cured, he returned immediately.
Upon seeing him, the Patriarch was pleased and ordered him to enter the hall for training; he was then assigned to the quarters of the attendants.

Only half a month had passed when a provincial official, returning to Shu after resigning his post, came to the Patriarch to inquire about the Way. The Patriarch said, "When you were young, did you ever read the *Xiaoyan* (Minor Elegies)?"
"No. There are two lines that are quite similar: 'Frequently calling for Xiǎoyù was originally for no reason; it was simply to have the donor recognize the sound.

When the Provincial Governor (Tíxíng) responded with 'Yes, yes,' the Master said, 'But be careful. Later, when the Master returned and was standing in attendance, [Zhao] asked, 'I heard the Master cite a poem about a beautiful woman.
Did the Provincial Governor understand it? The Master said, 'He only recognized the sound. [Zhao] said, 'Only...'"
"One must have the husband recognize the sound. Since he had already recognized the sound, why was it not so?
The Patriarch asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? [The Master replied,] "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master suddenly attained realization;
he hurried out and saw a chicken fly onto the railing, flapping its wings and crowing. He said to himself, "Is this not sound? Thereupon, he tucked [his robe] into his sleeve...
Xiang entered the room and presented his realization, offering this verse: "The golden duck has burned away the incense;
within the brocade curtains, one is supported home by others while intoxicated amidst the sounds of pipes and singing. This youthful episode of elegant refinement is known only to the lady herself.

The Patriarch said, "The great matter of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is not something that can be attained by those of inferior capacity or small roots. I rejoice with you. The Patriarch then addressed the mountain community at large.

An elder among the assembly said, "My attendant has attained Chan. Consequently, wherever he went, he was esteemed as a leader. During the Chongning era, he returned to his hometown to visit his parents;

the fourfold assembly came out to welcome and pay their respects to him. Guo Gong Zhizhang, the Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and Governor of Chengdu, invited him to open a Dharma seat at the Sixth Patriarch’s Monastery, later known as Zhaojue.
During the Zhenghe era, he retired from his duties and traveled south across the gorges. At that time, Zhang Wu...
He resided entirely in Jingnan, where he established himself as a master of the Way and was highly esteemed by those around him.

The Master (Zongmi) moored his boat to pay him a visit and engaged in an extensive discussion on the essential principles of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, saying: "The realm of direct perception (*pratyakṣa*) in the *Avataṃsaka* is the total reality of principle and phenomena;

there is not the slightest element of artificiality therein. Thus, the one is the myriad, and the myriad is realized as the one. One after one, myriad after myriad—it is vast and inexhaustible. His mind...
The Buddha, sentient beings, and the three [realms] are without distinction; they are free in their unfolding and rolling up, unimpeded and perfectly interfused.
Although this is the ultimate principle, it is ultimately just ripples on a windless lake. At this point, the Duke involuntarily drew his seat closer. The Master then asked:
"At this level, is it the same as or different from the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Duke replied: "It is the same. The Master said: "For now, you have avoided being caught."
Master Shi was visibly displeased. The Teacher said, "Have you not heard Yunmen say: 'Mountains, rivers, and the great earth have not a hair’s breadth of affliction'—this is still a 'turning phrase.
Only when one reaches the point where not a single color is seen is it 'half-raised.
You must further know that there is a time for the 'fully raised' beyond this. Were not Deshan and Linji instances of the fully raised? Master Shi then nodded his head in agreement.

The following day, they again raised the matter of the *dharmadhātu* of phenomena and the *dharmadhātu* of principle, proceeding up to the *dharmadhātu* of the non-obstruction between principle and phenomena.

The Master asked again, "Can this be called Chan? The Official replied, "It is precisely where Chan is best explained. The Master smiled and said, "Not so. This is still within the measure (*pramāṇa*) of the *dharmadhātu*.

For as long as the measure of the *dharmadhātu* has not been extinguished, it is not yet the *dharmadhātu* of the non-obstruction between phenomena and phenomena. Once that [latter] *dharmadhātu* is reached...
His [delusory] measures were extinguished. Only then did he begin to speak well of Chan. "What is the Buddha? "A dried-up dung pellet. "What is the Buddha? "Three pounds of flax.
Therefore, the verse by Zhenjing says: "Things and things are unimpeded; As one wishes, there is sovereign freedom. In hand, he grasps a pig's head; In mouth, he recites the pure precepts.
He chases his way out of the brothel, Yet has not yet repaid his wine debt. At the crossroads of the street, He unties the sack. The Master said:
"How magnificent is this discourse! How rarely can such words be heard? Thereupon, he was treated with the etiquette due to a teacher and remained at Biryam. Later, he moved to Doline.

Deng Gongzi Chang, the Grand Secretary of the Privy Council, memorialized the throne to bestow upon him purple robes and a formal title. By imperial decree, he was appointed to reside at Jiangshan in Jinling.

Scholars had no place to accommodate him, so by imperial decree he was appointed to Tianning Wan-shou Monastery. The Emperor summoned him for an audience, bestowing upon him exceptional favor and patronage.

At the beginning of the Jianyan era, he was further transferred to Jinshan. Just as the imperial carriage visited Wuyang, he entered the presence of the Emperor; the Emperor granted him the title Chan Master Yuanwu.
He was later reassigned to Yunju, and after some time, he again took charge of Zhaojue. A monk asked: "Yunmen said, 'Mount Sumeru. What is the meaning of this? The Master—
[The monk] said, "Pushing forward, it does not go ahead; drawing back, it does not retreat. He asked, "I wonder, is there still a transgression here or not?

The Master said, "Sit upon your tongue. [The monk] asked, "The Dharma does not arise in isolation; it arises only by relying on conditions. He then lifted up his sitting cloth and said, "This is the condition."

"That is the Dharma. The Master said, "But you, O *daratara*, have been robbed of your spear. [The monk] asked, "An ancient said: 'Carrying his staff slung across his shoulder, he looks not back at men;
he goes straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks. I wonder, where is his dwelling place?

The Master said, "A flying serpent coils around his feet; a road-weaver encircles his body. [The monk] said, "In the morning one gazes upon drifting clouds; in the evening one listens to the murmuring stream."
The Master said, "You must cut it off completely before you will succeed. [The student] said, "This time it is no dream; I have truly arrived at Mount Lu.

The Master said, "Keep your eyes wide open. [The student] asked, "After the monkey carries its young back to the green peaks, and the birds sing and flowers fall before the emerald cliffs—this was where you, Master, formerly established yourself and found your life-force.
What is the realm of Daolin? The Master said, "The temple gate."
[The Master] said: "Highly opening the wilds of Dongting, the base of the hall thrusts into the Chisha Lake. [The monk] asked: "What is it like to be a person within this realm? The Master said:
"The Jewel of the Sangha is present in every person; they are all pearls from the Canghu Sea. [The monk] said: "That belongs to Du Gongbu (Du Fu);

what about yours, Master? The Master said: "Do not speak so recklessly. [The monk] asked: "Regarding the saying, 'There is a phrase, there is no phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree,' how can one attain it?"
"Penetratingly free. The Master said, "A sky-reaching long sword that chills those who approach it.
[The student] asked, "As for 'the tree falls and the vines wither,' why did Muzhou laugh so heartily? The Master said, "He loved him; he took after him.
[The student] asked, "If a student were suddenly to overturn the meditation seat and break the staff, what kind of artifice would you employ then? The Master said, "That too is a thief."
Afterward, he drew his bow and asked: "Clearly revealed and manifestly majestic—why can heaven and earth not contain it?
The Master said, "The eight-sided staff in the hands of Vajrapāṇi. [The student] said, "If one suddenly calls out and returns, does that count as being alive?

The Master said, "Even Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana could do nothing about it. [The student] said, "It does not fall within illumination, nor does it fall within function. How should one deliberate upon this?"
[The student] asked, “Master, [how does one attain] measure? The Master said, “Drop the clouds. [The student] asked, “If one suddenly encounters such a person, what then?

The Master said, “Riding the Buddha Hall out through the mountain gate. [The student] asked, “When the myriad phenomena do not come and he speaks alone, who can be called upon to ascend the high peak?
The Master said, “You have wrongly applied names and phrases. He ascended the hall and said: “The whole body is eyes, yet it cannot see; the whole body is ears, yet it cannot hear.”
Chè. The whole body is mouth, yet speech does not reach it; the whole body is mind, yet discernment does not emerge from it.

Even if one were to realize this throughout the entire world without the slightest leakage, one would still be halfway there. To uphold the command and fully raise it—tell me, how is it to be manifested?
The sun and moon hang freely within the realm; across the vast void, ten thousand ages are spring. The fifth year of Xiangxi. August.
Chuyue manifested a slight ailment; sitting cross-legged, he wrote a verse to leave behind for the assembly, then cast down his pen and passed away.

During the cremation, his tongue and teeth remained unburnt, and countless five-colored śarīras were produced. He was interred in a stupa beside Zhaojue Temple, and posthumously titled Chan Master Zhijue.
Chan Master Qingyuan Foyan of Longmen in Shu Prefecture was the son of the Li family from Linqiong. He was dignified and upright, speaking but little. At fourteen, he received full ordination.
Later, while reading the Lotus Sūtra, he came to the passage: "This Dharma cannot be understood through thought, deliberation, or discrimination.
He took this up and questioned a lecturer, but the lecturer was unable to answer. The Master sighed and said, "The terminology and characteristics of scholastic study are not what I seek."
Having resolved upon the great matter of birth and death, he then rolled up his robes and traveled south to attend the Dharma seat of Chan Master Yan of Taiping in Shu Prefecture.
While begging for alms in Luzhou, he happened to fall to the ground; amidst his distress, he heard two people cursing each other in mutual abuse.
One who was admonishing them said, "You are still dwelling in affliction (*kleśa*). Upon these words, the Master attained a realization. When he returned, whenever anyone questioned him...
Yan immediately said, "I am not as good as you; you naturally understand it well. Or he might say, "I do not understand; I am not as good as you.
The Master became increasingly suspicious and subsequently consulted with the Head Seat Yuanli for a definitive resolution. Yuanli then took the Master by the ear with his hand.

He circled the brazier several times, walking and speaking as he went, saying, "You understand this well enough. The Master said, "I hoped you would provide some instruction; why do you instead mock me with such words?
Lirong replied, "Only after you have attained realization in the future will you understand the twists and turns of today. Taiping was about to move to Haihui Monastery.
The Master sighed deeply and said, "I have just returned from begging for alms; yet I must follow you again to that desolate place."
"How could I possibly investigate and resolve my own matter? he thought. He then composed a verse to take his leave and went to Jangshan to spend the summer retreat.

There, he met Chan Master Lingyuan by chance, and their friendship grew increasingly deep. During a relaxed conversation, the Master said, "Recently, I have seen a venerable elder in the capital whose words and phrases seem to have a karmic affinity with me.
Lingyuan replied, "Master Yan is a peerless patriarch, the very best in the world. Why [do you say this]?"

Therefore, he abandoned [his studies] to pursue travel afar. As for those so-called "karmic conditions," they were merely teachers of intellectual understanding who corresponded with the Master’s initial resolve.
Following their encouragement, the Master proceeded directly to Haihui. Later, he was appointed to oversee the reception of guests; it happened that one cold night, he sat alone.
Stirring the embers, he saw a spark about the size of a bean. Delighted, he exclaimed, "Deeply stirring the ashes, there is something here;

the affairs of my entire life are just like this. He immediately rose and examined the *Lamp Records* (*Denglu*) on his desk. Upon reaching the account of the "Fallen Hearth," he suddenly attained great enlightenment and composed a verse:
"Stroke after stroke, the forest birds cry out; I don my robes and sit through the night. Stirring the fire, I awaken to my whole life— How utterly exhausted!"
The spirit has returned to its ruin; the matter is clear, yet people remain deluded. Who can harmonize the winding and the plain?

Thinking of this, I shall never forget it; few pass through the open gate. Yuanwu went to his quarters and tested him with the story of Qinglin moving earth, saying, "No one since ancient times has been able to produce a response to this.
How do you understand it? The Master replied, "What difficulty is there in that? Yuanwu said, "As for him..."

"Way! This is the intent of the Iron Wheel-turning King throughout the realm. What do you think? The Master said, "I say that a proclamation of amnesty is being issued from within the palace of Śakra.
Wuzu later remarked to others, "It is fortunate that Elder Yuan already possesses a phrase that brings life to others.
From then on, he lived in seclusion at the Dazhong Hermitage in Simian. It happened that the entire country was renovating the Chongning Wanshou Monastery; Wang, the Governor of Shu...

He was summoned by Imperial Decree to disperse the assembly and was ordered to open the Dharma. He subsequently took up residence at Longmen, where his reputation for the Way was even more widely celebrated. Later, he moved to Baoshan Temple in Hezhou.

The State Censor Deng Xunwu submitted a memorial requesting that the Master be granted the title of "Teacher" (Shi) and purple robes. Ascending the hall, he said: "On the road to Mount Tai, travelers are exceedingly few;
before the Hall of the Broken Oven, there is no ground left for gratitude. Snow buries the cypress trees in the courtyard; ice locks the Yan River. Although..."
He stands at the head of the southern furnace; he does not enter the condiment jars of others' houses. Look!
On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, it is as if it were still cold in the first month of spring. You all must each exert yourselves and press forward; take care not to give way to self-defeat.
*Jinjiang Chandelu*, Scroll Five;
