Compiled by Zhaojue Zhangxue Tongzui.
Edited by Hu Shengyou of Huan’an in Xiangshui.
The fifteenth generation descendant of Dajian (Huineng),
heir to the Dharma of the Fifth Patriarch Yuan.
Chan Master Nantang Yuanjing of Daisui in Pengzhou was the son of Zhao Gong Yuezhong, a great Confucian scholar from Yushan in Langzhou.
At the age of ten, he fell gravely ill; every time he prayed for his recovery, he experienced a miraculous dream, leading his parents to allow him to renounce the world and enter the monastic life.

The Master followed the lineage of Zongyi at Daoci Baosheng Monastery in Chengdu. In the third year of the Yuanyou era, he attained ordination after mastering the scriptures and remained at the lecture assembly for many years.
He then traveled south, first visiting Chan Master Yong’an En, through whom he gained insight into the story of Linji’s three blows of the staff.
Subsequently, he relied upon various renowned masters, yet none satisfied his mind. Hearing that Wuzu was of sharp and rigorous faculty and wishing to test him, he went to visit the Patriarch.
The Patriarch then said, "This place of mine is not like other quarters.

Within this room, I do not require you to step forward or retreat, to point with your finger or raise your fist, to circumambulate the meditation seat, to perform the bows of a woman, or to brandish your sitting mat—none of these thousand kinds of clever maneuvers."
"Only when you speak one word that hits the mark will it be your true point of view. The Master was at a loss. He withdrew to practice for three years.
One day, after the private interview had concluded, the Patriarch said to him, "The words you have offered are already ninety percent correct; try to explain them to me further.
The Master then analyzed and presented his understanding. The Patriarch said, "You can indeed explain it well enough—now, give me your own judgment upon it."
The Master judged each question as it was asked. The Patriarch said, "Excellent, indeed excellent; yet you have not yet grasped the old monk’s way of speaking.
After the midday meal, come to the site of the Patriarch’s stupa, and I shall examine each point with you one by one. When [the student] arrived...
The Patriarch [Nanquan Puyuan] then spoke of "mind is Buddha" and "neither mind nor Buddha"; of Muzhou as the "man carrying a wooden board"; of Nanquan's "beheading the cat";
and of Zhaozhou’s words regarding whether a dog has the Buddha-nature or not. He compiled and analyzed these, responding to them all without the slightest hesitation.
When he reached the story of the "wild dog," the Patriarch suddenly turned his face away and said, "That is not it. The Master replied, "If it is not it, then what is?"
"How is it? the Patriarch asked. "If this is not it, then everything preceding it is also not it. The Master said, "I hope the Venerable One will compassionately instruct me.
The Patriarch said, "Look at what he says: 'The Son of Hu has a dog; it takes people's heads from above, takes people's waists from the middle, and takes people's feet from below.
Those who enter the gate must look well. As soon as a monk enters the gate, he immediately says, 'Look at the dog! He pointed toward [the monk].
"Zihu, speak where you saw the dog; give me a turning word that will leave Zihu tongue-tied and cause this old monk to clench his jaw.
That shall be your point of realization. The next day, when [Zhaozhou] entered the room, the Master silently revealed the meaning of what had been said.

The Patriarch laughed and said, "I do not say that you are not a man who has settled the matter once and for all; however, these words merely resemble those spoken by my former teacher. The Master said, "I..."
"Who could possibly be like Master Duan? The Patriarch said, "Not so. Although I am his successor, I consider his words to be clumsy;
this is because he only employs the methods of Master Yuanlu to receive people. As for me, I [employ different methods] alongside Master Yuanlu."
He would have walked hand-in-hand with Baizhang, Huangbo, Nanquan, Zhaozhou, and their peers; had he seen [Dongshan’s] words as clumsy, he would have deemed them unworthy.
The Master, however, did not think so. He took up his staff and crossed the river, only to find the waters swollen by a great flood, which caused him to remain at Fourth Patriarch [Dayu].
His peers urged him to return, but after another two years, the Patriarch finally gave his approval. Once, while they were discussing the past and present, he grasped—
The Master said, "What you have spoken must be my raising; what you have raised must be my speaking.
From this day forward, the secret essentials of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and the pivotal keys of all quarters shall not escape your grasp. He then established the Nantang Hall for him to reside in.
Thereupon, his fame topped the world. Governor Xi Gongdan of Chengdu invited him to open the Dharma at Jiayu. Not long after—
He moved several times, from Zhaojue to Nengren, and finally to Dawsui. Entering the hall, he said: "The sovereign is clearly aware; the generals are wide awake.
Once victory is achieved, the six states are brought to peace. Entering the hall, he cited the story of Linji’s visit to Huangbo.
Master Baiyun Endan offered this verse: "A single punch knocks down the Yellow Crane Tower; A single kick overturns the Parrot Isle. There is..."
"His spirit adds to his spirit; even where there is no elegance, he is elegant. The Master said, "Dasuì, it is not so.
At seventy years of age, I am old and clumsy, yet my eyes are sharp and clear and my ears do not ring.

If someone should suddenly come to insult me, I shall knock them down with a single punch and send them over the pass to the east of the River. Ascending the hall, after the question-and-answer session, he said: "Since the time of the Patriarchs..."
People misunderstand this; they take mere words and phrases to be the Way of Chan. Little do they realize that the Way has no essence—it is only because of an essence that it receives its name.
The Way has no name—it is only because of a name that its designation is established.

For instance, just now, as soon as you, Venerable Sir, came out in such a manner and returned to the assembly in such a manner, did the Way possess eyes or not? If the Way possessed eyes, then as soon as...
Coming forth in such a manner—where does the eye reside? If you say he lacked eyes, how could he have gone forth in this way?
O worthy ones, if you can see clearly and decisively at this point, you will know that when the Second Patriarch prostrated himself and stood in his place, he truly attained the marrow.
This very little bit is the life-root of the Buddhas of the three periods and the six generations of patriarchs.
The life-vein: the place where the old monks of the world establish their dwelling and sustain their lives. Although this is so, one must arrive there in person before it can be attained.
Chan Master Wúwéi Zōngtài of Hànzhōu was a native of Fúchén. Since leaving the Pass, he traveled extensively through monastic communities until he reached the Fifth [Patriarch].
On the day of the incense offering, the Patriarch brought up the story of Zhaozhou washing the alms bowl and had him investigate it.

When [Zhaozhou] entered the room, the Patriarch raised this story and asked the Master, "Tell me, what did Zhaozhou say to that monk? That monk attained enlightenment immediately. The Master said, "He said, 'Go wash your alms bowl.
The Patriarch said, "You know only the matters of the road; you do not know the flavor of the road. The Master said, "Since..."
"Know the matter of the road. What flavor is there on the road? The Patriarch said, "Do you not know? He asked again, "Have you ever traveled through Zhejiang? The Master replied, "No.
The Patriarch said, "You have not yet attained realization. From that time on, for five years, the Master was unable to respond.
One day, the Patriarch ascended the hall, looked at the assembly, and said, "An eighty-year-old old man rolls a brocade ball," and then he descended from his seat.
The Master joyfully stepped forth from the assembly and said, "Venerable Monk, try rolling it once and see.

The Patriarch made a gesture with his hands as if beating a war drum and sang a folk song from Mianzhou in the Shu dialect: "On Mount Douzi they beat the earthen drums; On Mount Yangping they scatter a hundred rains.
As the white rain falls, they fetch the Dragon Maiden; She weaves two zhang and five chi of silk. Half belongs to Luo Jiang, and half..."

Half of it belongs to Xuánwǔ. Upon hearing this, the Master attained great enlightenment. He covered the Patriarch’s mouth and said, “It is enough to sing up to this point. The Patriarch laughed heartily and returned home.
Later, when the Master returned to Shǔ, the fourfold assembly requested him to open the Dharma at Wúwéi. He was subsequently transferred to Zhèngfǎ. Ascending the hall, he said:
“This great matter of cause and condition—ever since the World-Honored One held up the flower and Kāśyapa smiled, the World-Honored One said: ‘I have...’”
The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye was entrusted to Mahākāśyapa.
Thereafter, it has been transmitted from lamp to lamp and passed down from patriarch to patriarch until the present day, continuing unbrokenly so that flowers bloom everywhere upon the ground.
For this reason, it is called the wondrous mind of *nirvāṇa*, and it is also called the original mind, the original nature, the original face, and the primary truth (*paramārtha*).
The Truth. It is also called the *śakara* eye, and it is also called the Great Mahāprajñā. In a man, it is called "man"; in a woman, it is called "woman.
You virtuous ones, simply awaken for yourselves! All such things are merely idle words. Then, picking up his whisk, he said: "To understand it is called Chan;
yet before awakening, it is truly difficult, difficult, difficult. Before one's eyes, there is a barrier that must be pierced."
Mount Mi: Awakening is easy, easy, easy. To speak from the mouth of faith, there is nothing that is not so. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Who told you to ask such a question? The monk hesitated; the Master said, "Awakened."
Chan Master Wuzu Baizhang of Qizhou was a native of Huai’an. He initially relied upon the Fifth Patriarch for the longest period of time, yet he had not yet attained realization.
At that time, Yuanwu served as the head of the assembly (Zaoyuan). The Master went to seek his instruction, and Yuanwu said, “Brother, try telling me where you have doubts.

The Master then cited the passage from Deshan’s informal sermon: “I do not answer those who come to talk; I give thirty blows to those who ask a question. Yuanwu said, “Prostrate yourself; I [will speak].”
"You have become my teacher, yet you still do not understand this story. After the Master had finished bowing, Wuzu ordered him to repeat the previous dialogue.

The Master said, "Deshan’s informal sermon stated that he would not answer questions. Wuzu covered his mouth and said, "Just look at it like this. The Master went out and cried out loudly, "A grievance! A grievance!
How can there be a public case (gong'an) that merely instructs one to look at a single phrase? A monk remarked:
The Master said, "Brother, you must not speak in such a manner. The Head Seat must have some skillful means.

Because he sat in meditation and investigated this for ten days, his doubts were suddenly resolved. He went to pay his respects to Wuzhuo, who said, "Brother, now you finally know that I did not deceive you.

He then went to the Abbot’s quarters; the Patriarch (Zongmi) welcomed him with a smile. From that time on, [his understanding] grew daily deeper and more profound. When the Patriarch was about to pass away, he left a message to the Prefectural Governor. The Governor...

He was appointed to succeed him on the seat, and monks arrived from all directions in such numbers that they could not be stopped. The Master posted a notice at the gate of his quarters for the attendants, saying:
"Dongshan has three statements; if anyone can express them, they shall be granted formal entry. The monks were all disheartened and withdrew.
One day, a monk carrying his sitting mat went straight to the master’s chamber and said to him, "I cannot express them, but I only wish to be granted entry. The Master was greatly pleased.
He called for the *vinaya-dhara* (Venerable of Discipline) to arrange the seating beneath the bright window. He ascended the hall. When the World-Honored One held up a flower, Kāśyapa smiled.
People of that time knew only the holding of the flower and the smile, yet they failed to recognize the World-Honored One. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Dancing the *zhazi* in a thicket of brambles. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "New..."
"Throwing the Golden Basin upon Giving Birth.
Chan Master Daochu of Longhua in Qizhou was the son of the Ma family of Zizhou. He served as Abbot Zu’s attendant for many years.

On the day he took up residence at Longhua, he ascended the hall and said: "When a rooster sees [another], it fights; when a dog sees [another], it bites. The *chīwén* (ornamental ridge-end) on the hall roof [remains] all day long..."
"Relative. "Why then do you not become angry? He then descended from his seat. The Master’s wit and eloquence were sharp and swift; his disciples were unable to fathom the depth of his realization.
One day he said to the assembly, "Yesterday I left the city; white clouds came and went through the void.

The pine wind clears the ears and eyes; it is truly superior to the human world. He called the assembly together and said, "This is the final word of my late teacher. After a short while, he passed away.
However, he passed away.

Chan Master Qing Su of Jiuding Peak in Jiazhou was the son of the Guo family of that same prefecture. He received the tonsure and ordination at Qianming Temple and traveled widely, knocking at the gates of various Chan masters.
Later, he visited the Fifth Patriarch; upon hearing the Fifth Patriarch cite the words of Shoushan regarding the meaning of the Westward Journey, he attained sudden enlightenment.
He recited a verse: "Upside down, upside down, upside down! The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. To act thus is utterly groundless;
Turning one's head, one does not realize one’s robe has been torn. When the Patriarch saw this, he asked, "What about Baizhang’s story of the wild fox?
The Master said, "Those who come to speak of right and wrong are themselves the people of right and wrong. The Patriarch was greatly pleased. After some time, the Master took his leave.

He returned to reside at Qingxi, and subsequently moved to Jiuding. When Governor Lü came to visit the Great Image, he asked, "Since this is the Great Image, why does it carry two pillars upon its shoulders?
The Master replied, "There are no idle laborers on board the ship.

Upon reaching the pavilion and beholding the Avalokiteśvara image, he asked again, "In the realm of Maitreya’s transformation, from where has Avalokiteśvara come? The Master replied, "The child is spoiled because the family is wealthy."
Shou then paid his respects. When Qin Laosu arrived, the Master asked, "When the sword is at the throat during a dance, what then?
Qin replied, "I humbly pray that you will graciously accept [this offering]. The Master rebuked him, saying, "Old thief! Go die! You ask me. Qin then proceeded with the previous line of questioning.

The Master folded his hands in a gesture of greeting and said, "Drag it apart! On the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month in the year of Yimao (1135) of the Xiangxing era, he fell slightly ill. He wrote this verse:
He addressed his followers, saying: "The wooden man prepares the boat; the iron man prepares the horse. The young boy of the Bing and Ding stems boards securely.
With a shout, he scatters the white clouds and returns. Thereupon, he passed away into stillness.

The Sixteenth Generation Descendant of Dajian (Da Jian), Chan Master Foting Fatai of Da Mei in Tanzhou, a successor of Zhaojue Qin and a native of the Li clan of Hanzhou. A monk asked: "Principle follows phenomena..."

Transformation: though it encompasses all existence, it is a single expanse of void-stillness; as phenomena follow along with principle, the myriad differences all return to the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
"What is the realm of principle (*dharmadhātu*)? The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. [The student] asked, "What is the realm of phenomena (*vastudhātu*)?"

The Master said, "The myriad phenomena are densely arrayed. [A monk] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between principle and phenomena? The Master said, "East, west, south, and north.

[Another monk] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between phenomena and phenomena? The Master said, "Above, below, and the four intermediate directions. He then ascended the hall for formal instruction.
Pushing toward the truth, the truth has no marks; exhausting delusion, delusion has no form. When both truth and delusion are non-existent, the eyes are revealed in vast openness.
The eyes being revealed, what do you see? "The morning sun melts the snow on the crags;
the northern wind blows open the wax-plum blossoms. [Ascending the hall: "When the precious sword is drawn, it is used immediately—how could there be any hesitation? [He points to his eyebrows.]
Lift it up and you go; there is no further turning back or evasion. In every place, he soars, illuminating the present and the past; in every place, he cuts through all nets and cages.

He does not strike the sharp edge, nor does he look back in reflection. Setting aside for a moment his solitary transcendence beyond all things—when the myriad functions have been utterly exhausted, what then?
"In the autumn of the eighth month, where is it hot? [The Master] ascended the hall and said: "Nirvana has no alternative path; expedient means..."
[The Master speaks] in many ways. He picks up his staff and says: "Look, look! This staff of mine has swallowed the waters of the Western River in a single gulp.
A carp from the Eastern Sea leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens. Indra, filled with wrath, strikes Mount Sumeru with a blow that shatters it to pieces.
The Earth Goddess, Sthāvarā, joins her palms and praises him, saying: 'Behold the Dharma of the Dharma King! The Dharma King—
Such is the nature of the Dharma. Striking the meditation seat with his staff, he descended from the seat and ascended the hall, saying:

"To realize the emptiness of persons and the emptiness of dharmas does not yet accord with the ancestral style of the Buddhas. To embody total function and total illumination is likewise not the essential subtlety of a patch-robed monk.
You must directly shatter the secure barrier and recognize the single aperture above. What is this aperture above? The spring chill is biting."
"Freezing to death the young man. He ascended the hall and said: "Today is already the middle of the first month. Everywhere the lamps and lanterns are in disarray;

the entire city is filled with crowds in silks and brocades, coming and going to enjoy the festivities. Mañjuśrī has run into the midst of the bustling crowd; Samantabhadra sits upright atop a high tower watching.
But tell me, where is Avalokiteśvara? The painted drums beat, shaking the heavens; the music resounds, deafening the earth."
Flute and song. Ascending the hall: Vast and remote, encompassing the ten directions; level and expansive, transcending form and appearance.
The eyes wish to look, yet the pupils wither; the mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have no skill at all.
Linji and Deshan were not without their bold proclamations: a tortoise swallowed the iron ox of Shanzhou, and a snake bit the Great Image of Jiaozhou;
they terrified the carp of the Eastern Sea until this very day, its belly remains bloated with laughter.
Chan Master Huiyuan Fohai of Lingyin in Lin’an was the son of the Peng family of Meishan.

At the age of thirteen, he left home to become a monk under Zongbian of Yaoshi Monastery. He went to Daci to study and practice, but later left to rely upon Chan Master Weihu of Lingyan, where he attained a slight realization.
When Yuanwu returned to lead Zhaojue, the Master went to him; there, hearing Yuanwu’s general discourse (*pushe*), he was presented with the story of Layman Pang.
The Master asked Mazu about the causal conditions for "not being a companion to the myriad dharmas. Suddenly, the Master attained sudden enlightenment and collapsed among the assembly.
As the assembly helped him up, the Master said, "I have awakened from my dream. Later that night, during a small *śamaya*, the Master went forward and asked:
"Pure and naked, empty with not a single thing; bare-boned and poor, without a single coin. My house is ruined and my family lost; I beg the Master for relief. Mazu said:
He seized all seven treasures and eight jewels at once. The Master said, "Calamity does not enter the door of a prudent household. Wuzhuo said, "The pivot does not leave its station;
you have fallen into a sea of poison. As he spoke, the Master let out a shout. Wuzhuo struck the meditation seat with his staff and asked, "Have you eaten the staff yet?
The Master shouted again. Wuzhuo shouted twice in succession. The Master then bowed. From that time on, their exchange of spiritual sparks continued.
Jungfa was unimpeded in his realization. When Yuanwu passed away, the Master traveled eastward and successively occupied famous monasteries.

From Huqiu, he received an imperial decree to reside at Gaoting; subsequently, he was again appointed to Lingyin by imperial edict. Emperor Xiaozong summoned him for an audience and bestowed upon him the title Chan Master Fohai.
He ascended the hall and said: "The New Year has its own occasion: brewing tea and ascending the wine tower. A pair of feet have become two."
Half a person has three heads; protruding, it is difficult to discern in meditation. Meeting face-to-face brings grief even to ghosts.
Blowing a holeless flute upside down, they dance the Liangzhou to a rapid beat. *Du!* (Hark!)
Chan Master Zhengfa Jian of Chengdu Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have no horns.
Beyond a single hair’s breadth, as vast as mountains and peaks. Upon the point of a needle, the lion turns its body; within the hollow of a lotus root, the great garuḍa spreads its wings."
"Indifferently he suddenly passed beyond Uttarakuru; the sun, moon, and stars all turned black at once.
Chan Master Anmin Huizang Miyin of Jian'an Fu was the son of the Zhu family from Jiading Fu.

Initially, he lectured on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* in Chengdu and became a refuge for those studying the scholastic teachings (*yixue*). At that time, Yuanwu resided at Zhaojue Temple, and the Master [Anmin] together with Chan Master Sheng...

He became a friend to Wuzu Fayan and visited him there. Upon hearing Wuzu’s small-scale discourse (xiaocan), he was presented with the kōan concerning the National Teacher’s three calls to his attendant.

Zhaozhou commented on it, saying: "It is like a person writing characters in the dark; though the characters themselves do not take shape, the traces of the brushstrokes are already manifest. Where is it that the traces are already manifest?
The Master harbored doubts about this and requested an audience by offering incense and entering the room. Wuzu asked, "What sutra does the Dharma Master lecture upon? The Master replied—
He said, "The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*. Wuzhuo said, "In the *Śūraṅgama*, there are the 'Seven Locations for Examining the Mind' and the 'Eight Reversions to Discern the Vision.

Ultimately, where does the mind reside? The Master presented many displays of artful understanding, yet Wuzhuo refused to accept them all. The Master again requested further instruction. Wuzhuo told him to compose a verse on the theme "Where the Pattern is Fully Manifested" in every situation.
By chance, a monk requested instruction on the *Ten Mysterious Gates of Discourse*. Just as [Wuzhuo] raised the question, "I ask you, the seal of the mind—"
"What face do I have? Wuzhuo shouted, "The patterns are already manifest! Upon hearing this, the Master attained a realization and subsequently sought certification.
Wuzhuo applied his authentic hammer and tongs, leaving the Master at a loss for words. One day, the Master said to Wuzhuo, "Master, please stop citing these stories;
let me speak on them. Wuzhuo agreed. The Master said, "When one ordinarily brandishes the mallet or raises the whisk, is that not the teaching found within the sutras?"
Daowei said, "All the various marks of all worlds are, in their entirety, the wondrously luminous true mind of bodhi.
Wuzu laughed and said, "So you have been making your living right here all along? Daowei spoke again:

"When you let out a shout or strike the meditation seat, is that not 'turning the hearing back to hear the self-nature,' whereby that nature achieves the unsurpassed Way? Wuzu said, "Have you not seen it stated in the sutras: 'The wondrous...'"?

The nature is perfectly luminous and free from all names and characteristics. Under these words, Wuzhuo attained sudden enlightenment. He left Sichuan and resided at Jia Shan. While Wuzhuo was concluding his lectures, he accompanied him on his travels.

One night, as Wuzhuo was giving a private instruction to the assembly, he cited the kōan concerning the ancient sail that had not yet been hoisted. Upon hearing this, Wuzhuo did not yet comprehend it.

He then sought a definitive resolution. Huineng said, "Ask me. The Master repeated his previous question. Huineng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. At that moment, the Master attained complete and penetrating clarity.
He said to Huineng, "The ancients said, 'It is like a drop of water cast into a vast ravine,' yet they did not realize that the great ocean can be cast into a single drop.
Huineng laughed and said, "What can be done about this fellow? Not long after, he was ordered to share the seat [with the Master].
Chan Master Ché'ān Dàyuán of Zhāojié Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture was the son of the Dèng family from Miān Prefecture. He received full ordination at Jiángjí Temple.

Later, traveling east, he went to call upon Chan Master Dào of Dàbié. While contemplating the words "Vast emptiness—no sage," he suddenly burst into laughter and said, "So it was here all along that Bodhidharma has been!
Dào praised him. Subsequently, he went to study under Chan Masters Fójian and Foyǎn.
Having received an official appointment as a reward, he went to Jinshan to rely upon Yuanwu. He informed Yuanwu of his insights, but Yuanwu did not approve of them.

When Yuanwu was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Yunju, the Master followed him there. Although he attained a degree of conviction and entry, he remained suspicious because a sense of obstruction had not yet been removed from his breast.
Yuanwu asked a disciple, "When the time of birth and death arrives, what then? The monk said, "The incense altar laughs at the Master. Yuanwu then asked the teacher, "What about you?
The teacher said, "The grass-robbers are utterly defeated. Yuanwu said, "If someone asks you this, how will you respond?
As the teacher was about to answer, Yuanwu overawed him, saying, "The grass-robbers are utterly defeated! At that moment, the teacher attained thorough realization. Yuanwu [said]:...

He struck him with his fist. The Master clapped his hands and laughed loudly. Yuanwu asked, "What did you see that you act like this? The Master replied, "The poisonous fist has not yet been requited;

it shall never be forgotten for kalpas. Yuanwu returned to Zhaojue and appointed the Master as the head of the community. When Yuanwu was about to pass away, he entrusted the seat of the abbacy to the Master.
Chan Master Yuanjue of Mount Xiang’er in Meizhou was the son of the Yuan clan of that prefecture. He entered the monastic order and transmitted the *Lamp of the Dharma*.

Having passed the scriptural examinations, he received ordination; his original name was Yuánjué (Complete Enlightenment). When the Prefectural Governor filled out the temple registration document, he mistakenly wrote the character "Yuán" (袁) instead of "Yuán" (圓).

Suspecting that the Master felt dissatisfied, the governor jokingly said to him, "Is it permissible for a name to consist of only a single character? The Master laughed and replied, "Even one character is already too many. The governor marveled at this. Once—
He received full ordination and left Sichuan to visit various venerable masters who possessed the Way. Later, he went to Daopei to rely upon Foxing.

After a short while, he entered the inner quarters to present his insights. Foxing said, "You have gone far astray," yet recognizing him as a vessel for the Dharma, he appointed him as an attendant to manage guests.
Whenever the Master attended upon Foxing, Foxing would invariably cite the four characters of the *Lotus Sūtra*: "Open, Show, Awaken, Enter."
He gave a word. Again he said, "Wait until the moment I nod my head upright; only then will you be correct. By chance, he was dismissed from his post due to negligence.
During the period of administrative restriction, having no place to rely on, he stayed at the home of a layman. One day, while reciting the *Lotus Sūtra*, he reached the passage:

"Furthermore, one does not know what is fire and what is the house," whereupon he attained sudden enlightenment. When the restrictions were lifted and he returned for an audience, Xingjian nodded in approval. Yuanwu—
He received another imperial decree to reside at Yunju. Upon arriving there, the Master presented his realizations to Wuzhuo. Wuzhuo scolded him, saying, "This is originally a place of purity;
why are you defecating here? At these words, the Master's doubts were suddenly resolved. In the Ding-si year of the Xiangxing era, the seat at Xiang'er in Mei became vacant.
The Prefect said, "This monastery has long been a den for vermin; none but men of renown and superior character can restore it from its ruins.
The various Chan masters recommended the Master to accept the invitation. He once said to a guest: "Sudao Dongpo said, 'I carry this stone back home; within my sleeves lies the Eastern Sea.
Huang Tingjian (Shan谷) said, 'Huihong’s misty rain, reeds, and wild geese sit me amidst the Xiao and Xiang rivers and Lake Dongting. I wish..."
"Calling for my small boat to return; bystanders say it is a painting. This is the very marrow of Chan. He also said:
"When I strike the meditation seat and raise the whisk, Śākyamuni and Confucius are both standing downwind. Someone once cited these words.
This resembles the words of Chan Master Haiyuan of Mount Yu. Yu said, "These are the words of Old Man Jue; here in my own tradition, it is not like that.
Chan Master Huayan Zuojue of Zhongyan in Meizhou was the son of the Yang family of Jiazhou. From childhood, he was intelligent and could recite from memory any book or history after reading it once.
He wrote a treatise to refute Buddhism, but when a terrifying vision suddenly appeared before him, he repented and left the household life, taking refuge under Hui mu.

Chan Master Neng soon thereafter developed an abscess on his knee that no physician could cure for five years. While he was transcribing the *Huayan jie shen mi yao fangbian fenqi zhang*, one night he experienced a miraculous dream.
At dawn, he immediately cast aside his crutches and began walking. One day, as he recited the "Chapter on Manifesting Signs," he came to these lines:
"The Buddha-body has no birth, yet it can manifest birth; the Dharma-nature is like empty space, and all Buddhas dwell therein. No—
He realized that even while abiding there is no going, and that the Buddha is present everywhere; thus, he attained enlightenment into the essential tenets of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.

Upon being enrolled in the monastic registers, the Master of the Prefecture invited him to lecture at the Qianbu Hall. His eloquence was grand and expansive, earning the admiration and respect of the assembly.

It happened that Chan Master Jing of the Southern Hall passed by his door and said to him, "I observe that your lectures are peerless in the southwest; yet, I regret that you have not yet transcended the realm of words."

"I foresee that if you should inquire into the Way beyond the mundane, you will be the present Zhou Jingang. The Master joyfully ceased his lectures and traveled south, relying upon Yuanwu at Mount Zhongfu.
One day, he entered the room [for private instruction], and Yuanwu cited the words of Luoshan: "When there are words, one crouches on the tiger’s head and gathers the tiger’s tail;
under the first phrase, clarify the fundamental principle. When there are no words, one directly reveals the sharp point of the pivot. As it was said:
"Regarding 'The same as a lightning-sweeping broom'—how do you understand this? The Master was unable to respond. He spent day and night investigating it, until suddenly he attained realization.
He presented a verse of his awakening, saying: "My home is atop a solitary peak; For many years the door has been half-closed. I lament that my own life is already old;
My livelihood is now entrusted to my descendants. Dongwu saw that he was acceptable. The next day, [the Master] entered the room for private instruction. Dongwu again asked: "Yesterday’s koan—"
"How is it? Ma prepared to respond. Wuzhuo immediately shouted, "The Buddha-dharma is not this kind of principle.

The Master remained with him for another five years, becoming even more bewildered and distressed. Later, while at Qixian on Mount Lu, he read Chan Master Fushan Yuan’s *Treatise on Eliminating Attachments*, which states:

"If one says that there are those who are close and those who are distant to awakening, how could there be stinking weeds growing within a sandalwood forest? At this, he attained sudden enlightenment.
He attained realization and composed a verse to send to Yuanwu, saying: "Leaving the forest, I have returned once more to the weeds; The celestial net is vast and wide, impossible to escape.
Who would believe that karmic conditions offer no place of refuge? Returning home, I fear not the loud voices of reproach. Yuanwu was greatly pleased.

He took the verse and showed it to the assembly, saying, "Jue has penetrated the depths of Huayan. Later, while residing there, a monk asked: "Regarding the first [Buddha], King of Majestic Sound, and the last..."
"Lou-zhi Buddha—may I inquire, whom did he meet? The Master said, "His home is in the city of Daliang; you ask again for the road to Chang'an.
[The monk] asked, "As for Deshan carrying his commentaries while traveling on foot, what was his intention? The Master said, "To press your eyes until they burst.
[The monk] asked, "How far apart are you and the Master’s realization of the essential principle of the Avatamsaka Sutra? The Master said, "The same."
Their paths do not share the same ruts. It is said: "The Virtuous Mountain of the past and the Master of today. The Master said: "The setting sun goes west;
the water flows east.
Chan Master Wenyuan of Fuyan in Tanzhou was the son of the Yang family in Chengdu Prefecture. A monk asked: "What is samādhi?"
Lin Zhengzhu said, "I have cut off the tongues of everyone in the world. The Master asked, "How should one approach you?

He replied, "To look upon me is to go blind. He ascended the hall and said: "When sitting directly before the sun, all traces of ordinary and holy beings are severed. When letting go with the hand, heaven turns and earth revolves.
It reaches the point where sun and moon intersect, tigers roar and dragons chant; in every head and every object, they are heard by the ear and seen by the eye."

In the Dingyi year of the Shaoxing era, he was appointed as a Palace Attendant (Jishi). He then met Chan Master Dahui at Mingqing Temple, where Dahui was presiding over the opening of the hall. Dahui [descended from the seat...]

Why then, today, have you suffered this defeat? Huì said, "The entire earth is this very Upāsaka Gǎo.
Where do you see him? The Official prepared to respond, but Huì struck him with his palm. The Official said, "I brought this upon myself. He then departed.
Yue Te begged for alms and sat in summer retreat at Mount Jingshan, naming his quarters the "Immovable Pavilion" (Budong Xuan).
Da sui Jingfa’s successor, Master Shitou Zihui of Diaoyu Tai in Hezhou, was a native of that same prefecture. His family had been stone masons for generations. Although...
He was illiterate, yet his mind was devoted to the school of Emptiness (*śūnyatā*), and he constantly sought someone to orally transmit the *Lotus Sūtra* to him; he was able to recite it from memory.

He left his home and joined the community at Dàsúi, where he served by sweeping and sprinkling water. When the temple authorities ordered him to quarry stones from a cliff, the Master did not let go of his hammer and chisel, yet he never ceased reciting the sūtra.
As he worked, Dàsúi called out to him, saying: "Today there is the sound of chipping stone; tomorrow there will be the sound of chipping stone. When birth and death arrive, what will you do?"
"How can this be resolved? The Master was startled. The monk set aside his implements, performed a prostration, and expressed his wish to hear the ultimate truth.

The Master then instructed him to cease reciting the sutras for a time and instead contemplate the kōan concerning Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman. The monk kept this thought in mind at all times. After some time, while he was chipping away at a particularly hard section of rock, he struck it with all his might.
Suddenly, seeing a flash of light, he attained sudden enlightenment. He rushed to the abbot’s quarters, prostrated himself, and presented his realization.
The verse says: Having exhausted all effort, there is not a shred of clue. The sparks fly apart; they were originally right here.

"The wife is precisely the foot of the Demon King; Zhaozhou’s handleless iron broom sweeps away the dust and smoke until all is empty and desolate.
Suikězhī subsequently conferred upon him the monastic robes. Because he attained enlightenment by striking a stone, he was known as "Returning to Stone" (Huishítóu).
He ascended the hall and said: "Studying the Way through Zen meditation is much like calling out for thirst from the bottom of a well; one simply does not realize that it is blocked."

The ears are blocked and the eyes are covered; there is no time to avoid it. Furthermore, as for walking, standing, sitting, and lying down throughout the twelve periods of the day, or moving about and performing actions—who is it that causes these to be done?

Only then will you know that this old man has entered into a solemn covenant with you regarding the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.

Chan Master Husheng Yuchou Jujing of Tongchuan Prefecture was the son of the Yang family of Chengdu.

"Do not linger by the cold crag; the grass grows green. Sitting amidst white clouds, the essence of the school is not marvelous.

The Master said, "Take care," and departed. He went to reside at Dongyan (East Rock). Ascending the hall, he said: "The moon gives birth to one [day]. Having newly settled at East Rock, my sorrow and solitude increase.

The dusty paths of the world have many twists and turns; in the granaries and storehouses, there is not a single grain. With the cliff as my companion and the spring as my mate, a brisk, clear breeze comes into the room.

Tear drops. Do not say that people of the world merely guard empty cliffs; there are also those who strike the western wall from the eastern hedge.

The Master said, "A nimble and sharp monk requires only a single spark. [The student] asked, "From antiquity to the present, when it comes to being born together and dying together, what then?"
The Master said, "A house-thief is difficult to guard against. The monk said, "Today this student has gone out for a small matter and encountered a great one.
The Master then struck him and said, "It must be I, the old monk, who strikes you before it is right. The monk bowed; the Master said, "Be careful not to feign clarity."
Chan Master Shiyuan Ku’gan of Liangshan in Changde Prefecture was the son of the Lu family of Hezhou.
While presiding over the assembly, he raised the koan of Yangqi’s “Three-Legged Donkey” and addressed the congregation, saying: "To heat the broth, nothing is better than extinguishing the fire."

The Way: whenever there are words or phrases, you must resolve each and every one back to yourself. But how so?

To wash and rinse—this too must be let go; it cannot be grasped. This is also a sickness. Furthermore, there are those who instead seek understanding in some minor detail of the words.
If one understands in such a manner, this sickness is the most difficult to cure. Therefore, his words possess a place of subtle skill;

only then can it be fully realized. It is not only that Chan practitioners cannot understand this, but throughout the world today...
Within the monastic communities, those who have realized the Way to transcend the world and benefit humanity are few.
If you wish to realize it, you must look lightly beyond the limit of Vipaśyin Buddha, back to the time before the empty kalpa. Seize it and act; press down and turn.

Head. Is there anyone like this today? If there is, come forth and speak. If not, listen further to this verse:

The water flowing down the ravine is far too busy. Who among the elders of Hunan understands this? The traveler must go even further.

Nanxiu Daozhe of Jianmen was a man of profound integrity. Since his realization through a single phrase under Dashi, he had served with unwearied diligence.

Mojiang Shangshu, whose courtesy name was Shaoxu, was of a family lineage from Fennings in Yuzhang.

He then ordered the drum to be beaten and ascended the seat, where he recited this verse: "The county magistrate’s summons does not allow for even a moment’s pause; How can it compare to the long-past events, which remain perfectly clear?"
"Formerly there was a song of non-arising; now, fortunately, the melody has been perfected. Having said this, he passed away.

Unable to carry on the lineage, he willingly cast himself aside as base. To break through walls and climb over fences—what a lack of true manhood! I venture to ask the great assembly:

Kong further asked, "What else did he pierce? The Master said, "To carry the stolen goods while crying out for injustice. [Kong] asked, "What is 'scraping the dust off the fur'?

Entering Penglai Island—this too is a matter of no concern. Treading upon a scale-weight as hard as iron—this also is a matter of no concern.
