He returned after a day. One day, [Wumen] raised the phrase: "Not mind, not Buddha, not thing. Suddenly, he attained clear and immediate enlightenment.
He offered this verse: "Not mind, not Buddha, nor yet a thing; Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, the mountain looms high. In the midst of the brilliant sun’s shadow, he turns his body upside down;
The wild fox leaps into the golden-haired lion’s den. Wu’an approved of it and immediately sent a letter with the verse to present to the Buddha (Foguo Yuanwu).
Zhaozhou Hai replied, "This matter cannot be exhausted by paper or brush. Layman, if you can pass me, you shall have something to hear.
He then went back to Huqiu. Zhaozhou Hai met him and said, "Your understanding, Layman, is sufficient only to enter the realm of the Buddhas."
"You have not yet even entered the realm of Māra," said Baizhang. The official continued his prostrations without ceasing. Baizhang maintained a solemn expression and said, "Why do you not say:
'The golden-haired lion leaps into the wild fox's den'? Thereupon, the official attained a profound realization.
Chan Master Biefeng Baoyin of Jing Mountain in Lin’an, a successor in the Huazang lineage, was the son of the Li family of Jiazhou.

From his youth, he mastered the Six Classics but grew weary of worldly affairs; he subsequently received the tonsure under Qing-su of De-shan. After receiving full ordination, he studied the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
Xin had exhausted his explanations and abandoned his reliance on Mimi at Zhongfeng. One day, Mimi raised a case:

A monk asked Yantou, "What is it like when arising and ceasing do not cease? Yantou shouted, "Who is it that arises and ceases? At this, the Master attained awakening and nodded his head in confirmation.
When Yuanwu returned to Zhaojue, Zhuanfeng Yin sent the Master to visit him. Consequently, he entered the room with the assembly.
Yuanwu asked, "How did the sages of antiquity receive people? The Master held up his fist. Yuanwu said, "That is what I, this old monk, use.
What is it that the sages of antiquity use? The Master struck him with his fist. Yuanwu also raised his fist and crossed them; they both laughed heartily.
He stopped there. Later, he went to Mount Jing to visit Dahui. Dahui asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Western Sichuan.
Dahui said, "Before you even left the Jianmen Pass, I would have given you thirty blows of the staff! The Master said, "It was not appropriate for me to trouble the Master."
Hui was delighted and swept his quarters to welcome him. When Hui moved southward, the Master returned west. He presided over several monasteries in succession.
Later, he crossed the gorges again and resided at Baoning, Jinnshan, Xuedou, and Jingshan. Opening the hall and ascending the seat, he said:
"When the World-Honored One first attained perfect enlightenment, he turned the Dharma wheel of the Four Noble Truths in the Deer Park. The bhikṣu Kauṇḍinya was the first to realize it."
Later, when Chan Master Zhenjing first resided at Dongshan, he remarked: "Today, within the cave of Xin'feng, I am merely turning this staff.
He then held up his staff, placed it to his left side, and asked: "Is there anyone here who attained enlightenment from the very beginning?
If not, a man of spirit naturally possesses the will to soar toward the heavens; do not walk where the Tathāgata has already trodden. He then let out a shout.
"Strike the seat! [The Master] said. "If it were an *abbot* (yinzhang), it would not be so.
Today, within the Phoenix Mountains, there is no leisure to turn the Dharma wheel of the Four Noble Truths, nor is there the strength to turn this staff.
I only instruct all you people to walk with slow steps and speak in low voices. Why? If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata."

Zhengfalu Xuan Chan Master was the son of the Xu family of Jiading. He left home to become a monk and received full ordination. Having studied under Anmin, he attained the essential instructions of the Dharma. In the Gengwu year of the Jiading era, by imperial decree, he resided at Mount Jing.

Monks from far and near flocked to him like spokes converging on a hub. Xuan felt compassion for those who had traveled great distances, their feet blistered with the journey. He [instructed them] until they reached the ultimate...

On that day, he had no place to eat or rest. Furthermore, above the Double Creek (Shuangxi), he constructed one hundred rooms as a reception hall to provide for those whom he could not otherwise reach.
Emperor Ningzong of the Song dynasty once bestowed upon him the two large characters "Huacheng" (Transformation City) and granted him the title "Furi" (Buddha Sun).
Létán Míng’s dharma heir was Chan Master Wúwéi Suì’ān Shǒuyuán of Hànzhōu, a native of the local Shì clan. At the age of thirteen, he suffered from blindness in his eyes;

he subsequently went to rely upon Chan Master Huìmù Néng of Xīchán Monastery, where he received full ordination. Later, he crossed the gorges and arrived at Bǎofēng, where he encountered the Master ascending the hall for a discourse.
Jingyue said: "The single moon universally appears in all waters; all the moons in the waters are encompassed by the single moon.
Upon hearing this, the Master attained clear realization. Later, when he ascended the hall, he said: "To unify the myriad with the one: the single moon universally appears in all waters."
The myriad returns to the One; all waters and moons are encompassed within the single moon. When extended, it pervades and encompasses the Dharma-realm;
when withdrawn, not even a hair’s breadth remains. Although these modes of withdrawal and extension follow different paths, this matter fundamentally possesses no divergent essence.
Only by being able to fix a single eye upon the root source can one see that the Buddhas of the three periods and the patriarchs of successive generations have all emerged from this.
Within this, there is manifestation. All the sūtras of the Tripitaka and the twelve divisions of the canon flow forth entirely from within this.

Heaven and earth, the sun and moon, and the myriad phenomena of the universe are all established from within this. The three realms, the nine stages, the seven destinies, and the four modes of birth all emerge and submerge within this.
The hundreds of thousands of dharma-gates and immeasurable wondrous meanings—even the worldly crafts—[all arise from here].
Those skilled in arts and crafts all manifested these activities in their conduct. Thus, when the World-Honored One held up a flower, Kāśyapa immediately smiled;
when Bodhidharma faced the wall, the Second Patriarch thereby attained peace of mind. When the peach blossoms bloomed in full splendor, Lingyun’s doubts were completely purified.
When the bamboo was struck and made a sound, Xiangyan suddenly forgot all that he knew.

This extends to Panshan awakening to the Way at a meat counter, and Maitreya receiving people in a fish market. Truly, it can be said: "In moments of haste and in times of distress, one must always abide by this;
walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, one is within it. Since there is such marvel, there is also such radiance. Since there is such...
It is vast and expansive, and yet it is all-pervasive in this way. Why, then, do you people still have delusion and enlightenment?
Do you wish to know? Fortunately, there is no place where it does not shine; yet, there is still a moment when it is not clear.

Chan Master Nankang-jun Yunju Wanan Desheng, whose posthumous name was Longxiang Gui, was a native of the He clan of Hanzhou. At the age of twenty, he received full ordination and studied the exegesis of the scriptures;
after some time, however, he abandoned that path. He went to visit Chan Master Wenshu Dao and inquired about the essential points of the Buddha-dharma. Wenshu showed him a verse:
[Zhaozhou] said: "The Khitans broke the Persian camp and seized a precious pearl, which they sold in the village.

At the crossroads, a destitute beggar has a pouch of elegance hanging from his waist. As the Master was about to respond, Xuefeng Shu said, "Do not err. The Master withdrew to reflect for three years before finally grasping the essential meaning.
He went to see Foxing, but their spiritual resonance did not meet; he then traveled to Min Province and went to visit Gushan, whereupon—
Question: "The National Teacher did not step over the stone gate—what is the meaning of this? Zhuan’an responded with a shout, saying, "Idle talk.
The Master immediately attained realization. Later, while residing there, a monk asked: "I do not ask about 'Zhengzhen not borrowing' and 'transcending the three realms.'"
"What is the true person of no station? The Master said, "Rich and noble when heard; poor and destitute when seen.
[The monk] said, "Lift your head and you must cover your ears; tilt your palm and you immediately turn over. The Master said, "Where is the true person of no station?
[The monk] said, "O Great Master, you do not even recognize the pivot of the teaching. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows!"

Chan Master Yunju Puyun Ziyuan, a dharma successor of Yungju Wuzu, was the son of the Yang family of Mianzhou. At the age of nineteen, he passed the scriptural examinations and received full ordination.
He remained in the monastic garden for five years before crossing the pass and traveling south. There, he visited various eminent masters in succession and finally arrived at...
Longmen. One day, while in the corridors, he had an awakening upon seeing a painting of a foreigner. That night, he reported this to Gao’an. Gao’an cited a verse by Fayan:
“A sable-fur hat upon the head, a horned awl suspended at the waist; his speech does not allow others to understand—it must be translated by one who knows him.
He then held up a torch and showed it to him, saying, “I have finished translating it for you. Thereupon, the Great Dharma...
Mingliao presented a verse, saying: "The sounds and languages of foreign lands are inexhaustible; Beneath Qiyun Pavilion, they are all at once understood.
The gateway of the mouth is vast and boundless; It swallows whole the thorny chestnut of Yangqi.
Yuan'an sent Master Yiyu to see Foyan. Foyan said to him, "My Way shall go East. He ascended the hall and cited a monk’s question to Yunmen: "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya?"
The Gate says: "Hiding one's body within the Northern Dipper. The Master said: "North, south, east, and west—ten thousand, ten thousand, a thousand;
Heaven and earth, above and below—both are boundless. Meeting and seeing one another, we laugh 'he-he'; Folding fingers and raising the head, the moon is in the midst of the sky."
Chengdu Prefecture Chan Master Xiangxi Jixiu, the Dharma heir of Huanglong Zhong, ascended the hall. He raised the public case of Mazu’s illness and said:
"When the two wheels are raised, smoke and dust arise; swift as lightning and racing like stars—how could one stop them? Before one's eyes, coming and going are unimpeded."
The pivot: the true command turns completely, with no distinction between inner and outer; the spirit of the man naturally pierces the heavens.
"I am I, and you are you. [This was said by] Lia of Xichan, the Dharma heir of [Fengxue] Yan.
The second-generation Chan Master Xishou of Xichan Monastery in Suining Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Autumn light is already half-way through; the heat is gradually fading.
Wild geese cross the void, piercing the azure sky like water; monkeys hang from the trees, shaking off the jade dew like pearls.
Even if one were to encounter such a clear opportunity, one would still not avoid mistaking a tortoise for a turtle. But tell me, how do you respond to the season?"
A single phrase is set aside. How would you say it? "The wild colors merge with the moon over the Three Islands; the stream’s radiance divides the autumn of the Five Lakes.
This is from Daomiao Guo, a Dharma heir.
Chan Master Zonglian of Yuyuan Qionggu in Jingmen Commandery was the son of the Dong family of Hezhou. Upon ascending the hall, after the question-and-answer session had concluded, he said:

"When a patch-robed monk stands before the assembly of devas and humans, engaging in one question and one answer, one seizing and one releasing, one contracting and one expanding, one pressing forward and one thrusting back—this must be done with the eyes of a vajra; otherwise, it is merely reciting words."
We belong to the same lineage, yet you went to West Qin while I went to East Lu; within the ancestral school, this matter is of no benefit at all.
It does not lie in speech, nor does it lie in silence; it is not obstructed by speech, nor is it obstructed by silence.

When the ancients offered a single word or half a phrase, they were simply making known the weapons of the state, employing them only when there was no other choice. Whether spoken horizontally or vertically...
It is said that one need only control the point where people enter; the reality does not reside in words and phrases.
People of the present day cannot penetrate to the root source through a direct path; they take mere language and written characters to be the ultimate Way.
They pass one phrase on and receive another, calling this "the Way of Chan," or "ascending and descending," or "bodhi and nirvana," or "the Patriarch."

The Master’s true core is exactly like "a Cao monk appearing in Zhengzhou. Among the assemblies of the ancestral masters from of old, there have often been those who took traveling on pilgrimage as their primary task;
as soon as they encountered a point of doubt, they would resolve it before the assembly.

Through a single phrase, they attained clear realization of the Truth, establishing the direct, untransmitted school of the Buddhas and Patriarchs for the sake of all sentient beings until the end of time.
Attaining and realizing together is still not yet the place of ultimate rest; how could it be merely opening one's lips to speak in foreign tongues or Hanese?

Stonehead Hui returned as the dharma heir of Chan Master Nankang Jun Yunju Peng’an Dehui, whose secular surname was He and who was a native of Chongqing Prefecture. Once, he ascended the hall and gave this discourse: [He] raised [the following case]:
The teaching points to the Middle Way: "If you see that all marks are non-marks, then you see the Tathāgata. What is the principle of these "non-marks"?
Running on pretense, feigning shame, casting a sidelong glance: the bamboo gate is half-closed, with a branch of blossoms hanging halfway down.
*Jinjiang Chandelu*, Scroll Seven.
*Jinjiang Chandelu*, Scroll Eight.
Compiled by Zhaojue Zhangxue Tongzui.
Edited by Hu Shengyou of Huan’an in Xiangshui;
the eighteenth-generation successor of Dajian (Huineng) in the lineage of Donglin Yan.
Chan Master Fayuan of Ba’en in Tingzhou was a native of Guozhou. On ascending the hall, he cited the karmic occasion of Juzhi pointing his finger and said:
"A beautiful woman rises from sleep too lazy to comb her hair; she takes up a golden hairpin and inserts it, and that is enough.
Generally speaking, it is because her natural bone and flesh are so fine that she is elegant even without applying rouge and powder."
Chan Master Zhizhe Yu’an Zhenci of Wuzhou was the son of the Li family of Tongchuan. Initially, he left home life under the guidance of Chengdu Zhengfa Temple.

After receiving full ordination, he traveled among lecture halls and listened to discourses on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*. Upon reaching the passage: "The four great elements are each separate; where, then, does this deluded body now reside?
Ultimately it has no substance and is truly identical to an illusion," he attained a realization. He then composed [the following]:
The verse says: A single bright pearl is within me; when touched or moved, it emits light that shakes the earth.
When presented to various lecturers, none were able to understand it. Returning home, he presented it to his own teacher, who then questioned him with the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature.
The teacher said, "Though there be hundreds of thousands of millions of koans, they do not go beyond this verse. His teacher, [thereby...]
[The master] considered this disrespectful and shouted at him to leave. The Master then traveled south and took up residence at Yuan Tong on Mount Lu.

At that time, Wan’an was serving as the West Hall Attendant. When he entered the room for the assembly, he raised the following kōan: "A monk asked Yunmen, 'When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what then? Yunmen said, 'The Buddha is also dust.
As soon as [Wan’an] uttered these words, the Master let out a shout and pointed to his own chest, saying, "The Buddha is also dust! The Master [then departed].
Again, he spoke in verse: "Shaking off the dust, one sees the Buddha; the Buddha, too, is but dust. Question resolved, answer resolved—turning over directly beneath one's feet.
I urge you to drink yet another cup of wine; once you have passed the Yang Pass to the west, there will be no old friend remaining. He further spoke a verse on the Samādhi of Dust-to-Dust:
Rice in the bowl, water in the bucket; a discerning jewel-bearing *kūṇapa* sits at the bottom of the abyss. One speck of dust runs atop Mount Sumeru;
the clear-eyed Persian laughs and snaps his fingers. He laughs and snaps his fingers: a pure breeze rises upon the coral branches.
Wanshan deeply approved of this.
Chan Master Zhaojue Shaoyuan ascended the hall and said: A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall?
Yunmen replied, "The golden wind reveals its essence. The Master said: To understand the mechanism of the trap for tigers, one must be a patch-robed monk of true substance.
Great Master Yunmen possessed a samādhi that transcends the common herd; he struck the joints and knocked at the gates within a flash of lightning.
He extends a single hand to untie the glue and remove the bonds for others, pulling out the wedges and extracting the nails—a truly skilled hand indeed.
Yet, if one examines this closely, it is much like providing a ladder to a thief. Zhaojue is not like this.

Suppose a monk were to ask, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall? He would simply answer him: "The setting clouds fly alongside the solitary wild goose; the autumn waters join with..."

"The vast sky is of one color. Now tell me: is this the same as Yunmen, or is it different? He further said: "Cease, cease! There is no need to speak; my Dharma is subtle and inconceivable. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Melting vases, plates, hairpins, and bracelets into a single gold; churning butter, curd, and clarified butter into a single flavor.
Thus, the way of guest and host is harmonized, and inner and outer are at peace. The five ranks of ruler and subject are all penetrated. Four...
He selected a single string of beads as his seed-material. To let them go is like a fine drizzle falling and the autumn wind blowing;
to hold them fast is to be utterly empty—dare anyone gaze upon this with a direct eye? Tell me: is it better to let go for the sake of others, or is it better to hold fast for the sake of others?
He spoke again: "Casually, it is just like the arrival of the autumn wind; unintentionally cooling others, yet people cool themselves."
Zhang Shi, whose courtesy name was Jingfu, served repeatedly as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel. He once sought instruction from Daoyan, who said: "If you see it, you see it immediately;
if you deliberate upon it, you have already gone astray. Furthermore, what then? Yan said: "It is still asking whether one knows it exists. Shi asked:
"What is the case when one actually knows it? Yan said: "Hearing sounds and seeing forms is exactly as usual. At these words, Shi attained sudden enlightenment.

He then left behind a verse, saying: "Hearing sounds and seeing forms are just as they always were; If one examines them with maturity, the principle of the refined and the coarse reveals itself naturally.

It is like the void containing the azure expanse; Not even a single hair’s breadth of excess exists. After he had spoken thus, his illness subsequently grew critical. Ding Sǒu sought his instruction, and Zhāo Chì said:

"To cast off the private desires of human nature is like a cicada shedding its shell; to harmonize with the subtle wonder of the heavenly principle is like the melting of spring. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
Zhi Shi spent his life immersing himself in the classics and histories, always aspiring to emulate the ancient sages and worthies.
He authored works such as commentaries on the Analects and Mencius, as well as treatises on the Supreme Ultimate (*Tàijí*). Scholars knew him as Master Nanxuan.
Xichan Xu, a Dharma heir of Nanjianzhou Jianmen Anfen Anzhu, had previously studied under Muguan at Anguo Temple. Later, he relied upon Lan’an, yet had not yet attained profound realization.
He took his leave to visit Daie of Jing Mountain; while traveling along the riverbank, he gazed up in admiration at the imperial palace.
Hearing the Street Official shout, "The Minister is coming," he was suddenly and completely enlightened. He composed a verse, saying: "For many years this matter has hung upon my breast;
I have questioned all quarters, yet my eyes remained unopened. Now, liver and gall are both rent asunder:

A voice cries out, 'The Minister comes upon the river! He then went directly back to Xichan. Lan’an welcomed him and bestowed upon him the *kāṣāya*. From that time on, he no longer followed formal regulations.
He resided later at Jianmen in a thatched hut, where his transformative influence spread throughout the regions south of the mountains. Students followed him;
the gāthās and hymns he composed were produced with the speed of a flowing hand, totaling more than a thousand pieces, which became widely circulated in the world.

Dashi Ziju Chan Master of Decheng Prefecture was a dharma successor of Dayue Xingfa; he was a native of Tongchuan. Entering the hall for formal instruction, he said: "When seeing the seeing, the seeing is not the seeing.
Seeing is already detached from seeing; seeing cannot reach it. He then gave a shout and said: "The whale swallows the ocean until it is empty, revealing..."
"Corals. Suddenly, if a monk were to come forth from among the assembly and say, "Elder, cease your drowsy talk," I would grant that he possesses a single eye.
Entering the hall, he held his staff crosswise and said: "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven;
seven, six, five, four, three, two, one. Counting them forward and backward in succession, until the day of the future reaches its end."
"Because of the seven, one is established; because of the one, the seven perish. Treading through the vast void, even the iron ox breaks into a sweat.
Breath ceases and no trace remains. Throwing down his staff, he said, "You must further let go of this very thing; only then will the work of study be complete."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Sometimes one takes away the person but not the environment; the staff wanders freely in all directions.
Sometimes one takes away the environment but not the person; this mountain monk acts in a topsy-turvy manner. Sometimes both person and environment are taken away."
The staff and this mountain monk erase our traces and swallow our voices. Sometimes, both person and environment are not seized. (He plants the staff and says:
"Accompanying me for a thousand miles, carrying you across ten thousand mountains. What is it like when one suddenly runs into Great Master Linji? (He shouts:
"If the seal of the mind-ground is not yet understood, it is difficult to penetrate the barrier of the Patriarch."

Master Juji (Juguang), the Dharma heir of Emperor Shizong, was the Chan Master Beijian Jujian of Lin’an. He was the son of the Long family from Tongzhou. He received full ordination at Guangfu Monastery in his native district.
He studied under Biefeng Tudu, remaining silent and secluded while seeking thorough investigation. One day, upon reading the records of Wan’an, he attained realization. He then went to study further.
The Buddha illuminated his capacity and they were in accord. From then on, he visited the Master’s gate for fifty years. He traveled to Jiangxi to seek out Zhongwen at Luhun;
when they engaged in discussion, Zhongwen marveled greatly at him. He subsequently bestowed upon him the bamboo pointer (zhubi) that Dahui had used while residing at the Yangyu Hermitage.
The Master was struck by this. After some time, he emerged from seclusion at Ba’en in Tiantai. Later, he moved to Jingci. When he ascended the hall, [the assembly] recognized him.
"Obtain one, and all matters are finished. A monk who has settled his affairs does not recognize a single character.
Even if you act in this way, it still does not merit the "Full Holding up. Where the power of Yu did not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west.
[He] ascended the hall and, citing the case of Master Mi and Dongshan at a bakery: Master Mi drew a circle on the ground and said to Dongshan, "Take this away. Dongshan said:
[The Master] held it up. Later, Master Baoning Yong said, "Not only could those two not lift it;
no one in the entire world could lift it. Beigan dared to say: "Baoning’s resources were exhausted and his strength spent.
He ascended the hall and, citing Zhaozhou entering the monks' hall and shouting, "Thief! Thief!", he seized a monk upon seeing him and said, "The thief is right here! The monk...
[The monk] said, "It is not I. Zhou said, "It is indeed so, yet you are unwilling to accept it. The Master said, "Zhaozhou’s way of gathering was too lax;
his letting go was too hasty. Jingci, however, is not like this: 'A house-thief is difficult to guard against; the family wealth will surely be lost.
Striking the meditation staff, he said, 'One may err in seizing, but one must not err in releasing. He passed away in the spring of the *Chunyou* *Bingwu* year.
He wrote a verse that said: "On the first day of the fourth month, take care. When the appointed time arrived, he passed away while dozing.
It is not known who his dharma heir was.

A monk from Shu named Fangbian came to visit the Sixth Patriarch and remarked, "I am skilled at sculpting. The Patriarch looked sternly at him and said, "Try sculpting me then. Fangbian did not understand.

The Master said, "Excellent. He then had a statue of the Patriarch fashioned, seven feet in height, executed with exquisite skill. Upon seeing it, the Patriarch asked, "Are you skilled at sculpting the Buddha-nature?
[Hui] replied, "I am not skilled at sculpting the Buddha-nature. The Patriarch rewarded him with clothing and other goods; [Hui] expressed his thanks and departed.
Daoliu was a monk from Shu who lived among the assembly. He once lamented that the Buddha-dharma was becoming muddled and corrupted, with divergent views arising like swarms of bees.

He said, "If I can attain genuine insight through the study of Chan, I shall not spare my verbal karma. He then made a vow to prostrate before the stupa of Mazu, doing so for many years without ceasing.
One day, the stupa emitted light, and moved by this, he attained awakening. Subsequently, he traveled extensively throughout the monastic forests to test and verify [the teachings].
The Elder [Tiantai] passed before Mount Xuedou and said, "This old fellow has water dripping from his mouth. When Xuedou heard these words, he seemed somewhat displeased.
Upon meeting Tiantai, Xuedou asked, "Do you not approve of me, Old Monk? Tiantai replied, "Old man, you truly do have water dripping from your mouth.
He then struck him with his sitting mat and departed. The temple steward, feeling indignant, sent someone after him on the road.
Someone struck him, injuring Taiyi’s foot. Taiyi said, "This was sent by Xuedou. One day he must break one of his own feet to repay me.
Later, it indeed came to pass as he had said.
A monk asked Zen Master Qin of Renwang in Shu, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Hearing the name is not as good as seeing the face.
The monk asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, “A monkey performing in a bustling marketplace.
The monk asked, “What is the Way? The Master said, “A tiger watching a water mill.”
Chan Master De普 (De-pu) was the son of the Pu family of Mianzhou. Having received the tonsure and full ordination, he mastered the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi* and the *Awakening of Faith*;

throughout the two rivers (Sichuan), none dared to challenge him, earning him the title "Tiger of Doctrine. At that time, Hui-sheng returned from Jiangxi, and Lü Da-fang, who had been appointed as the regional governor of Chengdu, treated him with the etiquette due to a disciple, visiting his quarters day and night.
De-pu secretly listened to their discussions, yet he could not understand a single word of them.
Returning to his room to lie down, he looked at the roof beam and said, "In the past, I was once a lecturer with a great reputation.

Master Lü was universally acclaimed as a man of virtue, yet we held such mutual respect and faith for one another. How could it be that I do not believe this now? He then departed from Shu and traveled to Jinyuan in Jingzhou.
One night, while staying with a monk, Huiguo asked, "In what way do the sutras and treatises contradict the Chan school, such that you, Elder, frequently disparage them?"

It is said that because this involves the conceptualization of emotional states, principles, thoughts, and mental measurements, it cannot by itself give rise to sagehood or lead to the attainment of the Way.
Even those who happen to attain the Way or become sages do so only by relying on these as conditions.

If one does not rely on self-awakening but instead depends solely on the sutras and treatises, then all those who can read, know, see, and understand them would have already realized sagehood and attained the Way. It is only because...
Because dead words constitute the cognitive obscuration (*jñeyāvaraṇa*), the Patriarch came from the West. As it is said in the sutras:

"All sentient beings are originally Buddhas; do you believe this? [The student] replied, "How could I dare not believe the words of the World-Honored One? [The Master] said, "Since you believe this..."
"Why have you come from so far away? He replied, "I have heard that the Chan school possesses a distinctively transmitted Dharma, and for this reason I have come.
Nan said with a smile, "This is not yet faith; it is merely the ability to believe. "Now Master Nanchuan of Jicui has been in the world for some time.

It would be best if you were to see him before it is too late. On that very day, Fupin set out. In the first year of the Xining era, he arrived at Huanglong and asked about Ānanda and Kāśyapa. The world...
"Beyond the transmission of the golden robe, what other Dharma was transmitted? Kāśyapa called out to Ānanda, who responded with "Yes.
Kāśyapa said, "Throw down the banner-pole in front of the gate! What is the meaning of this? Nan said, "When you, Master, left Sichuan, did you ever go to Yūquan?
[The monk] replied, "I went there. Nan asked again, "Did you stay there? He replied, "I departed after one night. Nan said, "A wise man."
"At the Dharma Hall, when did it ever matter whether General Guan offered incense or formed a karmic connection? Puhui remained silent and proceeded to address the previous question.
Nan bowed his head. Puhui hurried out and said in great astonishment, "The tiger of righteousness from the two rivers cannot withstand a single spit from this old man!"
Chan Master Daohui of Ba’en in Tongchuan once sent a letter with Baofu to Wang, the Grand Marshal of Quanzhou.
When the Marshal asked, "Has the Abbot of Zhangnan been acting as a teacher for others recently? the Master replied, "If one says he has been acting as a teacher for others..."
He then bowed to the Venerable Master. [The Master] said, "If you say you do not teach people, then you must also bow to the Grand Marshal.
The Marshal said, "Speak a single phrase; wait until the iron ox can chew grass and the wooden horse can inhale smoke. The Master said, "I am sparing my mouth for eating rice.

After a long silence, the Marshal asked again, "Does the donkey come, or does the horse come? The Master said, "Donkey and horse do not share the same path. The Marshal said, "How did you manage to arrive?"
At this point, the Master said, "Thank you, Grand Marshal, for grasping the meaning of the words.
Lord Fan of Shu sent off Chan Master Yuanwu on his pilgrimage, saying:
"When observing water, do not observe the water in a stagnant pool; the fish and turtles in a stagnant pool are base. When climbing a mountain, do not climb a gradual slope."

Mountains: when mountains stretch out in succession, the vegetation becomes sparse. To observe water, one must observe the vastness of the ocean; to climb a mountain, one must ascend the heights of Mount Tai.
What is attained will not be shallow, and what is seen will be lofty. Though all effort may be exhausted, it is not in vain. Fortunately, there is a place in the South for selecting Buddhas;
you should strive to exhaust the wondrous principles therein. In years to come, having become a vessel of the Way, you shall restore the collapsed order and not fail the manhood entrusted to you.
The child’s resolve to leave the household life—O great man, do not hesitate! How could one sacrifice one's life for the sake of empty fame? In a hundred years, one’s allotted time is not much;
do not let the passing moments stealthily add to your years. Moreover, Chengdu is a land of great splendor; you have stopped here only because of delusions regarding flowers and wine.
My teacher is fortunately one who has left the household life; would you be willing to follow the base and sink into oblivion together with them? I...
Master, you fortunately possess the ambition of a rainbow; why do you hesitate and wallow in the mud?
Have you not seen that a fish capable of swallowing a boat does not hide in shallow streams, nor does a tree with a trunk thick enough to embrace grow on Mount Danqiu?

When the Great Peng spreads its wings, it covers ninety thousand li—how can it be compared to a sand gull flying along a spring shore? Why not swiftly mount a thousand-li steed? Do not emulate the *jiaoliao* bird that clings to a single branch.
Even if one could expound upon a thousand sutras and treatises, it would still fall into the second level of the Chan school’s mechanism. White clouds have always clung to the high terrace;
shrouding at dusk and enveloping at dawn, they do not open for even a moment. Yet, to comfort the hopes of the common people for rain, he casually emerges from the mountains as before.
Furthermore, have you not seen? In the Jing Mountains there is jade called *juéyáo*; until a skilled craftsman encounters it, it remains amidst the weeds. When...
If at that time he had not left Jingzhou, how could the price of his "linked cities" have been so much higher?
Wuxin Guangdao, a native of Zizhou, first traveled abroad and asked Master Yungai Zhi, "What was the intent behind Xinghua’s striking of the *vīnāya*?
Zhi descended from his meditation seat, extended both hands, and stuck out his tongue to show him. Guangdao struck him once.
Guang struck his sitting mat once. Zhiyun said, "This is turned by the power of the wind. He then asked the Venerable Shishuang Lin, "What is your intention?
Lin said, "How is it with your mind? Guang also struck his sitting mat once. Lin said, "A fine sitting mat!
It is only that you do not know where it lands. He then asked Zhenjing, "What is your intention? Jing said, "How is it with your mind? Guang also struck his sitting mat once.
Jingyun said, "If he strikes you, strike back. He attained great enlightenment through this. Jingyin composed a verse, saying:
"If a man of character does not sever [delusion] himself, Xinghua acts as a thoroughgoing man for others' sake. Henceforth his own eyes shall open by themselves;
He was caned, fined, and expelled from the monastery."
The śramaṇa Yizhong of Hanzhong was a senior elder who sought teachers and pursued the Way, selecting the Buddha through Zen meditation.
Carrying his tools like dry wood, he performed his play as the occasion arose. Yet, while that play occurred for but a moment, its merit has benefited all for a thousand ages.
Thereupon, he changed the old regulations. Yet the people of Ying remained bewildered; they followed the instruments and sought the opportunity, for transformation and adaptation depend upon oneself.
How could one allow the line and square to constrain a grand design, or be limited by the compass and ruler? This is what is meant by saying that the "Son" (the literal text) cannot be taught;
what can be taught is but the dregs of language. It is not the ultimate subtlety of the mind; it is the ultimately subtle mind itself.
It resides within me; it does not reside in words or language. Even if one were to receive a secret transmission from an enlightened master, it would not equal the self-attainment of the mind.
Therefore it is said: "Attained in the mind, it is manifested in the hand"—both are the wondrous functioning of the numinous mind-dharma.
Thus, when it comes to threshing wheat, it serves as a millstone; when one wishes to refine rice, it serves as a roller; when one wishes to obtain flour, it serves as a sieve;
and when one wishes to remove the husks, it serves as a fan. Its overall structure and principles are entirely governed by a single crank.
Once the mechanism is set in motion, everything turns of its own accord without being pushed, simply because of the water. As soon as a single wave...
It moves: the preceding wave and the succeeding wave respond to one another in an endless succession because of the millstone.
As soon as a single wheel is raised, the large wheels and small wheels revolve one after another without end. Thus, the upper and lower parts correspond, and the high and low work together;
this wondrous function emerges spontaneously. Therefore, it does not depend on what human effort can achieve, yet its marvelous excellence is beyond compare.

Observing that which is profound beyond the profound, they then rotate to the left and turn to the right; moving vertically and coming horizontally, they strike and touch one another, producing the great sound of the Dharma.
This sound expounds suffering, emptiness, impermanence, non-self, and the various *pāramitās*. Those who hear it hear its mind;
those who see it see its nature. Even through smelling, tasting, and sensory cognition, all obtain the bliss of *dharmaprīti* and the joy of *dhyāna*.

Furthermore, how could the rice, flour, and all other necessary provisions provided for the kitchen of Fragrant Accumulation (Gandhavyuha) serve as two kinds of meals to satiate the assembly of meditators who come and go to select the Buddha?
Ziqing, the Tripitaka Master, was a native of Shu and was renowned throughout the monastic communities. He traveled extensively to visit great masters such as Zhenru, Haitang, and Pujo;
he journeyed to Mount Lu and entered the capital, where he met Chan Master Fayun Yuancong and traveled together with Master Xiu.
Upon arriving at Fayun Monastery, Xiu was permitted to enter the hall. Because the reputation of the attendant Qing had reached Yuantong, Tong said, "For now, have him lodge elsewhere;
once a unit here becomes vacant, he shall immediately be allowed to enter the hall. While Qing was staying at Zhihai, he happened to fall ill.
Xiu wished to go and inquire after his ailment, but there were no leave passes available at the mountain gate. He therefore slipped out secretly to see Qing at Zhihai. When Qing saw him...

He wrote a letter to Yuan Tong stating that Daoxiu had transgressed the rules in his conduct. Upon receiving the letter, Yuan Tong learned of the matter and, during the night assembly, he scolded him severely, saying:

"This man is truly a petty person. Because of their shared commitment to the Way and righteousness, he risked being expelled from the monastery to come and inquire after your illness, yet you instead report this to the authorities.
How could such an act be the deed of an upright man or a true scholar? When Qing heard this, he immediately ceased [his activities], and the entire monastic community spoke of it in this way.
Qing suffered a stroke while traveling to Yuan Tong and passed away.
The Elder Bai of Mount Emei once remarked, "The local people say Xuedou has over a hundred verses, yet their phrasing and meaning do not particularly stand out from others.
How is it that he has gained such a great reputation in the world? He then composed a thousand verses, adding ten more to [Xuedou's] number.

Twice as excellent. Having compiled this collection myself, I harbored the vain hope that my fame might one day surpass that of Xuedou. Everywhere I went, I sought someone who could appreciate my work.

There was a master of Mount Dahe who had traveled extensively to visit the eminent and realized elders of the age; he had received the Dharma from Chan Master Fachang Yu and emerged into the world to reside at Dahe, where he was known as the "Mountain Master.
His spirit overwhelmed all quarters, and he did not grant his approval lightly. Bai carried [the manuscript] with him...
He composed this verse and went to visit [Dahe], seeking the discernment of a single word so as to gain the trust of future students. Upon seeing it, Dahe spat and said:

"This verse is like a person suffering from the stench of a crow; standing against the wind, its odor cannot be smelled. From that time on, Bai did not dare to appear in public as if he were a human being.
Later, when Huang鲁直 (Huang Tingjian) heard of this, he went to Daci Temple in Chengdu and wrote these words in large characters upon the wall.
It is said: "The Elder Bai of Emei composed a collection of a thousand verses. Dahui once remarked: 'A crow standing against the wind [smells its own] stench.

Those who claim self-awakening without a teacher exhaust their heart's blood, thinking they will surpass others; yet upon meeting a person of true wisdom, they find themselves in a state of total confusion.
It is solely because of arrogance that they fall into this pitfall. Students of the Way, do not harbor such thoughts."
His foul odor lingers in all directions.
He was the nineteenth-generation descendant under Dajian [Huangbo] and the dharma heir of Tiantong Jie.
Chan Master Pò'ān Zuǎn of Wòlóngshān in Kuízhōu was the son of the Wáng family of Guǎng'ānzhōu.
Initially, he studied under Mìmàn and attained realization upon hearing his discourse during a formal assembly. Later, when Mì lived at Língyǐn, he appointed the Master to share the seat with him.
A practitioner seeking instruction asked, "What should one do when a monkey cannot be caught? The Master replied, "Why use a net to catch it? It is like the wind."
He blew upon the water, and patterns naturally formed. Later, after taking his seat for the assembly, he ascended the hall and said: "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing.
Unable to restrain himself, he acted as a means of liberation for everyone; picking up his staff and striking once, he said: "The flowing water silently erodes the rocks by the stream;
I urge people to eliminate the difficulty of right and wrong."
Chan Master Cao Yuan Sheng of Jianfu Monastery in Raoyang was a native of Nanjian. He composed this verse on Lingyun Rock: Clouds depart and clouds arrive, yet they have no intention;
Clouds come and clouds go, likewise without mind. When existence and non-existence are cut off, where is the "spiritual" (ling)?
A solitary peak stands abruptly, its greenness reaching to the present day.
The twentieth-generation successor of Dajian (Da Jian),
Chan Master Wuzhun Shifan of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture,
was a descendant of the Yong clan of Jianzhou. He entered the monastic order at the age of nine.
He requested instruction from an elder master on the method of sitting meditation (*zazen*). The elder asked, "What is Zen? Who is it that sits? The Master investigated this day and night.
One day, while going to the toilet, he attained realization regarding these words. He went to visit Fozhao of Yewang Temple. Fozhao asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Jianzhou.
Fozhao said, "Have you brought your sword with you? At these words, the Master let out a shout. Fozhao smiled.
It is said: "This is Wutouzi; he acts in a disorderly manner. When [Dongshan] arrived at Lingyin, Pō'ān was serving as the First Seat (Chief Seat).

They traveled together to Shishun An, where a practitioner requested instruction on the "Monkey Child" koan. At the side, the Master attained great enlightenment. Initially, he resided at Qingyuan in Mingzhou;
later, he received an imperial decree to reside at Jingshan. Entering the hall, he said: "At Vulture Peak they pointed to the moon; at Caoxi they spoke of the moon. One after another..."
This has been handed down through successive generations. It is like proving that a tortoise is an eel. Elder Fan usually had a mouth hanging on his wall that never moved;
today, having needlessly entered this practitioner’s door, with matters come to such a pass, he can do nothing but shake things out from east to west.
He cannot help but pick up his many years’ worth of records and point out some of the places where others have been deceived. Thus he speaks:
It seems as though you people simply require Guo Da, Li Er, Deng Si, and Zhang San to know that it is cold in the spring and hot in the autumn in Jiangnan and the Two Zhe regions.
Nevertheless, the Yellow River clears itself but once every three thousand years. [Ascending the hall:
If one were to discuss this matter, it is truly simple and easy to understand; it is mostly because you yourselves create difficulties and you yourselves create obstacles. Regarding this...
Sometimes, when people on the east and west corridors see me bowing in greeting, I simply lower my head in return.
There is truly nothing else to it; I merely wish for everyone to recognize that this old monk is a native of Longqing Prefecture in Sichuan.
If you can recognize this, I shall speak some local dialect with you and share some regional talk. For now...
I have not yet spoken. You must recognize the Elder; you must each know for yourselves. You must also know your own native place.
Do you know it? Mingzhou has six counties; Fenghua has eight districts. Entering the hall: It cannot be named, it cannot be described, it cannot be grasped, and it cannot be relinquished.
It is simply thus. But tell me, what is it that is attained? Three people testify that a tortoise is a turtle—this is the principle.
The Emperor summoned him to enter the Xuzheng Hall. His responses were detailed and clear, and he was granted a gold-embroidered *saṃghāṭī* robe.
Furthermore, he was invited to the Ciming Hall to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma; the Emperor listened from behind a curtain. He was bestowed the title Fojian.

On the first day of the third month of the Jiyou year of the Chunyou era, he fell ill. Thereupon, he ascended the seat and said to the assembly: "This mountain monk is both old and ill; I have no strength left to..."
"You people have been chattering here and there. Now, exerting myself, I shall bring forth what I have not previously spoken and shake it all out before you.
He then rose, shook his robe, and asked, "How much is there? Having said this, he returned to the Abbot’s quarters.
On the fifteenth day, he gathered the assembly and gave them his final instructions. When night fell, he wrote a verse: "When coming, empty and desolate; when departing, stark naked.
If you wish to ask for the ultimate truth, there is the Stone Bridge at Tiantai. Having cast down his brush, he passed away. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at Yuanzhao Hermitage.
Chan Master Shitian Faxun of Lingyin in Lin’an was the son of the Peng family from Meishan.

Initially, while traveling to Shichuang, he paid homage at the stupa of Lei Qian and composed a verse, saying: "A single thought of compassionate countenance is fundamentally not separated; why need one suddenly display such eccentricity?
To level the high and accommodate the low, his maternal heart is urgent; this vexes Old Lei, keeping him busy all night. Because of this, the Master’s name became "Shitian" (Stone Field).
He entered the monastic order. Having heard of the renown of Qionglong Pō’ān, he went to rely upon him.

In the meditation hall, when the master raised the story of the World-Honored One holding up the flower and Kāśyapa smiling, the teacher said: "A scorched brick strikes and freezes through to the bottom;

red-eyed one bumps into a firebrand. Pō’ān privately marveled at this. He first resided at Gāoshēng in Sūzhōu, and later moved to Fēngqiáo, Zhōngshān, Jìngcí, and Línghyìn. There, he addressed the assembly:

Simply grasp the root; do not worry about the branches. What do you call the root? What do you call the branches? "The pine and cypress remain green for a thousand years, yet they do not enter the minds of the fashionable.
The peony blooms red for but a single day, yet the gentlemen of the city all fall drunk.

When the mountain monk speaks thus, if there be anyone who does not agree, such a person is my fellow practitioner. Disciple Shi Jun has painted a portrait of his master and requested a eulogy. There is [a verse]: [Verse omitted per instructions]
He said, "The final phrase has been entrusted to Chushan. The assembly nodded in astonishment. The next day, he suddenly manifested illness and retired to Baoshou, where he prepared for his end.
His entire body was interred on the mountain behind the monastery.
Chan Master Jizan Cijue of Yunju in Nankang Prefecture was a native of Shu. He cited a monk’s question to Master Ye Xian: “What is the place where the student applies his secret mind?
Xian replied, “Rolling a ball through a bustling marketplace. The monk asked, “What is the meaning of this?
Xian said, “Invite everyone to watch. The Master composed a verse on it: Rolling a ball in the bustling market, everyone watches; A gust of pure wind [sweeps over all].
The wind blowing on one’s face is cold. To settle the turmoil, there is no need for a double-edged sword; to bring life back, what necessity is there for the nine-return elixir?

When the Master first ascended to Yunju, he stayed overnight at the Yaotian village the preceding evening. There, he dreamed that the deity of the monastery, Anle Gong, said to him, "You and Beishan share but a single karmic connection for a bowl of gruel.
The next day, after arriving at the temple in the afternoon, the evening assembly concluded, and he met two of his fellow robes.
The monks were quarrelsome and violent, and their conduct was reported to the authorities; consequently, every newcomer was customarily expelled. The Master felt deep suspicion and wonder.
Several years later, a scholar from Shu who had attained high office at court requested that the Master fill the vacant seat at Yunju.
The Master joyfully accepted the command and recalled his previous dream. He eventually arrived at Yaotian Village and passed away there.
Chan Master Yishan Liaowan of Jiangxin Temple in Wenzhou was a dharma successor of Zhongying of Jingci Temple. His clan was the Jin family of Linchuan. He was thin and frail in appearance;

at the age of fifteen, he gained renown for his proficiency in the examination essays. Nevertheless, his long-standing aspiration to leave the household life could not be dissuaded, and he followed [Master Chang] at Changle Temple in Jinxī.
When Yanshi Ren had his head shaved at the monastery, a numinous *lingzhi* fungus suddenly grew from the pivot of a door. A diviner said, "This is an auspicious omen.
Later, when the Master traveled to seek instruction, he visited Master Wen of Yanxi, Master Jue of Jingso, and Master Jing of Jianweng; all found him to be in accord with their teachings.

When Jianso took charge of Nanping, he selected the Master to serve as the *shuji* (record-keeper). One day, while passing by a shrine, the Master saw paper ashes swirling upward as they were carried by the wind. The Master...
Suddenly, he forgot what he had realized. He hurriedly informed the Elder, who questioned him until there was no longer any obstruction; thus, he received the seal of approval (*inka*).

Not long after, the General Superintendent of Jianghuai invited him to reside at Kaixian. When the Master took charge, the monastic community was renovated. Ten years later, he ascended to the abbacy of Jiangxin.
If he felt even slightly dissatisfied, he would immediately abandon his post. Although several hundred members of the monastery earnestly entreated him to remain, he followed them [to leave].
At Fenggong Ridge, they refused to follow him; they wept as they took their leave and dispersed. The Master remained serene, as if he had cast off shackles.
He was a dharma successor of Wuzhun Shanfeng, the twenty-first generation descendant of Dajian Huineng.
Chan Master Bieshan Zuozhi of Tiantong in Mingzhou was the son of the Yang family from Shunqing in Sichuan. At the age of fourteen, he received full ordination.
Upon hearing a monk reciting the words of Sixyan, he was filled with joy. At that time, Sixyan was residing at Qionglung in Suzhou; Zuozhi immediately went there to follow him as his disciple.
While reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, he encountered the passage concerning Maitreya’s tower opening and closing upon entry; he felt as if waking from a dream.
He then composed a verse on Lingyun’s seeing peach blossoms: "A single red dot amidst a thicket of myriad conditions—how many rejoice, and how many grow angry?
Yanyuan approved of it. Finally, he met Wuzhun at Xuedou; Wuzhun recognized him as a vessel for the Dharma and treated him with increasing respect.
Jùn would sometimes strike with both staff and shout, withholding not a single word of leniency. Whenever the Master attempted to respond, he was suddenly silenced and unable to utter a sound.
Through this, his reliance on intellectual understanding was completely lost. After some time, he spoke up and said: "All the skills I have cultivated throughout my life are but dead dharmas."
Now that I see this old man, the path to life finally begins. Shortly thereafter, he was transferred to Mount Jing; the Emperor ordered the Master to share the seat [with him].

In the *Bǎoyù* era, year *Bǐchén*, he received an imperial decree to reside at Tiantong. With but a single bag and a single bowl, he dwelt in a thatched hut. On the first day of the ninth month of the *Gēngchén* year, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"The clouds are thin and the moonlight is fresh; the trees have shed their leaves, and the mountain’s bones are laid bare. Since heaven and earth first came into being, how many have there been?"
His eyes were vivid. When someone came to inquire about the Dharma, the Master said, "It is too late for us to meet. Then he added, "Each of you must exert yourselves.
Ten days later, at midnight, he called his attendant and entrusted him with his final instructions, saying, "Hold the assembly in high esteem. He then crossed his hands and passed away in peace.
Chan Master Shixi Xin Yue of Jing Mountain in Lin’an, a successor in the lineage of Jinshan Kai, was a native of Meizhou. A monk asked, “What is the Buddha?
The Master replied, “A short man watching a play.”
The twenty-second generation descendant of Dajian [Huineng],
Chan Master Zhongqingfu Jinyunshan Ruhai Zhen of the lineage of Wuyong Kuan, was visited by Bifeng. The Master drew a [circle] upon the ground.
Feng drew a circle. The Master brushed it away with his sleeve. Feng then drew another circle and added a stroke within it.
The Master brushed that away again. Feng drew as before. Feng then added another stroke to form a cross. The Master brushed that away again. Feng drew as before.
Feng then added four diagonal lines to the cross to form the *svastika* (卍). The Master brushed that away again. Thereupon, the Master drew everything all at once.
When the twenty monks each answered in turn, the Master said, "Only now do you realize that the Buddha-dharma is so vast and supreme.
You should go to the north; there your Way shall flourish greatly."
The twenty-fifth generation descendant of Dajian [Huineng], Chan Master Zhaojue Zhongqing, Successor of Shaolin, ascended the hall and said:
"Eating salt only increases one's thirst. He descended from the seat. A monk asked: "Eating salt increases..."
When asked, "What is it like when one encounters thirst? the Master said, "A dog gnawing at its own shadow has no excrement to eat.
Later, Zen Master Zangfeng Jin succeeded Master Anzhao.
A monk asked him, "What is it like when one encounters a bridge and breaks the bridge? The Master said, "Where would one find such a thing?"
A person stepped forward and asked, "What is your meaning, Master? The Master said, "From the beginning, those of true skill do not manifest their names.
[He was] the twenty-sixth generation descendant under Dajian, the dharma heir of Guzhu Jun.
Chan Master Wuji of Donglin in Puzhou left the mundane world at the age of twenty. He wove bamboo to construct a hermitage and applied himself with unremitting diligence.
He would not even look at calligraphy scrolls as large as four fingers; he simply practiced his "dull" work with total, unseeing focus. Later, he attained great penetration and great enlightenment.
The Master had a verse that said: "To have no-thought is to cling to emptiness; to have thought is to cling to grasping. Both 'being' and 'non-being'..."
They forget one another; it is neither emptiness nor grasping. It is also said: "Quiescent illumination has no high or low; its radiance penetrates everywhere.
Originally there is neither black nor white; where is there that does not contain all? Chushan came forward to consult. The Master asked, "Where have you been staying for these past few years?
Chushan replied, "My dwelling is vast and empty, with no fixed location. The Master asked, "What have you attained? Chushan replied:

"Fundamentally there has been no loss; how could there be anything to be gained? The Master said, "Is it not something acquired through study? Sanshan said, "If not a single dharma exists, from where could study come?
The Master said, "Have you fallen into emptiness? Sanshan said, "I am not even 'I'; who falls and what is empty?
The Master said, "Ultimately, how is it? Sanshan said, "The water is shallow and the stones appear; the rain has cleared and the clouds have vanished. The Master [nodded].
[Zhaozhou] said, "Do not confuse the Way. Even if the Buddhas and Patriarchs were to come, they would not be permitted.
Even if you could freely swallow the entire Tripitaka and manifest hundreds of thousands of supernatural powers, here you would still not be permitted.

Xuefeng said, "Although the Master has cut off the vital pass, alas, it is no small feat to exhaust one's spirit in such a manner. The Master struck his knee once and asked, "Do you understand? Xuefeng then—
"Hai! The Master smiled and said, "One who can sustain the family must be one who can break the family. To manage the household affairs in such a manner is truly effortless.
Shan covered his ears and left. The Master bestowed upon him a verse of Dharma: "I have no Dharma to transmit; You have no mind to receive.
With neither transmission nor receiving, who would not achieve realization?"
The twenty-seventh generation descendant of Dajian (Daikuan),
Chan Master Chushan Shaoqi of Tiantong Chengsi in Jianzhou,
heir to Donglin Wufa, was the son of the Lei family of Tang’an. He entered the local monastery at the age of eight.
He was a schoolmate who had mastered the recitation of the scriptures. At the age of nine, he lost his father and went to Chan Master Tong Xuji to study the supramundane Dharma.
Later, he visited Master Wujie, who showed him the "Mu" (No) kōan. One day, while hearing the board signaling the end of meditation, a blockage in his chest dissolved like melting ice.
He went to see Wujie, who said, "Give me back the meaning of 'Mu'. The Master replied, "That monk’s question was already too full of complications. Zhao—
How could an old man ever involve himself in thought? A single word spoken offhand reveals everything. Yet, it turns out to be quite unnecessary and causes people to doubt.
[The Master] asked, "What is that place where you have no doubt? The Teacher said, "Green mountains and blue waters; swallows chirping and orioles singing—everything is vividly clear.
What more is there to doubt? [The Master] said, "Not yet. Speak further. The Teacher said, "My head touches the void, my feet tread upon the earth."
Diji said, "Not yet. The Master then prostrated. Diji said, "So it is, so it is. Later, while residing at Tianzhu, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Tianzhu?
The Master said, "The mountain stream is wide and clouds return late; the mountain peaks are high and the sun rises slowly."
[The student] asked, "What is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said, "Eyebrows beneath the forehead conceal the eyes;
ears at the side of the cheeks reach the shoulders. [The student] asked, "What is the family style of Tianzhu? The Master said, "A cloud-steamer cooks pine powder; an ice-cauldron boils moon-discs.
[The student] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The Sea God casts forth the night-bright pearl. [The student] said, "I, your disciple..."
"No. The Master said, "Mañjuśrī has lost his crystal cup. [The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A raw-iron scale weight.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "A stone or a clod of earth. [The monk] asked, "What is the Sangha? The Master said—
Holding up his black-lacquered staff, he asked, "Who is it that does not encounter cold or heat? The Master said, "I have already told you;
do you recognize him or not? The monk prepared to respond. The Master rebuked him, saying, "To conceive a thought is to deviate;
to open your mouth is to err. By the time you blink your eyes, the error has already passed. The monk said, "So it is so close, after all! The Master said, "What have you seen?"

"What principle is this? [The monk] said, "The face and features are distinct; they are not revealed when the opportunity arises. The Master let out a thunderous shout, and the monk was instantly enlightened.
In the fifth year of the Jingtai era, he resided at Touzi. A monk asked, "Having left Mount Xuan far behind, you have come to occupy Touzi.
As the assembly of monks faces the dais, we request the Master to offer prayers for the Emperor. The Master said, "The eternal seal within the cauldron; the ageless pine atop the peak. The monk said:
Having completed the ritual for the consecration of the Buddha, he received the Master’s instruction. [The student asked: "What is the teaching style of Touzi?

The Master said, "Carrying a water jar through the marketplace is not the work of an oil-seller. [The student] asked, "As for what the Patriarch said: 'Do not travel at night; you must arrive by dawn.'"
"Is there still anything definitive? The Master said, "Though there is sinew in the eyes, alas, the tongue has no bone.
[The student] asked, "Zhaozhou said, 'I have already had enough of the white; I will have even more of the black. What was his meaning?

The Master said, "If it were not for the exhaustion of arrows and bows, he would never have raised the banner of surrender. [The student] asked, "Today the Master ascended the seat to preach the Dharma; I wonder what [you have attained]?"
[The monk] presented an auspicious omen. The Master said: "The qilin strides beyond the vermilion heavens; the *utpala* flower blooms amidst the raging flames. [The monk] asked:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "When the snow melts, the mountain peaks are revealed; when the wind passes, the tree tops sway."
Chan Master Wugaijian was a native of Langzhong. He was a dharma successor of Wujiwu. He once composed a verse on "Tending the Ox" to show people, prefacing it with this introduction:
"Since there are appearances and causes, one establishes the rules for tending the ox; yet when there is no face and no form..."
Having no place from which to establish a name, he extensively opens up the medical prescriptions of the Dharma-gift to measure and treat the roots of illness, healing chronic ailments.

Although the act of scaling the city walls differs, entering the chamber is the same for all; it does not hinder one’s reaching out with the hand to summon others, yet this too is but a scene of confusion.
Since beginningless kalpas, like a water buffalo tending by the head, the nose-rope has been snapped, and one has galloped and raced through every field and marshland. No...
Remaining in a state of conjecture, one exerts oneself in deliberation and calculation, repeatedly investigating the Great Matter.

Desiring to rescue those lost on the path, one must follow the shortcut; never shirking toil and hardship, one traverses waters and climbs mountains. Wearing sharp-soled thorn-sandals, one traces footprints and seeks tracks.

This is because, having lost one's head, one identifies with its reflection; out of attachment to fragrant thickets, one turns away from awakening and unites with the dust of the senses, becoming ruined by the greed for self. This is the pitfall.

Amidst the steep ravines and deep recesses of the hills, how many times have you faltered and doubted? Within the vast and profound expanse of mist and clouds, how can one harbor indolence or negligence?

Exert yourself with even greater vigor and diligence; with a single mind, seek only the tracks of the wild boar. Suddenly, with a surge of strength, you encounter him; the silver mountains and iron walls shatter.
You dwell peacefully beneath the broken-legged cauldron; at the gate of the wooden door, by the mouth of the valley, the clouds are deep. *Xiao*.

Xiao Yujian’s *Hànqiū* (Immersed in Autumn) reads: "Brightly clear as a crystal pitcher soaking in the moon; accustomed to exposing the Yang family's ugliness on Mount Liang, one finally believes Nanquan called it a cow.
Mingchu enshrined this stele at the Yuanjue Hermitage in Lang.
Chan Master Guangshan Baoyuetan of Mount Bafeng in Taiping Prefecture was visited by Dahui.

The Master asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Dahui replied, "There are clouds upon the eastern ridge. The Master asked, "Are they clouds that will rain or clouds that will not rain?
Dahui said, "It is pouring with rain. The Master asked, "How is it after the rain has fallen? Dahui said, "White waves surge to the heavens. The Master [nodded].
The Master asked, "What is 'the myriad dharmas returning to the One'? Huì replied, "The cold and heat of the human world cannot invade it.
The Master asked, "What is 'the cassock from Qingzhou'? Huì replied, "Fortunately, it encountered the hands of a skilled craftsman.
The Master said, "The bright sun is in the sky, illuminating everything; why then is it obscured by a single cloud? Huì replied, "Boats go and boats come, yet the shore does not move."
The Master said, "Every person has a shadow; why is it that they cannot step upon it? Huì replied, "Yesterday someone came from Guangdong.
The Master said, "The entire great earth is a pit of fire; what samādhi have you attained so as not to be burned?
Huì replied, "A carp from the Eastern Sea swallows the sun. The Master said, "So it is, so it is," and bestowed upon him a verse, which began: "Heaven and Earth..."

Though vast, it could not contain him; though bright, the sun and moon find their light surpassed. He shall continue the lamp of wisdom so that it never extinguishes, its influence flowing through the ages and reaching every quarter.
His body was cremated, and his stupa was enshrined at Baoen Temple in Zhongchuan.
Chan Master Xuefeng Rui of Xichan Monastery in Chongqing Prefecture was visited by Tianqi. The Master asked, "There is nothing extraordinary," yet after some time he suddenly awakened.
He replied, "The stubborn ice at the bottom of the ravine swallows the universe; the bright moon in the lake reflects the coldness of the heavens.
The Master let out a great shout and said, "Do you still have a mind that detests the mundane and loves the sacred, or a view that sweeps away delusions to seek the truth? Tianqi replied, "Yes."
The Master said: "If you detest the mundane and crave the sacred, you sever the roots of goodness of Prajñā. If you sweep away delusion to seek the truth, you cut off the life-vein of all Buddhas.
He raised his voice and shouted again: "Who is the real? Who is the deluded?
Who is the mundane? Who is the sacred? At these words, his mind was suddenly and completely enlightened.
Shao-shi Chun-zhuo Cai, the Dharma heir of Master Liang of Yi-du, asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the east, west, south, or north. The Master struck him.
Regarding a solitary soul without a master, a monk said, "Do not strike recklessly with that blind staff. The Master said, "I am glad that this blind staff still has a blind fellow to eat it.
The monk said, "Blind! Blind! The Master said, "Even if you were blind in eighty-four thousand pores, you would still not have reached it."
