Chan Master Yongci of Dongming Haizhou in Huzhou was the son of the Yu family of Chengdu. He was born in the Jiashu year of the Hongwu era.

During his childhood, he encountered a monk who spoke to him of the great importance of the matter of birth and death; he consequently resolved to renounce secular life and proceeded to Dasui, where he paid respects to Chan Master Duzhao Yue and received the tonsure.
After residing there for eight years, he first began his pilgrimage, visiting Master Taichu He as his primary teacher.
Furthermore, when Chang first asked, "Before your parents were born, what was your original face? the Master immediately walked from east to west and stood with his hands folded.
Chang said, "That is not it; speak further. The Master replied, "Our two eyes face each other;
what is there to hide? Chang was greatly pleased. He then went to the place of Master Dongpu Wujie and recounted this as a method for practicing *gongfu*. Wujie—
He pursued his inquiries with impertinence. In the second year of the Xuande era, he left the Gorges to visit Master Linggu Xuefeng, with whom he attained profound resonance.
The Master invited him to serve as the Head Seat (Shouzuo). He then traveled to Wulin to receive full ordination and proceeded to Mount Gudao to meet the elder master Dongming.
Upon seeing him, they were immediately in accord. Dongming asked, "Who is it that can wear this markless field-of-merit robe? Dongming then descended from his seat.
[Daoming] gave him a slap. The Master said, "The four great elements are fundamentally empty; the five aggregates do not exist. How about you, Upādhyāya? Daoming gave another slap.
The Master said, "One slap does not function as one slap. Speak quickly! Daoming gave yet another slap.

The Master’s expression remained unchanged, and he said, "The reputation of the Old Monk is not spread in vain. He then unfolded his sitting cloth and performed three prostrations. Daoming said, "I dwell in antiquity..."
I have been at Dao-shan for thirty years, yet today I have seen only this monk. I wish to keep him here for several days and bestow my *kāṣāya* upon him.
The Master replied, "I did not come for the sake of robes. From then on, his reputation spread throughout the monastic community. Later, he retired to Tianjie.

In the second year of the Zhengtong era, the eunuch Yuan Cheng, admiring the Master’s virtue and character, made full preparations and requested a decree from the Ministry of Rites to appoint him as the abbot.

At Sunchon Temple, he established the mountain and preached the Dharma, and monastics gathered like clouds. Furthermore, on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month in the fifth year of the Zhengtong era, Dongmyeon entered nirvana.
He left a final testament to the abbot Baekam, saying: "I have two things: my robe and my Dharma."
He was escorted to Mount Dongshan in Jinling to see Master Haizhou, who instructed him, saying: "The characters for my name are bestowed by Cizhai Haizhou.
When you seek me, I shall have no recompense; on the day after next year’s first day, the western wind will smile and nod its head. On the appointed date the following year, he passed away.
Elder Bai’an, not violating this final instruction, requested the Head Seat, Faguang, to [preside over] the rites on the eighth day of the eighth month in the second year of the Jingtai era.
On the thirteenth day, he carried his robes and traveled to Dongshan. The Master ascended the seat, offered incense as a blessing, and received them.
The verses on ancient cases (songgu) and songs (geji) composed by his dharma heirs, such as Baofeng Xuan and others, have circulated in the world.

Having been a monk for seventy-four years, amidst many points of confusion and contradiction, at the mere sight of Dongming, [the Master] caused them to vanish. Taking up his whisk, he struck a circle (○) and said: "From Śākyamuni..."
"I have had countless old masters over sixty-two lifetimes," he said, striking a circle with his staff and adding, "Mostly they settle themselves within this.

With a shout of "Huh!", he laid down his brush and passed away. His stupa was erected on the left side of Dongming Mountain (at the same time, the one at Puci Temple in Chushu County was mistakenly identified as Yongci).
Chan Master Tang’an Zhenyuan Yan ascended the hall and said: "Mount Chu is truly like a dragon’s逆鱗 (rebellious scales) a foot long; it must not be provoked.
Tang’an has instead ventured to scratch upon the head of a venomous serpent. Does anyone understand how he can speak when there is no sound and nothing resonates?
Even until this very day, I continue to discuss it with my staff. Is there anyone in the assembly who hears this correctly? If you are correct, then tell me—"
"What did he say? After a long silence, he struck the ground with his staff and said, "Heaven!
Heaven! Tiancheng Qi, the Dharma heir of Guyu Jichuan Hong Chan Master, asked Chushan: "A gnat sucks dry the vast ocean; fish and dragons—"

“Where do shrimp and crabs find their dwelling and establish their lives? Shan said, “If your sea of consciousness were as empty as space, fish and dragons would naturally undergo their transformations.
The Master asked, “I wonder where the *jiaoming* insect is right now? Shan said, “It is beneath your eyebrows.
The Master said, “The jellyfish flies up to the Ultimate Heaven (*Akaniṣṭha*), enters the eye of Maheśvara, and performs a dance. Why is this so?”
[The Master] did not see him. Shanshan said, "How many people have, at this very place where you do not see, lost their nostrils?
The Master asked, "I wonder, what is the true eye of Maheśvara? Shanshan shouted, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand.
Shanshan said, "The two eyes on the face have nothing at all; the single point atop the head illuminates heaven and earth. The Master said, "Lianhu Bridge directly benefits people."
[Zhaozhou] pointed [at himself]. "Why is it that those with clear eyes fall into the well? Shishuang said, "High mountains have no perilous paths; level ground has deep pits.
The Master asked, "What is the matter of direct pointing? Shishuang said, "A stone lion atop a jade balustrade;
a white egret amidst red lotus flowers. The Master said, "Thank you for your answer. Shishuang said, "Be careful not to give rise to interpretations based on words. The Master... [nodded].
Prostrations.
While Master Haiju Zuyi Chan Master was in retreat at Shijing, Chushan struck the gate once and said, "I request to see the master within the retreat.
The Master stood with hands folded and body bowed. Chushan asked, "What is your daily practice?"
The Master said, "Look at Zhaozhou’s 'No-Character' (Wu). Shan asked, "What is the meaning of 'No-Character'?
The Master said, "A holeless iron hammer is thrown right in your face. Shan asked, "What was Zhaozhou’s intention? The Master said, "It is simply because his compassionate heart is so earnest."
"His liver and gall are turned toward others. Dongsan said, "Without involving existence or non-existence, how do you realize it?
The Master said, "When I reach this point, there is no place for the mind to function. Dongsan said, "That is already the functioning of the mind. The Master bowed.
Dongsan took up his staff and said, "Wait until you have passed through the barrier, and I will give you a beating. The Master said, "I am not even here right now."
Guānnèi struck the gate once with his hand and said, "What about this? The Master gave a shout. Guānnèi said, "Not yet; speak further.
The Master said, "The spiritual mechanism is without obstruction; walls and barriers are utterly transcended. Guānnèi then gave a shout in return.
The Master stepped forward to inquire after him, saying, "I thank you for your instruction. Mountan said, "The weather is scorching; take good care of yourself.
Changsong Dae-sim Jinwon, a Chan Master born into the Jang clan of Samchi, went to visit Chusan.

He asked, "Regarding that place where the words of the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past fall short, and where their practice cannot reach—please, Master, point it out directly to me. Chusan held up his staff and said, "Huh? (Nyan). The Master [thereupon] attained realization.
The Master shouted. Xishan struck him. The Master shouted again. Xishan struck him again. The Master then seized the staff and said, "Why do you strike?
Xishan gave a shout. The Master prostrated himself. Xishan said, "Whom are you traveling with on this road? The Master replied, "A wild crane soars alone beyond the Milky Way;
a clear moon shines solitary within the universe. Xishan said, "If you suddenly encounter a fierce tiger on the road—"
At that time, [Zhaozhou] asked, "How do you avoid it? The Master said, "Where is the tiger? Shan then made a tiger's roar.
The Master made a gesture of fear. Shan said, "Is that so? Have you actually seen a tiger come before you? The Master then made a tiger's roar. Shan laughed heartily.
The Master said, "I have committed an offense. Shan said, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "A clear night."
"The moon shines upon the cold plum blossoms; on this frigid night, frost strikes the sparse leaves. Shan said, "Is this it? Or is there something more?
The Master said, "A red crow flies from the branch of an ancient tree. Shan said, "Before your parents were born, try and speak a single phrase.
The Master said, "I cannot speak it. Shan said, "Why can you not speak it? The Master said, "He has no mouth. Shan said, [Nods.]
Again, the Master said, "The Way is lost at the mouth. Yunmen replied, "I thank the Master for answering my question. Yunmen said, "The final phrase reaches the secure barrier;
it blocks the vital ford, allowing neither ordinary person nor sage to pass. How do you understand this?
Yunmen replied, "A clay ox enters the sea and swallows the old dragon’s pearl. Yunmen said, "Not yet. Yunmen stepped forward, crossed his hands, and stood in silence. Yunmen [said], "..."
He said: "It is so, it is so.
Sōngpān Dàibēi Temple’s Chóngshàn Yītiānzhì, State Preceptor (Guoshi) from Pén County, possessed extraordinary features at birth.
At the age of twelve, he took Yuèguāng as his teacher. Later, he succeeded Huìxīn in residing at Sōngpān. At that time, the non-Han tribes (Fányí) rebelled."

Furthermore, he was not constant [in his presence]. While the Master resided at the frontier, pacifying and transforming the people, none among the various tribes and barbarians failed to submit to him.
During the Tiānfùn era, he was repeatedly conferred the title of Guoshi (State Preceptor). When Chūshān visited him, the Master presented his realization. Chūshān asked, "What is the meaning of 'No'?
The Master replied, "A drawn sword from its scabbard; its cold light pierces the Dipper and Ox. Chūshān asked, "Why did Zhàozhōu say 'No'? The Master replied, "The waves..."
Chewing on ice and snow, one does not perceive the coldness of one's teeth. Shanshan said, "Having set aside existence and non-existence, how do you find a place of rest?
The Master said, "In the deep night, who takes my hand to stroll together through the Imperial Street? Shanshan said, "Is there anything further, something extraordinary, beyond this?
The Master said, "The moon in every house on an autumn night; flowers everywhere when spring arrives. With a pair of clear, bright eyes—"
At Chuchachen Sha, the Master said, "Excellent.
Shijing Huotang Zu Chan Master was the son of the Ju family of Chengdu. He studied the Dharma for transcending the world under Chushan.
Mount Shan was reading the *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. The Master went before him and asked, "What you are reading is merely 'lettered prajñā.
Now, apart from these letters, I do not know what the true prajñā is. Mount Shan then held up the sutra and said:
"Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand. Shanshan said, "Can it be called 'words'? The Master said, "Can it not be called 'words'?
Shanshan said, "The true emptiness of *prajñā* is certainly not words, yet it is also not separate from words. Why is this?
It is because the nature of words is empty, and thus there is no duality between it and the essence of *prajñā*. The Master said, "This..."
Within the non-dual emptiness, can one still be attached to these words and names of the Prajñā? The Mountain Master said:

"Within the non-dual emptiness, names and words are fundamentally transcended, and there is neither truth nor falsehood. Yet, the World-Honored Buddhas of the past provisionally employed names and words to speak—namely, by not destroying conventional designations, they accomplished the wisdom of Prajñā;
without abandoning a single dharma, they realized full enlightenment. This is the text."
“This is a realm of distinction; it is not the vision of the two vehicles. The Master said, “If that is so, then names and forms are detached from their nature, and even speech is non-speech?
Mount [Shan] said, “This very absence of form and name, this absence of attainment and speech—this is true *prajñā*.
The Master then picked up a sutra and asked, “Tell me, what is this? Mount gave a shout and said:

"What do you say it is? The Master also shouted. Baoshan then snatched the sutra away and held it up again, saying, "The hundreds of thousands of samādhis and immeasurable wondrous meanings all flow forth from this single scroll of sutra. Do you know the source from which this sutra emerges?
The Master snapped his fingers once.
Chan Master Sanchi Yuezhuang Changhui was the son of the Li family of Jianzhou.
He went to visit Chushan, who asked, "Where have you been dwelling all along? The Master replied, "Because my nature is empty and without self, I dwell neither in form nor in formlessness.
Chushan said, "What is it like when both existence and non-existence are cast aside? The Master replied, "Not departing from this very place is precisely it."
“Awakened nature is the wondrous site. Yaoshan said, “I do not ask about that very place; setting aside words, movement, and stillness, what then?
The Master said, “Although you, Reverend, hold fast at the vital ford and cut off the tongue, how can you deny that the whole body is fully revealed?
Yaoshan said, “Do not speak recklessly. The Master said, “When the person is present, there is no room for evasion; how could I dare to measure it with private intent? Yaoshan said, “...”.
“Have you not spent all six periods of the day in vain? The Master said, “I have been practicing the ‘Mu’ (No) koan. Deshan asked, “What is this ‘Mu’?
The Master said, “Just now, as I went up the mountain, I felt so very weary. Deshan asked, “What is the meaning of that? The Master said, “The autumn moon is cold when the wind blows;
the old plum tree is frigid when weighed down by snow. The Master offered this verse: “No, no, no—where there is nothing, there is no place.”

Nor is it non-existent; when the clouds disperse across the vast sky, the moon stands perfectly alone. From antiquity to the present, it has never been obscured—if you wish to have your name inscribed in the charts of the patriarchs, you must realize this.
While the Chan Master Shao of Tiānchéng was in seclusion, Chǔshān knocked on his door three times with a staff and said:
"Is the master of the gate here? The Master said, "He has never had any coming or going; who says he is present or absent?
He then opened the gate, performed a prostration with unopened sitting cloth, and bowed. Yunmen said, "This is still merely the business of servants and slaves.
I request to meet the master of the gate. The Master then stood with his hands folded in silence. Yunmen said, "This is simply falling into a state of silent oblivion. The Master said, "Just now—"
The questioner asked, "What? The Mountain said, "I ask you, the master of Guanzhong. The Master said, "Can it be called 'silent stillness'?
He then presented a verse, saying: "This very silent stillness is not silent stillness; Within that which is not silent stillness, even 'not' is cut off.
His face has already been presented to the Master; In movement and stillness, when has there ever been any distinction?"

Chanshi Ruifang of Xichan was the dharma heir of Chan Master Hongyin Baowen; he was the son of the Zhang family of Tangcheng. He paid his respects to Chushan, who, upon the completion of the three-year mourning period following the death of Prince Ding and the subsequent removal of the ritual fast (*dian*), was requested to ascend the seat.
The Master stepped forward and asked: "The thunderous voice shakes the earth; the field for selecting the Buddha has opened. This single assembly—"

"The Vulture Peak remains solemnly as it was before its dispersal. I do not know how one may repay the Imperial Grace and the Buddha’s Grace. Mount [Shan] said: "The vast wind of Yao purifies the six realms;
the brilliant sun of the Buddha illuminates the three thousand worlds. The Master said: "I have heard your words of auspicious praise regarding the Master's own intent.

But as for the meaning of the flower being held up and the smile—how is that? Mount [Shan] said: "Before the pivot of the occasion, words find no place upon the tongue; I grant this only to the head."
Duo gave a smile and passed on the transmission. The Master said: "The jade plum pierces through the snow; the crimson leaves wither in the frost.

It is precisely the occasion when the imperial house removes the mourning for the Emperor, yet it is also the day the Celestial Carriage departs for the immortal realms. I wonder where the golden countenance of the Lord of Dingwang resides this very moment?"

Mount Shou held up his whisk and said, "Having already attained Equal and Perfect Enlightenment, I radiate great light and turn the Wheel of Dharma together with the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
Do you see this? The Master said, "If so, then the entire realm is free from concealment. Mount Shou said, "Even so, there are those who have eyes yet cannot see.
The Master said, "In that very place where one sees yet does not see, there is not even a hair’s breadth of separation. Mount Shou said, "..."

“This is not yet the wondrous. The Master asked, “I do not yet understand; what is the wondrous? Shanshan said, “When both extremes are wiped away, only then does one see the person prior to the kalpas.
The Master said, “I have received your pointing out of the adamantine eye; from death to birth, I shall no longer doubt.
The Master said, “It is you, Dharma brother, who has spoken it correctly.”
Bafeng heard that the Dharma heir of Zhaojue, Chan Master Wugaitong, had visited him; Bafeng instructed him with the "words" and "wordless" sayings.

After ten days of investigation, he attained realization. Following his formal installation, practitioners from all quarters arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "In years past, Luzu faced the wall; Mimi..."
Holding up the pitchfork all day long, he fails to understand how to adapt and transform when the moment arises; it will be a donkey’s year before he is permitted to reach home.
He was the twenty-ninth generation descendant under Dajian (Nanyue Huairang), the dharma heir of Guxi Cheng.
Chan Master Zongyou of Xizong in Chengdu ascended the hall. Holding his staff horizontally across his chest, he said, "Before one's parents were born, it was only this that was clear.
After one's parents were born, it was only this that was clear. He stood the staff upright and said, "Look, look, everyone!
What is this? It is like the clatter of a hot bowl. He then threw the staff down and returned to his quarters.
Liao Chan, the Dharma heir of Chengdu’s Zhaojue Baozang Tong Chan Master, addressed the assembly. He cited the karmic occasion of the moon’s waxing and waning, and offered this verse:

“Holding up the full and the deficient moon, he asks the master of the house; The autumn light has intoxicated him until his eyes are blurred. Upon the river, white artemisia meets surging red waves.”
Mistaking reeds for snowflakes.
The thirty-first generation descendant under the Sixth Patriarch, Tianmu Jin.

Chan Master Baoming Jian of Baiyun at Qian’an was a native of Shu. Having studied under Chan Master Tianmu Jin of Shoutang and attained the Dharma, he left the gorges to travel extensively through the regions of Xiang and Hu.
During the Zhengde era, he took up residence at Mount Baiyun in Huanggang for many years.
A monk asked, “What is the student’s own self? The Master replied, “Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; where there is no Buddha, one must hasten.”
He walked past and said, "I, a student of the Way, do not understand. The Master said, "A single palm has five fingers.
He asked, "What is it like to be one among the people of Baiyun Mountain? The Master said, "Binding the three strips of bamboo; a single-character barrier across and down."
The thirty-first generation descendant of Dajian (Da Jian),
Shimen Haifa’s successor,
Chan Master Da Xiu Zonglong of Qijianfeng Peak in Suizhou, was a son of the Jia family from Yidu. He relied upon [the monastery] of the local prefecture’s stone...

The Buddha shaved his hair and stayed at Beisi Temple in Chengdu as the *dianzuo* (chief cook). While going out into the street to fetch water, he suddenly forgot where he was walking and struck his head against a wall that had collapsed.
At that moment, he attained realization and composed a verse: "The nature and essence of the great earth, mountains, and rivers are empty;

How can one distinguish between south, north, east, and west? By chance, I have struck upon the impartial phrase: Ten thousand waters and a thousand mountains are all one and the same. He then went to Qianzhou in Henan.

He stayed for some time in the Wujin Chamber (Inexhaustible Room) of Ming Temple. Like a needle meeting its eye, their minds met; he sealed this with a verse: "The Way is lofty, requiring no cultivation;
Virtue is weighty, encompassing all principles and affairs. This single branch of the True Dharma Eye Is entrusted to Long Da-xiu.

After he had taken up residence there, while he was stringing melons, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master pointed to an eggplant and said, "Wang-gua and eggplant. The monk did not attain realization.
He descended the mountain and visited another venerable master. The master asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Peak of the Pinnacle.
The master asked, "What words did Daixiu say? The monk recounted the previous conversation. The venerable master joined his palms and said, "Truly, what great compassion!
On the eighth day of the eleventh month in the twenty-first year of the Jiajing era, he gathered the assembly and wrote this verse: "Grasping the three periods of time..."
Holding his staff, he said: "The ten directions are originally the old cassock; the clay ox and stone tiger know the news.
Treading through empty space, one arrives home. He then set down his brush, sat upright, and passed away.
The thirty-second generation descendant of Dajian (Mazu),
Chan Master Yifeng Fangtan of Baima Temple in Dazhou, a dharma heir of Fabi Ji, was the son of the Luo family of Benzhou. He went to visit Jinfoshan.
Yun’an was instructed to contemplate, "What is the mechanism that ghosts and spirits cannot perceive? After three years, he attained a realization.

He left the gorges to visit various masters extensively before settling in a thatched hut by the Double Creek. One day while cooking his midday meal, he heard a sound from within the steamer; suddenly, he experienced great enlightenment.
The Verse says: The Three Mysteries and Three Essentials have no source from which they emerge; Exhausting all intellectual ingenuity, there is nowhere to seek them.
A step forward at the window, a step back to the hearth— The white snow and blue peaks nod their heads in unison. Nodding their heads in unison: Mount Heng and Mount Tiantai share a single tally.
It is further said: "A girl of sixteen marries a new husband; she spins hemp and twists thread just as usual.

She passes her time according to the family’s abundance or scarcity, and does not lazily burn incense before the ancestral hall. Upon hearing this, Wuhuan remarked, "This person has practiced subtle and refined cultivation.

Those who know the sound strike together. They strike together; the seasonal rhythms do not spare one another. The three springs have already passed; the nine summers are now in full bloom. The green willows open like eyebrows and eyes;
the red peach blossoms accord with the fundamental mind. Therefore it is said: "Without leaving the Hall of Precious Flowers, one does not transcend the Bodhi-maṇḍala.
Layer upon layer, the Flower Treasury worlds interpenetrate; point by point, the pearl nets are perfectly radiant. But tell me, speak!
By whose grace and power do I wield the Mohe sword to uphold the true decree? In this realm of Great Peace, I strike down the foolish and the stubborn.
Ascending the hall to give thanks for the snow: The piercing cold and majestic stillness reign supreme; Flakes of snow drift upon the flames of the red furnace.

Roll up the curtain and grasp the meaning of the Western Come; Countless jade branches brush against the willow twigs. Ascending the hall: The mind is not the nature; to identify the nature is to deviate from the source.
The nature is not the mind; to establish the mind is to lose the essential meaning. The nature is fundamentally unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*), and the mind likewise has no form.
Within this state of the unconditioned and formless, one discerns the ultimate point: all forms whatsoever are the mind, and all that is conditioned is the nature.
When released, heaven and earth are filled to overflowing; when gathered in, the wind blows and the grass bows. Now, regarding this single phrase of gathering and releasing—how do you speak of it?
"The thread on the tip of the pole is played with by you; yet, without disturbing the clear waves, its meaning is naturally distinct."

Chan Master Huijueyi was the son of the Xiong family of Qijiang. Having lost his father at the age of seven, he reached thirty years of age and awakened to the suffering and emptiness of worldly existence.
He received the tonsure under Master Changbai of Huayin Mountain. Later, he attended upon the Old Man Shuanggui, finally receiving certification of his realization.
Upon returning, he resided at Zhiping Temple in the city of Yuzhou. Ascending the hall, he said: "For six years, I have endured bitter hardship and diligent toil; a single point of clarity..."
A star pierced his eye. Just as it was said that Gautama attained Perfect Enlightenment, he ascended the hall at three *geng* (hours) past noon, as on the previous day.

Father and son share the same sentiment, utterly devoid of "self" and "other"; ruler and minister are in accord, profoundly transcending intimacy or estrangement. Thus he governed the state and regulated the family.
Above calls and below responds; entering, it is like a vine leaning against a tree; exiting, it is like an arrow leaving the bowstring.

Not only does it pierce nine layers of armor, but it also penetrates directly through the myriad affairs of state. Sometimes both the bow and arrow are withdrawn, and their sharp points fall to the ground.
Tell me, where lies the benefit or the harm? The King’s command has already been issued throughout the world; the General beyond the frontier has brought all dust and smoke to an end.
Chan Master Linmu Shou was the son of the Jiang family of Fengling. He attended upon Master Ming of Shuanggui and served as the head administrator of the monastery;

it was there that he first received formal certification of his realization. With a mind inclined toward joy and travel, having heard of the exquisite beauty of the mountains and waters of Wu and Yue, he set out on a single boat with a carefree air, leaving behind a verse that spoke of not being among the common sightseers.
Later, he returned to Zhaojue in the capital of Jin’guan. At the request of his Dharma brother, Master Zui, he ascended the hall to preach. Out of compassion—

Recalling the past while meeting this auspicious festival, ten thousand *li* of mountains and rivers spread out like brocade. Having paid my youth’s dues, I now enjoy the abundance bestowed by the Sage’s grace;
from a lion-forest or leopard-den, one may become a hero. But tell me, what is this "hero"? Heaven attains it and becomes clear;
Earth attains it and becomes peaceful. When a sovereign attains it, the myriad states come as subjects; when high ministers attain it, they harmonize the soup with salt and plum. As for the scholar—
The people gain a filial son and a worthy grandson; the patch-robed monks gain a pillar for the school of the lineage. I venture to ask the great assembly: what is this "one"?
The fragrance of the Double Magnolia wafts far; at Zhaojue, clouds of compassion gather. In the end, he returned to the Great Buddha Temple in Nanpu.
He was thus honored for his excellence in old age.
Chan Master Yunhuan Chen was the son of the Wan family in Wanzhou, Dongzhou, Shu. He had always harbored the aspiration to transcend the mundane world.

At sixteen, he left home to become a monk; at twenty, he received full ordination from Chan Master Xiangya. After serving him with the water pitcher and towel for three years, he went to attend upon Master Boshan.

Having devoted himself to this for several years, he was granted the prediction of his future enlightenment. Responding to the invitation from Zhongfeng Chan Monastery in Bazhou, he entered the monastery and ascended the hall to preach.
With a single step, he transcended all; with a mere snap of the fingers, he fully realized the unconditioned. His two eyes opened wide, as if suddenly attesting to the wondrous fruit of Buddhahood.
The mind is fundamentally the Buddha; why must one seek the sword and carve the boat? Thought is itself emptiness; how could one leave the waves to seek the water?
As the moon reflects upon a thousand rivers, there are transformed bodies by the billions everywhere; as spring returns to ten thousand trees, there are responses to conditions at every turn.
The brothel and the wine shop are the very site of Maitreya’s Dharma assembly; the tiger’s den and the demon’s palace are originally the precious abode of Śākyamuni.

By citing one to illuminate three, one cuts off the divergent paths of humans and devas; by knowing ten to answer a hundred, one does not fall into the rungs of the stages of ordinary beings or sages.

It is capable of repaying the unrequited kindness of others and serves as a transformation of non-action. The heavens of Yao and the suns of Shun increase in brilliance, and the golden chariot and Dharma wheel turn eternally.
At such a time, how do you express the single phrase for blessing the nation and benefiting sentient beings? How would you say it?
The smoke of war has ceased throughout the four seas; may all nations enjoy only peace and prosperity.
Master Jiguang Huo was born into the Yang clan of Nanchong. In his middle years, he shaved his head and received formal certification from Master Ming of Shuanggui.
He resided at Fuzi Chan Temple on Mount Longyin. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "The great furnace is first opened; the tongs and hammers are heated."
"Pungent! Hot iron on a cold block—each strike must land exactly where it is aimed, never missing its mark. Even so, Old Monk Mu would not yet grant full approval to such talk.

He struck the ground once with his staff and said, "Do you understand? Both Buddhas and Patriarchs, as well as all things animate and inanimate, are entirely upon the tip of this mountain monk’s staff.
Therein lies the power to bestow or withhold, to kill or give life. Among the assembly, was there anyone who...?
If you can perceive this, listen to a verse: The scales weigh both killing and giving life, surpassing all heroes; When the banners and drums are raised, their courage is lofty.
How many great generals are there who can draw the bow? With a single well-placed arrow, they bring down two vultures. (He lets out a shout.)
Chan Master Yiyuan was the son of the Liao family from Ziyang. While reading the *Nirvana Sutra* (Yuánjué), he contemplated the impermanence of the world;
at the age of thirty-three, he finally underwent tonsure. Hearing that Master Ming’s dharma style was greatly flourishing, he went in person to study under him, changing his name to Yinshi.
He subsequently received the master’s seal of transmission (*kaji*). Later, while residing at Daxingshan Temple in Xian’an, he ascended the hall and said: "The mysterious mechanism operates alone."
The present and the past are as one; time and season are not easily spared. Cold and heat alternate in succession: at Yunmen, the wooden horse neighs in the wind;

when the myriad yin energies are completely stripped away, on the Snowy Ridge, the mud ox roars at the moon. As the first yang returns, the cold light shines brilliantly through the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*), and harmonious warmth radiates from the ninefold palace.
Throughout heaven and across all lands, all alike receive the grace of their creation and sustenance. But how should the man of the way beneath the forest trees respond?
Only taking up the story of the Śāla tree at Vulture Peak where the flower was held aloft, may it assist and support the imperial destiny for ten million springs. Entering the hall, he said:
"Jade bones and ice-like flesh—the plum blossoms are still far away. In the vast sky, stars and moon form frost-flowers. Clearly, the Way issues forth from within this;
For what reason does one further count the sands by the sea?"
The Venerable Shengke of Huayan in Yuzhou was the son of the Wang family of Yingzhou. He was short in stature and profoundly silent, remaining aloof from the secular world.
Once, while listening to the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, he heard it said that beings born from eggs, wombs, moisture, or by transformation all realize the indestructible body of adamant.

Feeling a slight sense of doubt and wonder, he subsequently left his home and went to Liaoyang to become a disciple under a master, receiving the Dharma name Deyu. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or...
While lying down, he began to doubt that this body was composed of pus and blood, being like a mass of foam. He wondered, "What among these is my indestructible diamond-like self?
Consequently, he went to consult Master Ming of Poban. For several years, he questioned him with his previous words until he finally received certification of his realization.
Because his wild monkey-mind had not yet been brought under control, he traveled across half the world. Later, he returned to the ancient cave of Huayan, where people from far and near...

Listen to this. Those who return are as numerous as in a marketplace. The assembly requests that he ascend the hall: the crowing of roosters, the barking of dogs, the chirping of magpies, and the cawing of crows—Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva has arrived.
Within walls, tiles, rubble, the great earth, mountains, and rivers—the Vow-King Samantabhadra is present.

To seek the person amidst sounds and forms, or for him to extend his hand from within hearing and seeing, is certainly not impossible; yet to overturn sounds and forms and kick away hearing and seeing—[this is the true path].
[The Master] said: "How would you say it? 'A few sounds of the clear chime lie beyond right and wrong; a single idle man dwells within heaven and earth.

While staying at Fushan in Luzhou, on the occasion of the Buddha’s Birthday, the Prefect, Lord Chen, entered the mountain and hung ceremonial banners. He invited the Master to ascend the hall. A monk asked: "The Ruler's grace is like a mountain;
how can one repay it? The Master said: "The rain falls steadily through the night. The monk pressed further: "Parental grace is like the sea; how..."
[The Master] replied, "A clap of thunder after a flash of lightning. Xuefeng advanced and said, "I have repaid your kindness and requited your virtue as you have pointed out to me.
Now that the Dharma Protector Chen has entered the mountain, how will you receive him? The Master said, "The cassia fan is just right for this summer;
the rice-planting needle is swift during the wheat harvest. Xuefeng said, "If that is so, then within the Gate of Non-duality there is no discrimination—how about human sentiment?"
"The Buddha-dharma is complete in both parts. The Master said, "It must also be personally realized by you, O *śrāmaṇera*. He then said: "Dharmada manifests in the body of a high official;
how could the clouds of Māra and heretics ever invade him? Last year his golden body was sixteen feet tall; this morning those sixteen feet are truly Kāśyapa.
Suddenly, he took up his whisk, called to the assembly, and asked, "Do you recognize Kāśyapa yet? [The disciple] replied, "A subject repays the kindness of his sovereign."

"Returning kindness to one's parents. [The Master] struck the whisk twice. While staying at Jia Rui Temple in Suizhou, Zunyi Prefecture, he ascended the hall for the summer retreat and raised the following case:
Ancestor Huqiu Long was asked by a monk, "Regarding the ninety-day restriction of the feet—what is the meaning of this?

The Ancestor said, "When principle prevails, one follows it. The monk pressed further, "As for those whose six sense organs are incomplete, can they still observe this restriction? The Ancestor said, "To pierce through..."
[The Master] pinched his nostrils. [Xuefeng] stepped forward and said, “This student has come out small but encountered something great. The Patriarch said, “A surrendered general is not executed.
[Xuefeng] said, “If that is so, then please let me go as I please. The Patriarch said, “Imprisoning prisoners only increases their cunning. The Master [Yunmen] said:

“Patriarch Long’s such cleansing of the feet and tuning of the mind—highly building the walls and fences, deeply digging the moats and ditches, and secretly fortifying the numinous root—can truly be called having...”

Fundamentally, it is simply that you have been too narrow-minded in your approach. Today, De-yu is not like this. Suppose someone were to ask: "What is the meaning of the ninety-day restriction of the feet (the *kaḍaśī*)?
One would have a precedent to cling to if there is one; if there is no precedent, one clings to an analogy. "Can those whose six sense-faculties are incomplete still observe this restriction?
"In brothels, many are painted with surnames; in wine shops, there are poems bearing famous names. The student has stepped out only a little and encountered a great challenge.
"Amidst ten thousand waters and a thousand mountains, there still remains the dust upon one's straw sandals. The verse says: Who knows that mind which has no abiding?
Even lightning and sparks are too slow in comparison. For now, take the Dharma-realm as your bed and seat; within the gateway of entering principle, there is the nightingale.
Chan Master Kuai Xue was the son of the Wang family of Dangqu. He possessed a refined spirit and a clear, vigorous temperament, with an air of elegant detachment.
He entered the quarters of Master Ming and later resided at Dongchan Hermitage in Nanlong. Upon ascending the hall, he was asked: "What is the scenery within the mountains?"
The Master said: "The green waters flow surging through the mouth of the cave; light yellow leaves flutter down from the treetops. He then continued:
"Since my coming of age, I have split open this gateway. When I try to pull it up, it will not budge; when I try to prop it up, it will not stay.
Amidst deep mountains and vast wilderness, I have no one on either side to rely upon. Forced to sustain myself alone, I plow with a blade for my livelihood and gather grain for sustenance."
Three or five *shí* of grain suffice for my robes and skirt; day and night, my mind never ceases. My backbone is cast from forged iron;
I rouse my aged spirit and nurture the tree within my heart. For several years I have not left the mountains, experiencing neither honor nor disgrace.
Yet I encountered a heartless fellow who forcibly drove me out. I do not yet understand the Way of Chan, nor am I adept at human affairs. I am but a mountain man.
I am ashamed of my own lack of ability; all day long I remain as if in a daze, like a pillar.
Chan Master Shou of Heshang Stone Banner in Hezhou was the son of the Yao family of Jialing. Initially, he resided in the hall of Master Zhang at Yumen, attending him for a very long time.
He subsequently went to Shuanggui to receive formal certification and lived at Longyou in Puyang, where his single mat was desolate and simple.
He possessed nothing extra; he maintained the style of returning to Stonehead. A monk asked, "What was it like before the Master had seen the Old Man Pó?
The Master said, "The light of his eyes pierced through the four quarters of the world. The monk pressed further, "And what was it like after he saw him? The Master said, "Blind."
The student said, "It is not so for this student. The Master said, "Try to say it. The student said, "Before I had seen the Master, I was blind;
after seeing you, my eye-sight has pierced through the four worlds. The Master held up his whisk and asked, "Do you see? The student said, "I see. The Master then struck him.
He ascended the hall and said: "The six gates are open and unobstructed; how could the myriad phenomena escape their shadows? By transcending through the single gate, all objects [are revealed]."

From this point on, he concealed his traces. Within a single gate, six doors are contained; though there are a thousand variations, they share the same track. By means of the six doors, one returns to the single gate;
though there are ten thousand distinctions, they originate from the same source. There is neither interior nor exterior. Its brilliance surges through past and present; it is neither dark nor light.

If you can realize this, you will transcend the conventional and leap beyond the lineage. Ascending the hall, he said: "The dragon roams where there is no dharma to speak of; its movements are free and unimpeded. Pick it up—"
The turtle-nosed snake reveals the crane soaring to the clouds; let it go and it traverses the universe, gather it back and it follows its natural fit.

It does not linger in the mechanism of existence or non-existence, nor can it be divided by the smallness or greatness of the moon. In essence, everything is thus—whom could anyone possibly fathom? [He ascended the hall.]

Upon entering the Way, upon what does one rely for abiding? The binding of the mind occurs spontaneously and simultaneously. Without following such a gradual progression, from where could one establish the framework?
The pearl of the nature shines with brilliant light; the waters of craving at the source of emotion dry up. In every instance, one returns to actual reality; in every thing, one realizes *tathatā*.
Ascending the hall at Dinglin Monastery: A single phrase is fully raised, cutting off a thousand divergent paths. Two mirrors reflect one another, illuminating the mechanisms beyond the norm.
Though phenomena have many routes, the principle has no different destination. To thoroughly awaken to the source of the Dharma, one knows its own limits;
to penetrate to the very top and bottom, one must rely on the far-reaching penetration of sagely wisdom. Those with shallow views and meager learning are simply deluded and inferior.

Zhi ascended the hall and said: After the ashes fly from the reed-pipes, the first yang energy circulates throughout the world. The cowherd is too weary to tend his calves; the fisherman is too timid to cast his hook.
The mountain’s countenance grows thin with cold dew; the water-realm is secluded in frosty chill. The岭梅 (Ling-mei) plum possesses much spirit;
amidst the snow, its dark fragrance floats forth.
Chengdu Randidian Baicheng was a Chan master born into the Shen family of Kuizhou. He received the Dharma lineage from the Venerable Poshan Ming.
At the invitation of Du Yongzhou, he resided at the Zhunti Pavilion. Entering the hall, he said: "The body dwells amidst the dust of the world, yet the mind transcends beyond it."
Although he dwells in the Yellow Hall, his past causes still remain. He has dispatched a note three times requesting that you fly your staff [to him] for our mutual reliance.

Regarding this matter, how can it be carried on with a single word? And what matter is there to carry? After a long silence, he said: "The fish swims in the spring water; the flowers toss upon the waves."
A bird enters the jade grove to sport with its colorful branches. Entering the hall: For many years I have harbored my simplicity, reclining amidst mists and clouds;
on this day, dwelling in the marketplace, every matter is deferred. It is not that I have a heart greedy for wealth and honor, but simply because the rain and dew fall upon the mountain home.
Thus, Scholar Su left behind his jade belt to stabilize the mountain gate, and Prime Minister Pei bequeathed his memorial tablet and official staff to illuminate the ancestral seat. Now...
The ancient hands and eyes differ, yet for the most part, the nostrils are one. (He suddenly holds up a whisk and says: "In the past at Vulture Peak, you were the foremost;
today at this Dharma assembly, you act as the golden rampart."
Yichuan Huan Chanshi of Yunqing Temple on Mount Sifeng in Luzhou was the son of the Yang family of Sanrong in Jiazhou, southern Sichuan.
He was born in the Jiawu year of the Wanli era of the Ming dynasty. From birth, he was precocious and possessed auspicious physical marks.

At the age of seven, he went to Mount E to tonsure his hair. He had previously studied the *Lotus Sūtra* and the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, and by the age of nineteen, he ascended the Dharma seat to lecture on the scriptures, never descending from it.

He was surrounded by ten thousand people. Later, he traveled extensively to visit renowned masters throughout various regions; however, because his spiritual faculties were dull and slow, he purchased a boat and returned to Shu.

At Tashan Temple in Jiang’an, he lectured on the *Lotus Sūtra*. Coinciding with this, the Elder Po began teaching the Dharma at Panlong, so he went directly to that assembly, yet again it did not accord with his capacity.
He then entered a three-year retreat at Guangfu Temple, concluding his stay at Yunqing Temple.

Having lived in seclusion for many years, in the autumn of the *Renchen* year, the Old Man [Zhaozhou] summoned me down to Shuanggui with a handwritten note. Consequently, I issued the records of the lineage and the transmission of the seal.
The local officials and commoners of this prefecture requested that I open the Dharma at Yunqing. Ascending the hall, I struck the drum and took my seat.
I planted tortoise-hair within the fire and rolled up the mats before the assembly; I turned the millstone in mid-air. Even so, it is not permitted.
It is not that it cannot be so; yet it is also not that it can be so, nor that it cannot be so. Why? Because they have no wounds themselves, do not injure them.
All phenomena are fundamentally at ease; only people are themselves restless. Moreover, at this very moment, what is it like?
A single mass of samādhi light illuminates the universe; with a sincere heart, one secretly serves the imperial grace.
Liangsheng from Songqiu in Zunyi was the son of the Ding family of Yongchuan in Shu.
Both his parents dreamed that the monk Zhencong had come to visit them; that very night, a son was born in their chamber.

Consequently, both the elderly and the young called him Zhencong, and he was thus named Liangsheng (Two Lives). From childhood, he abstained from alcohol and meat. At the age of seven, he went forth under his paternal uncle.
He was unusual among his peers; from a young age, he practiced lecturing. Later, he received formal certification (*inka*) from Master Ming of Shuanggui.
At the invitation of Hengzhao Chan Temple, he ascended the hall to open the Dharma. "Today is the first day of the tenth month; everywhere else the work of plowing and harrowing is finished.
Only here in the mountains of Hengze is there yet another precedent. But tell me, what precedent is this? A new one has emerged."
This herd of young calves has only today been pierced through the nose; wait for the proper time to arrive, and each one shall plow over the great earth.
The Defense Commissioner requests the Master to ascend the hall. Today is the fifth day of the first lunar month; the Star of Longevity shines brightly upon the prefectural seat.
The subordinate officials move about like smoke; where does the man of the forest retreat dwell? The entire assembly has gathered in the Dharma Hall in great numbers.
"I must further strike a drum of words for you. Let me ask all of you: do you understand?
He struck the meditation staff once and said, "Lifting up the eighteen beats of the *huqia*, its melodic tones and rhymes shall endure for a thousand ages. At Huoguo Temple, he ascended the hall.
Today we joyfully encounter the "Nine Yang" (shangjiu) hexagram. It stirs the assembly of humans and devas; monks from the four quarters have returned here.

This is precisely the time to shake off all dust. Thus it is said: "The matters of kalpas past reside only in the present. That which lies beyond the limit of awe-inspiring sound (weiyin) is entirely within one's grasp.
The Dharma follows the Dharma in its application, reaching everywhere without exception. The mind follows the mind in its functioning, pervading everywhere without exception. Upon arriving...
"What is being discussed here? One hundred years in the human realm is but a single day and night in the heavens. [The Master] suddenly presents his staff and says:
"If you understand this thoroughly, then the World of Wondrous Joy in the East does not depart from this very place;
the World of Ultimate Bliss in the West does not depart from this very place; even the world of the *kāṣāya* does not depart from this very place. The lapis lazuli of the heavens..."

The crystal world and the Hall of Good Dharma atop Mount Sumeru are both entirely not apart from this very place. Thus, when one location is illuminated, a thousand locations and ten thousand locations are radiant;
when one mechanism is turned, a thousand mechanisms and ten thousand mechanisms unfold clearly. Yet, all the while, they do not depart from the single fundamental phrase.
How would you say it? "When meeting someone, speak only three-quarters of what is on your mind; do not yet cast forth your whole heart.
He lived seventy-two years and passed away without illness. His entire body was interred to the right of Songqiu.
Chan Master Liuxiu Kui of Pengxi was the son of Zheng of Changshou. He strictly observed the principle of "central harmony" (*zhonghe*).

Profound, humble, and straightforward, he went to visit Master Ming at Shuanggui, where he attained realization under the master’s staff and subsequently received dharma transmission from him. Later, he resided at Mount Lianpeng in Pengxi.
Upon ascending the hall for a formal address, he said: "Today, Lianpeng opens a new furnace; the auspicious destiny unfolds as the heavens open and the atmosphere relaxes. The Way is harmonized..."
The Sage Ruler manifests his virtuous transformation; in times of harmony, the faithful offer incense at the kitchen. Where dragons coil and tigers crouch, he dwells in meditative concentration;

when the elephant departs and the master arrives, they serve as protective talismans. This great causal connection is a most sublime matter; together we gaze upon the Buddha-sun and pray for the imperial destiny.
Ascending the hall: Yesterday, the day before yesterday, and today—layer upon layer, these are the public proclamations of our own family’s private matters.

It is not that there is idle chatter from beneath the tongue; rather, it is intended that everyone shall know this exists. Ascending the hall: On the fifteenth of the third month, the Lantern Festival, the Imperial Guard do not impose prohibitions.

The fire-trees and silver flowers burst forth in brilliance, their radiance piercing the clouds and heavens. The star-bridges and iron locks are opened, and the sounds of songs and pipes resonate through the mountains and valleys.
Long streets and short markets; it is as if one has arrived at the celestial gardens of Langyuan or Penglai. Willow alleys and misty villages are transformed into the world above the heavens.
In such a fine season and rare spectacle of a prosperous age, how may a monk beneath the forest trees celebrate and enjoy this? *Chan*.
Chan Master Yumu Zhang of Yunxi in Luzhou was a native of that prefecture.

Having shaved his head at the age of seven, he subsequently visited the Dharma seat of Old Man Poshan at Panlong Temple in Jiang’an, where they shared some karmic conditions, which are recorded in detail in the master’s own records.
Upon the conclusion of the summer retreat, he received the master’s formal transmission and resided at the Xingfo Chan Monastery in Yunxi for over thirty years. (Kangxi...)
Winter of the Gui-mao year. Opening the furnace, he ascended the hall and, with his whisk, drew a circle, saying:
"Do you all recognize this? This is the manifestation of the primary truth; it flows forth from the boundless oceans of lands. It is fundamentally pure."
Without deficiency and without excess; without birth and without cessation; without gain and without loss. It serves as the root of all phenomena, and is also called the single mark of marklessness.
It is profoundly still and perfect, manifesting in its entirety; it alone reveals the true and eternal, tranquil and non-dual.
When Shan-yeh makes such an announcement, it is like gouging a sore on healthy flesh. Even these wondrous words and profound expressions cannot avoid the laughter of bystanders.
Setting this matter aside for a moment: how do you speak the single phrase for opening the furnace? After a long silence, he said: "The vast grace first manifests before heaven and earth;
the peaceful transformation returns to the Great Sage. He ascended the hall and said: "The Ultimate Way cannot be approached with a mind of intentional effort."
It can be attained, but it cannot be sought with a mind that is absent. At this very moment, there is no mind within and no form without.
Above, there are no Buddhas or patriarchs to look up to; below, there are no sentient beings to pity. Utterly bare and naked, completely free of anything to take on; vividly clear and pristine.
There is no mutual interdependence. When you arrive here, it is not turbid when stirred up, nor is it clear when settled; one must be a person of this very caliber to attain it.
Therefore, such a person is called a "man of non-action. [The Master] suddenly holds up his whisk and says:
"Do you see? Do not resent my former abundance of spirit; he [the Master] has once trodden upon the highest pass."
Chan Master Gengyun Jian of Zhiji Monastery in Jianzhou was the son of the Wu family of Neijiang. He was the uterine younger brother of Master Lingfa and later succeeded the Elder Shuanggui.
While presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and said: "Subtle conduct and secret practice—transcending the kalpas, one stands with body erect."
He manifests great spiritual wonders, standing alone as the sovereign within the world. This is neither the silent meditation of Śūnyatā-janman nor the supernatural powers of Śāriputra;
it is simply the value of his majestic and wondrous function, his formidable authority, which causes the celestial Māras to fold their hands in submission and the non-Buddhists to surrender.

May it forever serve as a protective citadel for the Buddhist realm and eternally act as a pillar and beam for the Dharma-gate. Thus, the ancestral Way is magnified and the lineage’s principles are grandly supported.
The mundane world is transformed into a *śītavana* grove, and this defiled land becomes a pure realm.
May the true pulse of the Cao Yuan source flow on unceasingly, and may the family reputation of the Ji Bei school be perpetually resounded. (He lets out a shout.)
Chan Master Yunqiao Shui of Shuanggui was the son of the Zhao family from Bazhou. Initially, he went to see Master Ming at Qifeng to request instruction.
Master Ming asked, "What is it that you lack? The Master replied, "Nothing deficient and nothing in excess. Master Ming then held up his fist and said:
"You have not even dreamed of this yet," the Master said, and with a shout he departed. Ming called him back and gave him a slap. "What more bowl do you seek?
From that time on, his state of doubt grew ever more intense. When Ming went to Jincheng Zhai on Mount Liangshan, he commanded the Master to compose a verse:
"The Phoenix perches today, dispersing water and clouds; Whether moving forward or backward, let it act as it pleases. A broken sand-pot contains the True Dharma Eye."

Fearing that the pursuit of worldly defilements would pollute the basin, he later entered the room of Master Ming at Shuanggui. Master Ming asked, "When walking, you do not go out the door; when sitting, you do not occupy the hall.
The Master replied, "The bright moon is before the courtyard's cassias; pines and bamboos draw in the pure breeze. Ming said, "A fellow who scratches his itch through a boot.
