The gate possesses the eye; behind the elbow lies the seal-base. With a single movement, one knows whether it is biased or correct.
If you are solely addicted to sounds and forms, you will inevitably miss the mark right before your own face. [He] suddenly took up his staff, struck it once, and said: "Do you understand?
Do not taste the water from a household infected by poison. Later, while residing at Ba’en, he addressed the assembly: "Yesterday I made a trip to Suzhou. Long...
At the ends of streets and short alleys, people come from the east and go to the west; they have never seen anything at all.
Only at the pork stalls, every block of meat is as fresh as the face of Mount Pan; in the teahouses and wine shops, every phrase is like a spring breeze, singing out the very heart of the towers.
How many onlookers are like the wind passing through trees? How many who are utterly intoxicated are like butterflies?

Loving flowers; greedily pursuing life, one hastens about in vain. Calling out, they do not turn their heads—what can be done? To the assembly: At the winter solstice, the first yang arises; it is like frost added to snow.
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth freeze until the cliffs collapse and the rocks crack. The myriad phenomena and all things are shrouded in stillness.
Following the teaching, leaves fall by the branches; the frogs and earthworms do not yet know how to turn over, and the cats and dogs—how could they recognize long from short?
O worthy ones, let us not speak of the ground where yin and yang exist; but on the ground where there is no yin or yang, how will you deliberate?
After a long silence, he lets out a shout and says: "If one does not undergo a single freezing of the bones, how can one attain the plum blossom?"
Poxue Xiang. Linye Qifa was a dharma successor of Chan Master Xianjue;
he was the son of the Yu family of Hezhou in eastern Shu. At the age of seven, he paid homage to Master Taikong and left the household life.

He replied: "At fifteen, I frequented lecture halls and thoroughly refined myself in the Three Studies. I visited the elder master Mi of Tiantong and asked about the karmic occasion of 'All phenomena return to One.
Upon being struck by the elder with a single kick, I attained realization. At that time, Master Linye was residing at Guanghua Temple."

He then hurried to his seat and received the seal of certification. After some time, the community of Luohan Chan Temple in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, requested him to preside over the monastery.
He ascended the hall and said: "I have no desire to appear before people in my ordinary state; for what reason have I now changed my course?
It is simply because we met unexpectedly on a narrow path that I cannot avoid displaying my clumsiness this time. Thereafter, having nowhere else to hide...
Gate! One must simply don these tattered and filthy robes and engage in a bit of "entanglement" with the assembly. [The Master] suddenly brandishes his whisk and says:

"If one discusses this matter, it radiates brilliance through the present and the past, encompassing and exhaling the ten voids. It cannot be known by intellect; it cannot be recognized by consciousness.
To look upon it is to go blind in both eyes; to smell it is to split open the crown of the head. Even were it the Buddhas of the three periods..."

A towering wind has arisen. The patriarchs of successive generations had their share of stepping back; yet for one of vast capacity, to cast aside Chan, the Way, and the Buddha-dharma all at once—this is already something special.
Why need there be three ascents and nine climbs, or seven breakages of the meditation cushion?
Before those with clear eyes, these are but a source of laughter. Now tell me: how do you speak the single phrase of "taking one's place according to the position"? After a long silence...
It is said: "When the waves of the four seas are stilled, the dragon sleeps soundly; when the clouds of the nine heavens are clear, the crane flies high.
This refers to when Great Master Linji first resided in Hebei, where he spoke to Puhua and Ke fu, saying: "I wish to establish the school of Huangbo here."
"You two may now ordain me. The two men respectfully descended.
Three days later, Puhua came up and asked, "What did you say three days ago, Master? Linji struck him. Three days later, Ke Fu came up and asked.

"Three days ago, why did the Master strike Puhua? Linji also struck him. The Teacher said, "Old man Linji, establishing the Yellow Cliff (Huangbo) school in such a manner can truly be called 'cutting through nails and severing iron.
That Puhua and Ke Fu were thus brought to their knees was also a model for all time.
But tell me, when the Korean monk (Xinluohan) raises this case in such a way, where does his intent lie?"
"In the past, no one recognized his meritorious labors; it was only now that his epoch-making achievements were duly discussed.
Chan Master Mì of Huating, a native of the Jīn clan of Róngchāng, shaved his head and donned the monastic robes while still a child. He was profoundly silent and lived with simplicity.
Having spent many years investigating the Way under the late Master Mitoku of Tiantong, one day he attained thorough penetration upon hearing the sound of a bell.
In the autumn of the *Renwu* year, he encountered Master Lin, who succeeded him on the seat; their karmic conditions were in perfect accord, and he was thus granted formal certification (*inka*).

He first opened the Dharma at Qizhen Temple and later moved to Chuanzzi Hermitage in Huating. Entering the hall, he said: "The bright pearl of Zhenhai is revealed at every moment; the precious blade of spiritual sharpness..."
The sword manifests before one day after day. Since it is thus inherently perfected from the beginning, why need one draw lines on the ground to limit oneself?
Nevertheless, in a forge there is still much dull iron, while at the door of a skilled physician, the sick are most effectively healed.

Therefore, those who have long attended superior practitioners need not weary themselves by chasing shadows; however, those beginners who have not yet awakened must suddenly exert their utmost vigor and brilliance. Suddenly—

There you slip your foot and fall to the ground, smashing your very face of birth. You must encounter a person whose hands and feet are like those of a pig-eating dog—one who grinds east and grinds west;
once he has made this single error, his eyes will be revealed throughout his entire body.

Only then can you take the broken cord and pass it through the nostrils of the monks of the world. When you reach this point, the Buddhas of the three periods stand in the lower wind, and all the patriarchs...
Even the Patriarch of the past could not peer beside you; yet even reaching such a state is still not the fundamental practice of a monk.
What, then, is fundamental practice? Pine cones burn until they are red-hot and sizzling; their ears are scorched and their faces turn yellow.
On the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall: dragon lanterns vie for prominence, smoke-trees scatter blossoms, and fire spews from human faces—how painful!
"Penetrating Śākyamuni—just at such a time as this, where is the ancient Buddha Dīpaṃkara? With shoulders touching and arms draped over one another, they form a crowd of drunkards;
at midnight, amidst the sound of pipes and songs, they are supported home. His mission of seeking alms was nearly complete when he was implicated by a certain incident. The Master sighed and said:
"Fundamentally, there is nothing to do. Why is it so? He then asked his attendant, "Is it noon? The attendant replied, "It has already passed.
On the following day, he asked again, "Is it noon? The attendant replied, "It is exactly noon. Thereupon, he spoke this verse:
"When I returned home yesterday, the time had not yet come; Today I return home at the very hour of noon. Dreams, illusions, and empty flowers cannot be retained; This mind is able..."
"How many people know [this]? Having spoken thus, he sat upright and passed away. Consequently, everyone along the way was filled with reverence and admiration;
when the fourfold assembly from near and far heard of it, they wept. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on the southern slope of Qishan in Yixing.
Chan Master Xiyi of Fengxue Yun'e was the son of the Chen family of Ziyang.

Upon observing a corpse rotting and emitting a foul odor, he was moved by the realization of the impermanence of all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) and resolved to leave the household life. His parents opposed this, so he immediately began a fast. After a long time, they finally consented.

He then went to a venerable elder to receive the tonsure and shaved head, traveling extensively to visit various masters (*jñānin*), all of whom provided him with encouragement and advancement. In his later years, he entered Tiantai.
He visited Master Linye Qi and asked, "The staff-tip that turns things around is rarely met with a true知音 (zhinian);
when meeting on a narrow path, how can one communicate? Qi replied, "Clouds and mist lock the thousand mountains. The Master said, "Before reaching Tiantai, one cannot help but harbor doubts."

Wang Qi said, "To take a ladle and measure the ocean is to recklessly attempt to fathom its depth. The Master said, "If it were not for the path of the woodcutter, how could one reach Ge Hong’s dwelling?

Wang Qi said, "The peaks and ridges rise in exquisite beauty; the bird-path is difficult to traverse. The Master then gave a shout. Wang Qi struck him. Thereupon, he attended closely at the Master's seat.
One day, while accompanying the Master on a mountain excursion, Wang Qi asked, "Mountains, rivers, the great earth, light and darkness, form and emptiness—what do these have to do with you?"
"Are they the same or different? The Master said, "If they are the same, they are all the same; if they are different, they are all different.

Qiji scolded him with a stern look, saying, "You speak the principles well enough. The Master had no reply. Qiji immediately grabbed him by the chest and said, "Setting aside 'all' and 'different,' 'same' and 'different,' speak quickly!
Speak quickly! The Master stood there lost in thought. Qiji suddenly gave him a shove toward a precipice. The treasure within his breast—*
Alas! It was as vast and clear as ice melting away. Looking back at what I had previously attained, it was like but a single drop in the great ocean.
He then spoke a verse: "Enough, enough, enough! Rest, rest, rest! Lying across and sleeping supine upon the mountain mounds, I turn my body and crush the very bones of empty space;
The myriad phenomena and all that exists smile and nod their heads. He presented this to the Abbot, who then granted him formal certification (*inka*).
The thirty-seventh generation descendant of Dajian [Huineng], Chan Master Shiguo Hui (石谷慧), lineage heir of Xiangya Ting (象崖珽), was the son of the Jiang family of Hezhou.
Although he mastered the scriptural teachings, his aspirations lay in the Chan school. After two...
Ten years passed, and the knot of doubt was finally unraveled. Having received the transmission from Master Xiangya, he subsequently opened a Dharma center at Yunshih Leishui.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The lamp of wisdom blazes across the earth; the flames of letters illuminate the heavens. The colors of the rain intermingle in radiance, its light pervading beyond the kalpas."
I ask you all, do you understand? If you understand, then with both nostrils hanging down and eyebrows arched like the character "八" (eight), you extend a single hand at the proper time;
upon a bottomless boat, you take up the oar and seize the rudder, wandering through the bitter sea of suffering to deliver all sentient beings.
When there is not even one more being left to deliver, you then join hands with the old fellow with the big belly and laugh heartily. Only then will you know that there is something else.
Truly wealthy and noble. Should it not yet be so, simply look at this mountain monk’s staff: ten thousand strings of cash wrapped around its waist, riding a crane up to Yangzhou.
Later, he resided at the Songhe Chan Temple in Fo Shan, Chengdu.

On the first day of the fourth month of the Gengzi year, manifesting a slight ailment, he spoke a verse to bid farewell to the assembly: "A decrepit, solitary, and stubborn stone man; returning again to the Sahā world for a thousand..."
Ten thousand times over. His coming was like a spring breeze upon withered wood; his going was like a flash of lightning in the autumn moon.
At times he slept peacefully within the pores of all Buddhas; at times he appeared upon the trees of swords and mountains of blades.
With a single shout across ten thousand miles of clouds and sky, he was no ordinary trampling or piercing. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
Chan Master Yúnfù Zhì of Guīyáng was a native of Qūxiàn. In his youth, he left the household life at Shuǐyuè Ān.
He first studied under Xuěmén and later received formal certification from Upādhyāya Xiàngyá. Ascending the hall, he said: "The Three Yangs are in motion; all things are renewed.
The spring is mild and the scenery is exquisite; the frozen ice of the azure pool has already melted. Everywhere there is song and joy, as all offer congratulations on the New Year."
Section. As for the phrase, "Not involving the new or the old," how would you handle it? "Clearly and vividly, there is neither past nor present; where in heaven and earth does it not shine?
On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "The first month of spring is still cold. Auspicious snow blankets the world in silver; droplets freeze into ice.
Mountains and rivers transform into jade and crystal. Have you not heard it said: 'When it is cold, let it kill with cold'?"

"O Acharya! In the heat, the heat will kill you, Acharya! If you can penetrate through to a place that is neither cold nor hot, you will be able to cast off the net and transcend the three realms, no longer moved by cold or heat;
only then will you be a person at leisure beyond the mundane world. If this is not yet so, then everywhere the bright lamps shine resplendently.

Take heed, Zen practitioners, look with clear eyes! [End of] the Retreat (Xiezhi) *Note: This text is a traditional Chan (Zen) discourse, likely from a "Lecture on the Opening of the Retreat" (Jieshang). It uses paradoxical language to challenge the practitioner toward a state of non-duality.*
In the Hall, the furnace is opened for the ninety-day retreat. Every monk seeks its essential core; the fierce tongs and hammers do not spare him.
Should he hesitate or open his mouth, they strike him head-on. His mother-born nostrils are pulled up to his lips.
The matter beneath his heels is as clear as the sun. Today, having untied the mouth of the sack, he goes east and west at will. But tell me, Qing—
"What about Elder Liang? [The Master] slung his staff across his shoulder and said, "Originally a man of the mountains, I am now returning to the mountains.
Chan Master Yushan Rui of Dongshan in Qujing Prefecture was a native of Guang'an; by nature he was serene and simple, remaining aloof from the world.
[He] succeeded to the Dharma under Chan Master Xiangyai Ting. Entering the hall, [he said]: "A dry dung pellet.
He hurls a lump of iron out of thin air, shattering everyone’s hot face-skin; one is left with nothing but a mouth unable to explain it. A barefoot Persian enters the Great Tang;
the carp of the Eastern Sea has already leaked the secret. Pearls are scattered from within the purple silk curtains, making the barbarian monk laugh to death."
His teeth were missing. Looking left and right, he said, "Where is the True Man of No Rank to be found? Ascending the hall, he said: "Investigate apart from mind, intellect, and consciousness;
smash through the iron gate. The mud ox bellows forth from the sea; it collides with and topples Mount Sumeru.
Cutting off the path of the mundane and the holy, the void lacks a single foot. Go ask Old Yunmen—this foul water is splashed directly upon your head! [He spoke thus] amidst the assembly.
"Is there anyone who has not been struck by the 'poisonous water'? *Pah!* "All day long you go about indulging in greed and anger. The tip of the staff is sharp and brings life to people's hearts;
it is just like a purple-bearded Hu dog, baring its fangs and claws without mercy. You discerning Zen practitioners, look and see through this!
Shout loudly and curse this wild fox spirit, who stole Yunmen’s dry dung-pellet, failing to distinguish between what is noble and what is base."
Who would swallow what is base? One’s family meal does not accept the fires of the human world; for smelting, one must rely on the furnace, bellows, and anvil.
With copper heads and iron jaws, it is difficult to bring down a beak. A lion yawns and stretches, leaping out from the herd. At Changle Monastery in Yunnan, he ascended the hall and said:

"A thousand hands and a thousand eyes—this is Great Compassion. It shines through all that is right and wrong in the human world. Fully wielding the axis of the earth, it transcends the ten thousand phenomena."

The Master’s stringed instrument resonates through Mount Sumeru. Is there anyone among the assembly who can respond to this occasion? Looking left and right, he planted his staff and descended from the seat.
Self-Appraisal: Face-to-face, there is no private intent. A staff reaching to the vast heavens; when one encounters the occasion, a blow across the head.
Both "touching" and "turning away" are transcended; neither sages nor ordinary beings are spared. Seizing and releasing according to the moment, he opens the heart-mind. I ask you: [He strikes.]
"Who is it? It is Master Yushan. His Dharma words turn the celestial pivot and revolve the terrestrial axis; they capture tigers and rhinoceroses and distinguish dragons from snakes.
Only a truly vital and dynamic man of great capacity can ensure that every phrase meshes perfectly and every function resonates in harmony.
Furthermore, tell me: since antiquity, who has ever been able to take up this matter?
In the summer of the Guihai year, while residing at Dongshan Temple in Qujing Prefecture, Yunnan, at the age of seventy-four, he manifested a slight ailment and was interred at that same mountain.

Lingra Chang, the Dharma heir of Chan Master Zizhi Zang, was the son of the Zhang family from Baxian. Having shaved his head at Mount Da’e since childhood, he attended upon Master Lingra for many years, serving as his attendant.
One day, he received formal certification. Subsequently, he opened a dharma hall at Zhulin Tang. Upon ascending the hall, he sat.

Severing the tongues of all people under heaven, leveling the ground yet remaining solitary, perilous, and steep; opening wide the precious treasury of the *Cintāmaṇicakra*, where environment and wisdom are spontaneously manifest.
Taking the one mind as immeasurable minds, he demonstrates that one dharma is all dharmas.

Suddenly causing every person to be free from delusion, he reveals that all phenomena are primordially perfected. A thousand or ten thousand years, the ancient cypress remains ever fresh; for billions of...
The flowing golden light is veiled and reflected. Although it is thus, alas, those who understand are rarely encountered.

What is it to be one who understands? "After Xiatang has passed, there is no one to know him; who would have thought that Master Yuan would come today? He ascended the hall and held up his whisk, saying:
"High above, it has no exterior; deep below, it has no limit. It is the root of humans and devas, the profound source of the patriarchs and Buddhas—even for insects and moths."
From grasses, trees, birds, beasts, dragons, and fish, there is none that does not receive this majestic radiance and perceive its original face.
Only the bamboo grove stands uniquely detached, transcending all common currents; it manifests speech where there is no speech and brings forth function within the useless.

It can cause the Demon King to fold his hands in submission and cause those who wander like clouds and water to turn their hearts toward it. At every step, it clarifies the mechanism of the original source; at every point, it reveals the fundamental nature.
To manifest a marvelous and extraordinary matter. But what is this marvelous and extraordinary matter?
*Chan*. Xuebi Luan was a dharma successor of Guiyang Yuesong Yi Chan Master; he was the son of the Song family from Ba County. He left home at the age of twenty and studied under Poxue He.
Furthermore, having broken through the lacquer bucket, he received certification from Master Xuebi and began teaching at Mouni Chan Monastery.

Upon ascending the hall, he said: "The precious sword that shaves hair has long been hidden within its scabbard; today it is drawn forth—dare any dare meet its edge? The Demon Kings are utterly defeated, and the hundred monsters hide their tracks.
All Buddhas of the three periods stand downwind; as for the one flower and five petals, to whom shall they be entrusted?"
The Essential Principle: Throughout the ten ages of past and present, it flows and circulates as one. At this very moment, the rivers are clear and the seas are calm;
the myriad nations come to submit. In every village, songs are sung and feasts are held; in every household, they whistle under the moon and chant by the wind.

But tell me, when the new Elder arrives at the monastery, is there anyone who can join in the song? "Lifting my head to gaze beyond the heavens—who else is there like me? [He] ascended the hall and said:
Yesterday, white snow piled up before the mountains; this morning, a clear breeze rises upon my seat. It is neither existent nor empty;
it is the direct manifestation of the supreme school. The stone maiden on the cliff-edge has just awakened from her sleep; she claps her hands and laughs with inexhaustible joy.
"Tell me, Great Assembly, what is she laughing at? [The Master] looks left and right and says: "She is laughing because this mountain monk does not begrudge his eyebrows."
Ascending the hall, he offered incense to extend his auspicious prayers for the current Emperor: The sun of Shun shines with lofty brilliance, illuminating the vast wilderness;
Only the azure heavens remain, free from a single speck of cloud. Ice melts and walls crumble, leaving no room for conceptual deliberation.

Even stones and rubble rejoice; grasses, trees, and insects all emit their light. The Eye of the True Dharma flows on in secret intimacy; The flame is sustained in succession, spreading far and wide. [To those] who meet this opportunity...
Exerting himself with vigor, he can let out a lion’s roar. Having first entered the West Mountain arena for selecting Buddhas, he did not yield to Master Zhang who personally attended Mazu;
he was truly the same as that madman Linji. Seizing the tiger’s head and grasping its tail, his Three Mysteries and Three Essentials spread throughout all quarters.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "I am forty-seven years old; the springtime passes as swiftly as a split arrow. I am ashamed to lack the talent to respond to the world, yet I have found benefit in dwelling upon this mountain.
My thatched cottage consists of only two or three rooms, secure and most secure. Fortunately, it is situated within a great golden fortress, further augmented by the power of external protection.
As the laws and regulations are properly enforced, demons and monsters have all vanished from sight. The nine-tufted phoenix chick’s wings and feathers are now complete. Gold...

The Lion of Hair immediately turned back and leaped about; those who were chirping cried out, and those who were howling roared, shaking heaven and earth with a great resonance and brilliantly illuminating the sun of the Buddha.
Above and below the heavens, he alone is called Honored; in the mundane and supramundane worlds, who can oppose him?

At such a time as this, the four seas sing praises as they submit to his sacred transformation; the myriad kingdoms present their tributes and all universally acknowledge themselves as subjects. To the assembly: Long rains have not ceased; the crags and peaks...
In the deep shadows, white clouds gather at the door; the weeds in the courtyard grow ever deeper. How should a patch-robed monk beneath the forest trees respond?
He then lets out a shout: "The void shatters to pieces; the great earth sinks level. In an instant, a red sun is sent forth, its brilliance once again pervading heaven and earth.
Yet, how does one speak the phrase that belongs to neither sun nor rain? A few fragments of white cloud.
Transversely across the world—among these, who is the one who emerges? Addressing the assembly while ill: I am fifty-seven years old; I have contributed nothing to benefit the Dharma-gate.
To pay my respects at Shangtiandong, I am pressed by both old age and illness. This manifestation of illness is not actually illness; to whom can this meaning be explained?
Fortunately, my spirit remains undiminished, and my sinews and bones still possess strength. With a shout, I burst through the clouds atop the ridge. *Beng!*

When he emerged, the light of the sun shone forth, its brilliance penetrating the four quarters and its radiant splendor illuminating both present and past. "Do not occupy the stupas of sentient beings;
why must you laboriously seek out land? He cast [the writing] into the great river, where fish and dragons were satiated with one full meal. Having thus cast down his brush, he passed away.
Minju (Minsu) was a Dharma successor of the Chan Master Eodae Tae (Ear-toxicated Tae) of Nampu Cheonwon-sa. Born to the Xu family, he was of imposing stature and profound breadth of mind;

he was not concerned with trivial matters. His spirit was concentrated and his demeanor serene and detached, such that he remained aloof from worldly affairs. The Old Man [Baegun] often called him "The Sack Man" (Budaeji).
The Dharma successor of Venerable Heshang Yu Minsu ascends the hall and says: "The great sun overflows the eyes; ten thousand *li* are not hung with a single cloud.
The autumn waters are clear and limpid; a single abyss can contain all waters. The dragon roars and mist rises; the tiger howls and the wind is born.
Peering at the well, peering at the donkey; the Sun-Face and Moon-Face; the thorny chestnut and the diamond ring; the dry dung pellet and the three pounds of flax—let it all go!"
Standing to one side, he directly smeared excrement upon the Buddha’s head. As for the one who untied the bell beneath the lion’s chin—who is this person?
"Without leaving this very place, it is eternally serene; seek it and you will know that you cannot see it. Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat:

Today is the fifteenth day of the fifth month. A gentle breeze pervades the earth everywhere; in every household, curtains and blinds are rolled up, and in every door, there is the sound of flutes and songs.
Regarding the communal dance: Wufeng did not act like this at all. He let loose the reckless monk; striking east and knocking west, he concealed his sharpness and left his tongue tied.
Striking the bamboo and pointing at the flower, he vanished his traces and hid his footsteps. Thus, he roamed freely through the universe, wearing horns and holding up his head.
Were it not for the fierce hammer and tongs, how could such a strategy have been displayed? (He strikes once with his staff.)
He said: "On this auspicious festival of the Lantern Festival, everyone sees it; yet who clearly knows this matter? Entering the hall, he said:

"The three great collections of the Buddha’s teachings—though Gautama exhausted every stratagem—were of no use when brought forth. Laozi’s five thousand words—though he performed every trick—were likewise useless when applied."

Why must you labor so hard to contemplate? If you can realize it prior to the time of Vipaśyin Buddha, it is like a silver mountain or an iron wall shattered by a single blow and cast into the vast ocean, where not even a grain of rice remains. Startled, the earthen ox bellows upon the water’s surface;
the wooden horse chases the whistling wind. Let the waves rise and the boat tower; let the wind blow and the grass bow. Why is this? Because along both banks, the reeds are in bloom.
It is entirely like snow; the stars and moon across the heavens are white as silver.
Chan Master Tianyin Chong was the son of the Bi family of Dajian.

Having traveled extensively to study under various masters, he finally attained thorough enlightenment under Master Minshu and inherited his Dharma lineage. He resided at Taiping Chan Monastery in Langxi Commandery, Sinnan Prefecture, Guizhou.

The Abbot ascended the hall. "Throughout the ages, when the sages appeared in the world, they investigated nothing but the One Mind. They established the five schools, transmitting directly and pointing straight at the source.
Those who cling to words and linger in phrases bury their own family treasure; those who employ staffs and shouts have not yet penetrated the root.

To speak in such a manner is to leave it sticking to the lips and catching on the teeth. Even if you were to realize it, it would already be a groundless matter. He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the state of being present?"
[Zhi] attempted to resolve this with the "Three Mysteries" (sanxuan) and his staff, but the Master struck him with a shout.

Zhi advanced and said, "Striking is not without purpose, but what is 'seizing the person but not seizing the environment'? The Master said, "Under the staff there is the patience of non-arising; who would let you off when the moment arrives?
Zhi asked, "What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'? The Master said, "Since the time Mount Hua was split asunder, it has been yielded to this very day."
Juling advanced and asked, "What is 'both the person and the environment being taken away'? The Master set down his staff and said, "There is no need to brandish spears and lances;
let us sing songs of celebration for the Great Peace. Juling asked, "What is 'neither the person nor the environment being taken away'? The Master said:
The seas are calm and the rivers clear as we sing of the Sun of Shun; the common people and their children rejoice in the Heaven of Yao. A student asked, "What is the first mystery?
The Master said, "I shall speak it for you from the tip of my staff. The student asked, "What is the second mystery?
The Master said, "The tongue is already at the edge of the teeth and lips. The student asked, "What is the third mystery? The Master said, "Linji."

[The student] did not understand the meaning. He spoke in vain before the Master’s eyes. The student asked: "What is the first essential? The Master said: "Meeting [him], one is too weary to open one's mouth;
the staff has already arrived. The student asked: "What is the second essential? The Master said: "A single blow opens the crown of the head;
for a thousand sages, there is no further mystery. The student asked: "What is the third essential? The Master said: "The feet are worn thin by the straw sandals."
"Kuan! You have traversed every path in Chang'an. The student stepped forward and asked, "The Three Mysteries and Three Essentials have been pointed out by the Master;
as for the ultimate vehicle of the ancestral school, what is it? The Master said, "Be careful not to fall into their traps. He then continued: "Linzhi’s glorious reputation arose in Hebei;
The fundamental tenets of Taiping were established at Langxi. Do not say that this day is not that same day; True-bone descendants and kinsmen receive the highest capacity."
He then threw down his staff and said, "The mountain monk makes this announcement: Do you recognize the immovable spear and banner of the new Taiping?
Do you understand the three mysteries as its weapons and armor? Without even raising the tongs and hammer, do you grasp how he integrates Dongshan’s five ranks of ruler and subject?
Responding to conditions to provoke realization, does he open up Yunmen’s 'Single Character' barrier? Carrying his sword at his side, has he sliced through Yangshan’s nine [ranks]?"
Are these sixteen kinds of perfect marks anything other than utterly devoid of identity or difference? Do they not transcend the Dharma-eye and the doctrinal gateways of the six characteristics?

If you can penetrate and break free from this, you will personally see this old monk; only then will you recognize the courtyards of the five schools and no longer doubt the provisional and ultimate teachings of the thousand sages.
(He lets out a shout and descends from his seat.)
National Teacher Kōkoku Jō was the son of the Yang family of Zhongzhou. Having traveled extensively throughout various regions, he returned to Xun and succeeded Master Min as his heir.
He first resided at Sengsheng Temple and subsequently moved to the Imperial Capital. King Shuncheng invited him to reside at the Zhenru Chan Monastery at Baita.
Upon ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the Prince at Birth? The Master said, "Directly facing one another is most intimate. [The monk] stepped forward.
[The student] asked, "What is the Prince Born by Transformation? The Master said, "Shouldering the sun and moon across.
[The student] asked further, "What is the Prince Born at Dawn? The Master said, "Arranged in full array upon the platter.

[The student] asked further, "What is the Prince Born Last? The Master said, "Hidden and manifest, beyond measure. [The student] asked further, "What is the Prince Born Within? The Master said, "The copper tally and the iron peg."
The student said, "The Prince’s five stages have been pointed out by the Master; what is the matter with ascending the seat right now?
The Master said, "A blink of the eye reveals the core intent; turning the head expands the orthodox lineage. The student said, "If that is so, then the preaching of the Dharma is already finished.

The Master said, "This profound intention shall age together with Heaven and Earth; this pure name shall forever share the fragrance of the Way-wind. Looking left and right, he said, "The eight wildernesses are at peace."
Quiescence. During the reign of the Buddha-Mind Emperor, when the four seas were clear and peaceful, the worthy kings and great ministers had deep faith in the Triple Gem.
They caused the ancestral Way to flourish and upheld the spirit of the school. As for the elder Cheng, he is dull-witted and ignorant; there is no Chan to be practiced and no Dharma to be preached.
He only remembers that in the past, at Mount Kongwang, there was a "Song of Herding an Ox. Now, he [offers it] to people...
The Celestial Multitude brought it forth before him. With a single roar of majestic authority, he said: "If you can realize it here, there is no need for the toil of traveling on foot.
If this is not yet the case, you must buy more straw sandals before you may succeed."
Chan Master Qianling Chisongling was the son of the Han family from Tongchuan. At the age of fifteen, he constantly reflected that this floating world turns in an instant to emptiness;
he subsequently entered the mountains to practice, wearing clothes of grass and eating food from trees, remaining composed whether in pleasure or pain. He frequently studied the Avatamsaka Sūtra.
Upon reaching the "Chapter on the Manifestation of Signs" [of the Lotus Sutra], the World-Honored One was preaching the Dharma to the devas. The devas constantly hear the sound of the celestial drum;
this sound does not come from the four intermediate directions, above, or below, and it is neither born nor extinguished. "The Dharma I preach is also like this.
Unconsciously, he lost his voice and attained realization. He traveled to Longshan on the Sea of Following Righteousness and relied upon Master Minshu for a long time.
Thus he bestowed his prediction of enlightenment. Residing at the Shou-shi Chan Monastery in Guiyang Prefecture, he ascended the hall for the opening of the retreat.

To serve as a cause for the conditions of transcending the world, he established guest and host according to the occasion, avoiding the clichés of conventional Chan and nurturing tigers with horns. "Be careful of your footsteps."
Do not be muddled along the way. When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, it is out of parental affection that I fail to notice my child’s ugliness.

Is there anyone here who recognizes the underlying intent and possesses the true eye? After a long silence, he let out a shout. Ascending the hall, he spoke on the occasion of the lifting of the retreat restrictions: "The conditions of the mechanism [of awakening] are fundamentally without words or phrases."
Wiping away the moon and donning the wind, they go and stay according to conditions. Singing out the song of non-arising, they beat the drum of Heyishan.
Each and every one enters perfect clarity, never leaning upon another’s gate. Such travelers as these all perform the lion’s dance;
when they emerge in the future, they will surely be the masters among masters.
Chan Master Jichu Shang of Kaiyuan Temple in Kuizhou Prefecture was the son of the Chen family from Yidu in Huguang.
At the age of twenty, he paid his respects to the elder master Yingxu and received the tonsure. He entered Fenghuang Mountain to dwell in seclusion, vowing: "If I do not realize the illumination..."
He never descended from the mountain again. Subsisting on wood and drinking from mountain streams for nearly five years, one day he sat wearily and upright; before he knew it, midnight had passed.
Suddenly, as if a mountain were collapsing with a roar, he was startled until sweat poured down his entire body. In that moment, he was suddenly unimpeded.

From then on, he no longer harbored doubts regarding the tongues of the elder patriarchs throughout the world. He subsequently descended the mountain and went to the presence of the Elder Master Pogre at Shuanggui to complete his training.
[He was] fully endowed [with these qualities]. Later, he studied under Master Minshu of Ciyun and received his seal of approval (*inka*).

In the Jiyou year of the Kangxi era, Governor Xiong of Kuifeng and Commander Ma invited him to reside at Kaiyuan Chan Temple. He ascended the hall and said: "The clouds follow the dragon; the wind follows the tiger.
A single path of cold radiance pervades heaven and earth. The sunflower inclines toward the sun; the willow catkins dance with the wind. New growth..."
Old age has arrived; for now, one must respond to the occasion. One can only steer with the wind and release the hawk upon seeing the hare.
Sometimes it is so: in the human realm and the heavens above. Sometimes it is not so: not even a drop of water can pass through. Suddenly grasping his staff, he said:
"Tell me, how do you speak that single phrase which cuts off the vital ford? He gave a shout and said: "The public office does not admit even a needle; the private house..."
He was proficient in both vehicles [of Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna].

Dànzhú Mìmí (澹竹密密), the dharma heir of Wànshòu Xiǎoyuán Jì (萬壽曉元濟) Chán Master, was the son of the Liu family of Lóngchāng. While reading the *Dàzhū Lù* (Record of Dàzhū), he came upon the passage beginning with "The eyes are like..."

Miaoyou of Shaolin resolved to leave the household life. He first studied under the Patriarch Baizhang to realize the essential meaning of the teachings, and later received formal certification from Master Dan.
He established the Dharma at Wanshou Chan Temple. Entering the hall, he held up his staff and said:
"Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja, there was this news; the thousand hands of Great Compassion could not reach it. After King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja, there was none..."
A message: all people in the great earth are stumbling and cannot rise. At this very moment, the eyes of Maheśvara are gouged out, and the nostrils of everyone are pierced through.
But how can one speak of it clearly? After a long silence, he said: "The mountain monk commits a transgression. Ascending the hall:
On the Qingming day of the second month, every thing vies for its own beauty. A hundred flowers bloom in brilliant splendor; the embankment...
The willow drags its smoke straight; everywhere Mañjuśrī appears. At every turn it is Samantabhadra. Suddenly encountering the staff, he bows his head before it.
In one moment, all public evidence has been passed; there is neither faction nor partiality. Since there is neither faction nor partiality, how is one to settle this?
Pointing the staff to the left and looking to the left, pointing to the right and looking to the right, he says: "Family disgrace must not be broadcast abroad."

Small Assembly: The heavens are cold and people are cold; here we huddle together. This living reality requires no contriving. To ward off hunger, one cooks coarse rice; to provide warmth, one uses dry firewood.
In every thing and every circumstance, all is naturally harmonious. My way is simply this: a single state of equanimity.

Sitting dazed and still beneath the precipitous cliff, I provoke the falling flowers from heaven to come rushing to the earth. At such a time as this— *Note: The term "small assembly" (xiǎocān) refers to a brief informal teaching given by a Chan master to a small group of disciples.*
Furthermore, how shall one settle the matter with all of you? [Zhaozhou] struck his staff and said: "Beneath the staff, a single wheel of red; clouds and mist gather in the vast sky.
A tortoise drills through a wall; the pillar laughs at the lantern. He laughed heartily and descended from the seat.

Ziwei, originally from the Wu family of Jianzhou, was the dharma heir of Chan Master Chechen. In his middle years, he left the secular world and took the tonsure under Master Dan of Bailu, where he deeply realized the essential points of the Dharma.
He subsequently returned to Mount Ziwai and composed a verse, saying: "The sun has risen from the east since time immemorial;

It returns to set behind the western hills. When it is the hour of Yin (Tiger), simply rise early; When it is the hour of Hai (Boar), bend your limbs to sleep. In its application, there is something [to be known]."
The Master Zi was not affiliated with any school in either ancient or modern times. At another time, he will turn his body around and leap out from the den of the Lion King.
Caotang Hou, a Chan Master of the same rank, was the son of the Wang family of Rongchang; he received the Dharma succession from Master Dan of Bailu.
Residing at Caotang Temple in Jingguan, he ascended the hall and said: "Spring returns once more, and all things are renewed.
In vain do I try to explain my inner treasure to others. If there is a tendon in the eye, one can see forms; Who is there within the ear that can hear? The fish swims without stirring the water;
The bird flies without clinging to the clouds. I strike the drum of Heyuan; I lift up the broken sand bowl. He then made a gesture as if supporting something with his hand.
Shi said: "Look, look! Residing at Kaigang Temple in Jiancheng City, I ascend the hall. In the depths of the Jian River, waves strike the heavens;
clusters of fishing fires dot the fishing boats. With lines cast from the tips of poles and fine bait dangling, where can the golden-scaled fish hide as they break through the waves?"

Holding his staff, he made the gesture of casting a line and asked, "Is there anyone? Is there anyone? He subsequently resided at the Dharma seat of Caotang, where he was honored with the title "Master Youlao.
Chongyin Chan Master was the son of the Ding family of Yuzhou. Having left the secular world from childhood, he was profoundly silent and solemn in demeanor.

His spiritual capacity accorded with that of the Venerable Dàn of Dàsuí, who then granted him certification. He resided at Cishòu in Xīndū, where the two lay practitioners Zhāng and Zhào [served him].

The Dharma robe was delivered; he ascended the hall and said: "With bitter resolve and weary body, like a wild crane dwelling in the clouds; tilling the clouds and hoeing the moon, one has long since forgotten artifice.
I am ashamed to lack the strength to proclaim my family’s disgrace, yet I truly rejoice that you have worn this soiled robe for many years.
Picking up the robe, he said, "This is the new one. What is the old one? After a long silence, he said, "Ask Zhang Gong and Zhao Gong. He resided in Chengdu.
**At the Grass Hut.** Ascending the hall: Shouldering the *zhilu* staff, he enters the grass hut; dragons gallop and tigers bound in the midst of spring sunshine.
Lacking the virtue of coolness, he merely illuminates his ancestors; leading water to irrigate the vegetables, he awaits the future master.

**Ascending the Hall on New Year’s Day:** Having resided in the grass hut for two springs now, the expansion of yang and the contraction of yin are difficult to evaluate. Who presides over the pivot of creation? The seven-foot crow...
The Petition and Credential.
Baoguang was a native of Anfu who studied under Chan Master Conggu. In his youth, he was immersed in the midst of military turmoil; though he drifted through life, he possessed great ambition.
He delighted in the subtle and precise forging of Bai Lu Dan, and thus, having attained self-conviction, he took him as his successor to the Dharma. The fourfold assembly welcomed him.
The Master presided over Baoguang Temple in the new capital. Ascending the hall, he said: "At this very moment, there is not a speck of dust.

Who can recognize the person of old? Majestic and imposing, face-to-face, there is no concealment. To deliberate or reflect is to be ten thousand miles away in the clouds. He struck his staff and said:
Utterly independent and vibrantly alive; clarity is like the bright sun illuminating heaven and earth.
When a monk personally realizes this, the wondrous interplay of eye and sound, ear and form, is beyond description.
Chan Master Daoyan of Zhushan, a Dharma heir of Boshan Lai, was the son of Shen of Dazhu. Having lost his mother in childhood, he donned the monastic robes while still a youth.
He traveled south with Ziying, seeking the essential core of the mind. Consequently, upon reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he realized the principle of sealing the mind; body and mind... [the world].
The realm suddenly became empty. He then said: "I have come to this pavilion as one who dwells within the mind; I have spoken to people of the age, yet they remain not yet clear.

Having finished his lecture, he went to the White Gate to seek out Chan Master Bolu Shanlai, where he was invested with the office of Xitang. One day, the master gave him a seal of certification, saying:
A single branch protrudes crosswise from Mount Boshan; it is hidden within your own mind. He immediately conferred the full precepts upon him and bestowed the name Daoyan.
Later, he moved to Dufeng on Jiangpu, where the Master renamed it Zhongding Chan Monastery. He ascended the hall and said: "Yuan, heng, li, zhen—these are the virtues of Qian.
Weiyin is the origin of all Buddhas; Yingguang is the beginning of all Patriarchs. From the origin to the end, [the transmission] was bestowed..."
Marking the beginning of the year and the dawn of the three seasons, the imperial wind has opened the reign of fortune;

both court and countryside are renewed. Holding up his staff, he said: "The Sovereign, from this very place, secures the state and stabilizes the nation, ascending to peace while reclining with folded hands.

The high officials, from this very place, assist in transformation and nourishment, harmonizing the flavors of the imperial cauldron. This is the total presentation of Linji’s mystery and essentials. He illuminated [the truth].
In their simultaneous application, Dongshan’s subtle resonance harmonizes ruler and subject; his profound traces follow the path of birds.

In the circular pivot of Miaoxin and Daowu, father and son share the same root as they wield the powers of killing and giving life. In Yunmen’s direct pointing through his glance, the gateway is lofty and steep.

In Fayan’s secret employment of form and sound, the mind-dharma is perfectly luminous. Though the five schools have different doors, they enter the inner sanctum together. This is the single phrase that unites their source.
"How would you say it? He struck his staff and said: "The three heavens and five elements are harmoniously beautiful throughout the world;
a single branch of plum blossoms releases spring upon the mountain ridges."—Recorded by Qinglong Baiyu, Dharma heir.
Chan Master Ziju of Jianfu Temple in Jingzhao was the son of the Liao family of Zuomin. He received the Dharma lineage from Master Baiyu. While ascending the hall, he said:
"Holding fast to heaven and earth, never letting go; the great furnace and bellows fan a glowing red.

All the myriad phenomena of the universe are cast together in the crucible—this is to force the living snake to transform into a dragon. Suddenly raising his whisk, he said: "The Great Man (Shang Daren). Upon his head..."
There is the blue sky; beneath its feet there is not an inch of earth. Walls, tiles, and rubble are the heart of the ancient Buddhas.
Carrying water and dragging mud is the primary truth. Do you understand? Among these, there is one phrase that can extinguish a thousand calamities and accomplish ten thousand virtues.

There is one phrase adorned with a hundred blessings, wherein not even a speck of dust can stand. There is one phrase that reaches the ultimate limit of the present moment, yet does not dwell therein.
Pàn. Furthermore, tell me: which phrase is it? [Ni-女+口]. Ascending the hall: White hair grows upon the back of empty space; one pulls out a strand, then another.
A stone woman twists jade thread within the realm; a wooden boy passes a golden needle beyond the heavens.

Woven is an ancient brocade containing the image of spring; yet he does not pass the golden needle to others. If you can realize this, you shall become the grandfather of the world after heaven. Then—
"To know that the ancient Buddhas are one's own descendants. O Great Assembly, do you yet know where this pivotal point falls?
Even if one were a transcendent genius of extraordinary spirit who could span heaven and earth, and were to shoulder the True Eye here—at a glance, such a person is still but a 'Cloud-Abiding Arhat.
[The Master] raises his whisk and calls to the assembly, saying: 'Do you see it? This single stroke is equal to the Buddhas of the three periods.'"
The Buddha is a fellow practitioner. He harmonizes with the Dharma-realm and all sentient beings to share in their longevity. Śākyamuni does not come first; Maitreya does not come later.
Before even entering the gate of transformation, he has already leaked it out. What is this? It is the unsurpassed mantra; it is the unequaled mantra.

the thirty-seventh generation descendant of Dajian,
heir to the lineage of Zui of Zhangxue.
Chan Master Xisheng was a native of Pingshan. His family had held their office as hereditary military commanders for generations under the supervision of Grand Secretary Liao.

Because he failed in his duties during the invasion by the Chén rebels into Shu, he first shaved his head and donned monastic robes to live in seclusion among the mountains of Suíyáng. Not long after he settled there, he established Huó Ān (Flame Hermitage).

He received full ordination under Master Chang of Niu Mountain. He served as the head administrator of the monastery for several years. When Master Chang accepted an invitation to Yumen, he entrusted the abbacy of the monastery to him.

Upon ascending the hall to open the Dharma, [the Master said: "As for the matters of the ancestors since time immemorial, they sat without occupying the central hall; throughout successive generations, those who promoted compassion did not venture beyond their own doors.
Having no other choice, we must now dig a cave into empty space and open the gate of the second meaning. [He then] raised his staff.
Brandishing the whisk, staff and shouts fly back and forth; sometimes sweeping the ground at the foot of a pine tree, sometimes waiting for someone on the street;

even drawing a bow, holding a forked staff, brandishing a blade sharper than a hair, or rolling a ball—though this mountain monk is but a weed grown in their field, I ultimately do not hide my body here.
*He lets out a shout.* The Four Postures: Walking in the mountains, barefoot, leaving tracks in the mud; climbing stones and running, startling [the deer].
A person of clear-headed awareness dwells in the mountains; they have carved a door into the mountain wall. When guests arrive, they offer them a great radish.
They sit upon the mountain on a meditation cushion worn threadbare; there is no end to its fraying, yet they dare not make a new one.
They lie down upon the mountain with a paper quilt falling over their heads; when they turn over, both ends of the quilt are equally tattered. Singing of this tattered robe, look at this very robe!
Torn to pieces until it is threadbare; its weight is but seven catties. How many people do not make use of it? Mud-pigs and mangy dogs are all gathered therein.
The crippled tortoise and the blind turtle are bound by it. Rain cannot wet it; wind cannot touch it.
When worn out by the sands of dust, it is patched up a thousand times and a hundred times when it tears. Whether noble or base, it is handled by all who pick it up. It has been cut.
A foot-robe (cīvara) is measured according to the person; from its inception, it has never been bleached in the sun. Thrown east and west, it has never been washed. Its stench of sweat is great.
When a monk of the Eastern Land pays three prostrations, his greetings penetrate to the very marrow.
The Venerable Master of the West stands smiling, unable to shake it off. It clearly covers the bare lump of flesh; the "True Person of No Rank" is entirely enveloped within it. Mount [Name].
Throughout his life, Yuanzhao lived with great ease, relying entirely upon this worn-out patchwork robe. Later, he moved to Pingwu, where he passed away.
His remains were collected and interred in a stupa to the left of the ancestral stupa at Zhaojue.
Chan Master Yuechang Liao of Anlong Prefecture was the son of the Mao family of Jiangjin. His mother dreamed of a monk bringing her a peach to eat, after which she conceived.

At the age of sixteen, while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, a state of profound doubt suddenly arose within him. He then informed his mother of his intention to shave his head and dye his robes, and subsequently traveled to consult various venerable masters.
One night, both mind and environment became simultaneously empty, and he attained a sudden, expansive realization. He then paid his respects to Master Zhang at Yumen.
He served as the *karmadāna* (rector). His spiritual affinity with his master was profound. In the winter of the *guisi* year, he began teaching at the Shibo Chan Monastery in Southern Yunnan.

Emperor Yongli, drawn by his reputation for the Way, requested instruction and sought a verse from him. He bestowed upon him the Dharma name Zhenfo and granted him purple robes; the imperial favor was exceedingly generous.
He drew from the state treasury to offer prayers for the nation’s well-being. On two occasions, he presented petitions and verses to the throne, which greatly pleased the Emperor. The Emperor—
The Hall. Heaven cannot cover it; earth cannot support it. It encompasses the five Sumerus and breathes in and out the great trichiliocosm.
Śākyamuni and Maitreya have no place to set their feet; Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have intentions difficult to comprehend.
Birth-and-death and nirvāṇa are cut off; true thusness and buddha-nature are defeated. Even so, regarding this one phrase for opening the hall for the sake of the nation—how is it?

The Way: suddenly transcending the intent of all Buddhas and Patriarchs; I look up and pray for my Sovereign’s ten million years of spring. Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "Nanming has a mouth, yet it is difficult to speak;

sitting and cutting off the thousand deviations is not worth a penny. Now, before this assembly of humans and devas, I lay out the tangled web of teachings, so that you may directly and earnestly awaken to the field of the mind.
The boundless sea of suffering is entirely sweet nectar; the skull-bone suddenly accords with the source. Hereafter...
He moved to Anlong Yuquan Temple. In the winter of the Bingwu year, he manifested a slight ailment and took leave of the assembly.

There were two monks who said they would attend upon the Master as he proceeded ahead; one monk passed away without illness, and after the Master entered parinirvāṇa, the other monk followed in death.
His cremation took place behind Yuquan Temple, and the stupas for the two attendant monks were erected, one on each side.
His worldly age was fifty-three, and his years of monastic seniority were thirty-seven.
Chan Master Changsong Duanni was the son of the Guo family of Neijiang.

While listening to the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he harbored doubts regarding the "ever-abiding true mind" and repeatedly sought its definitive resolution, yet he had not attained entry. He ascended to Baiyun Cave to study under Master Jiansui. One night, he dreamed...

A strange monk appeared, his beard and hair like silver. He clapped his hands three times and said, "Quickly, quickly, recite the Buddha's name! Upon waking, he composed this verse: "In a dream, a strange monk came to me, clapping his hands;
Amitābha is vividly cast upon the platform of my mind. Reflecting back, the path of affection and worldly passions—"
The axe that hews at one's nature was idly applied in its pruning. He then traveled with Yun'e to Panlong Temple in Jiang'an to study under Lao Ren (Old Man Po).

There, he repeatedly inquired into the essential points of the mind within the monastic regulations. Because the rebellion of Jia Yi and others had caused the fall of Shu, he settled in a thatched hut at Guiyang.
In the year Jichou, he received full ordination (*upasaṃpadā*) from Master Zhang at Bauniu Mountain. While attending him, they passed through Yumen Temple, where he studied under Tiantong.

In the *Record of the Secret Patriarchs*, there is a passage concerning "advancing and retreating" that had remained as a blockage in my breast for three years. One day, it was suddenly cleared away like waking from a dream;
all obstructions vanished entirely. I composed a verse, saying: "Between advancing and retreating lie two gates; How many heroes have been stymied therein!
Clearly there is a path leading to the Milky Way— It is neither the 'three before' nor the 'three after. Immediately thereafter, I received his seal of approval (*in-ka*).
Chan opened Longsong Lingfeng Temple. When the assembly requested that he ascend the seat [to preach], he firmly declined, refusing to grant their wish.

He delighted in traveling and sightseeing; wherever he encountered a scene or circumstance, he would spontaneously compose verses. A brief excerpt reads: "The solitary peak presides over the night, the realm vast and silent.

Entering the chamber, the cold wind leaves no time to flee. Dwelling in wealth, one clings to it and loathes its lack; Living in poverty, one maintains simplicity and rejoices in its nobility. [Regarding] delicacies...
How can yellow jing roots compare to this nourishment? Elegant robes cannot match the hundred-knot robe. Universally responding to the myriad affairs, we sing the "Snow" melody;
where sea and sky are one color, our hearts rejoice.
Master Lansheng was the son of the Jian family of Rongchang. From childhood, he maintained profound silence; his character was solitary and lofty.

He resolved to practice Chan and traveled extensively to visit venerable elders. He studied further under Master Zhang of Yumen, where their exchanges were characterized by the mutual resonance of their spiritual faculties.

Later, while staying at Gaoping on Jinchuan, he ascended the hall and said: "Hitherto I have harbored my simplicity and lived in poverty; today, however, I can no longer conceal it. Although it is revealed..."
A myriad of ugly ends; my earnest wish is that you all take care. But what is it you are to take care of? He brushes his sleeves once and says:
"An old fellow from the mountainhead forcibly pushes forward, striding before others without a backward glance. He brings to laughter the wall-facing elder of yore."
"Reduced to utter poverty, his mouth produces nothing but foam. (He lets out a shout.

Later, while visiting his senior master at Zhaojue Temple, he happened to encounter the Provincial Judicial Commissioner Lord Huan’an Hu, Lord Song of Songzhai, and Lord Zhang of Anshan. They requested a verse on the theme of "Sending off the Wild Geese.
The Master responded with alacrity: "You were fortunately born in a year of great abundance; Your movements are free and easy, mingling with the clear sky."
Having fully experienced the peach-blossom rains within my breast, I push aside the willow mists along the embankments.

When weary, my shadow follows as the heavens fade; when vigorous, my mind dwells amidst the white clouds. One truly knows that for the idle traveler beyond the mundane world, the square inch of the heart is as vast as the universe.
Furthermore, I recall the verse on plum blossoms: "The slender frame and icy skin—its essence remains undiminished. How could such wild freedom be confined by ten thousand mountains?"
At dawn, he turned over other objects, manifesting his true heroism; his influence pressed upon the Southern Sea, never desolate. As the wind blew gently, fine birds pecked at remnants;

as the rain fell drizzling, wandering bees gathered and sought nectar. Knowing that you had long held an appointment at the Jade Terrace, you did not fail your initial resolve and were honored by this invitation.
On the eighth day of the first month of the *Yichou* year of the Kangxi era, he manifested a slight ailment; sitting upright, he passed away. His body was cremated.
He collected his remains, including solid seeds as large as soybeans and several like millet grains.
His dharma-heir, Zhuyou Jiabu, brought them back to Gaofeng in Luoyuan, where he erected a stūpa for him. [The Master] was seventy-four years old and had fifty-two years of ordination seniority.
The Great Chan Master Dahanwo of Kunming Xiangguo was the son of the He family from southern Shu. He received the Dharma succession from Master Zhang of Yumen.

On the occasion of a prayer for clear weather, he ascended the hall and said: "A fierce nature gives rise to a rugged, bald wooden trunk; heavenly flowers fall in profusion as the stars of the Dipper and Ox grow cold."
Repeatedly striking the rain-colored world—a thousand autumns of blessing; Shifting the bright radiance—the myriad phenomena find peace. The eight characters open wide the two doors;
Right before one’s eyes, he casts forth the ocean’s vastness. Travelers, do not say the azure heavens are harsh;
Rise your eyebrows and look closely. Ascending the hall on the Buddha’s Birthday: Since the moment he tied his tongue at the Dragon Pool, His countenance has remained peerless under heaven.
This was originally when Guiming first crossed over; it was as if Śacī had left the golden palace.

When those within the jade towers saw him, he appeared truly elegant, still leaning on a crimson silk fan to shield the moon. It is not that men do not have black hearts; rather, men only fear their hearts lack blood.
Even if one were to wash them until the bones were revealed, how could the marrow ever reach its proper time? Cherish this, O Vaiśālī!
Yuanli Ren (Garden Dweller). Gu Sihuoshuijian Meijie (Gazing at the Hair and Eyebrows in the Water Mirror):
Chan Master Lancishi of Daci, a native of the Zhang family of Zhongzhou. He first visited Master Ming of Shuanggui at Shizhuzi.
Later, he attended Master Zhang and passed through Hanzhong, where he established the Dharma at Jingming. Upon seeing his teaching and proclamations, [the Master’s] chest...
Next, he was suddenly enlightened; having received the seal of approval, he succeeded [his master] to the seat. When the Great King Myeongnam invited him to ascend the hall, [the Master said]:
"The universe is a single, perfect furnace; the sun and moon blaze alone in the center. Today, Jeongmyeong adds more charcoal, raising the tongs and hammer so that the intent is naturally relaxed.
The myriad phenomena display an auspicious luster; the three worthies and ten sages have their beaks and snouts all blunted. Copper-head...
An iron forehead is difficult to avoid; it has been refined until the entire body is free of a single speck. Therefore it is said: Prajñā is like a great mass of fire;
