As for Chan Master Bai Fu of Yüquan, he was the son of the Gōng family in Mèizhou. Having shaved his head and donned the dyed robes in his youth, he completed his period of inquiry and study.

He went to the forge of the Elder of Zhaojue and was thoroughly penetrated by his hammering; only then did he succeed to the lineage. He ascended the hall and said: "Face-to-face, I open wide the gate of non-duality.

Where the sentiments of sage and ordinary are exhausted, there is no distinction between the distant and the intimate. Phrases like hooks and thorns stir up wind and rain; they block the valleys and fill the ditches—what a tangle of vines!
But as for one who bows high to Śākyamuni and does not prostrate to Maitreya—who is this person? After a long silence...
It is said: "The ninety-day retreat has begun this very morning; I strip away the immortal kernel of the coiled peach.
Yushelu Shan Xisheng Chesheng (Mountain of Jade Conch, Silent Sound, Penetrating Eulogy) Chan Master was the son of the official Chen family from Anping County, Anshun Prefecture, Guizhou Province.
In his youth, he studied Confucian classics and possessed an intelligence that surpassed others. His family maintained an image of Bodhidharma, which the Master praised as follows: "Azure..."
Eyebrows like conch shells, a beard like a spiral; eccentric and strange, neither ordinary nor holy, as if foolish or deluded. At King Liang’s palace, his words failed to meet the mark;
he shifted his body and sat stiffly, his courage failing like that of a thief caught in the act. His family estate has been squandered, leaving not a single scrap of essence. How startling!
Just now he cast down a pair of sandals—one to the east and one to the west. The Master sought to leave the household life, but his parents would not permit it.

He built a hermitage by the side of their residence, abstained from meat and wine, and grew weary of worldly affairs. There he met Master Fuyan, who assigned him the *huatou* (meditation topic) of "The myriad dharmas return to One.
His state of doubt suddenly arose. Later, while traveling with his father on official duty to Zunyi, he went to Taoyuan Cave to pay his respects to Master Zhang.
The monk Xue’s wit and speech were in perfect accord with those of Master Zhang, who marveled at him, saying, "This lad is a truly fierce lion cub.
He then went to visit Master Minshu; as Min was about to speak, the Master stepped forward and covered Min’s mouth, then covered his own ears and departed.
Min remarked, "Truly a sharp instrument! After his parents passed away, the Master abandoned his home to enter the mountains, where he said: "As for all the patriarchs of the past..."

Each possesses both hand and eye. Whether it be a bell or a gong, a staff or a whisk—the Master takes a piece of wood about five inches long, with a rounded head and a pointed base, and names it "Attaining Joy" (*deluo*).
He composes a song for Attaining Joy and chants it daily while wielding the whip:
"Strike! Attain Joy! Strike! Attain Joy! You have one; I also have one. One has one; each and every one adds nothing more."
The whip! In the midst of busyness, one misses it all. Reflect carefully: let go, and you shall be joyful. Joyful in the morning, joyful in the evening;
though they call me mad, I am joyful; though they laugh at my folly and stubbornness, I am joyful.
In the midst of bustling crowds, I find joy; in the secluded forests, I find joy.
With a single lash, I am spun in circles; the great earth, mountains, and rivers come alive. I do not practice virtue, nor do I commit evil.
He did not compare lengths nor distinguish thicknesses; he would jest when he wished to jest and speak when he wished to speak.
But tell me, what was it he spoke of? "All conditioned phenomena are empty; it is better to let go and strike for joy. When a monk came, the Master would raise his whip and say, "Strike!
Strike! This continued for several years, and no one could understand him. Eventually, taking up his staff, he traveled on as a wandering monk, visiting famous mountains and great peaks everywhere.
Chuán (Chuan). He had many spiritual friends with whom he studied. He delved into the profound mysteries and exhausted the ultimate principles of the school’s tenets, never yielding to others.
Upon entering Shu, he went up to Zhaojue Temple where he met Master Zhangxue again. Zhang said, "It has been a long time since we last parted.
How are your daily activities? The Master replied, "I strike it with joy. Zhang said, "Bring that joy here. The Master raised his fist. Zhang said, "Set it aside."

[The Master] said, "This very one. The Master made the gesture of raising a whip. Changzong called out repeatedly, "How joyful! How joyful! At this, the Master attained great enlightenment and subsequently transmitted the Dharma to him.
Lumen Cheyan, the layman Peng, was a native of Jiangning. While serving as Governor of Yizhou, during his leisure time from attending to administrative affairs, he focused his mindfulness upon...

Having once grasped the essential meaning, he frequently sought out wise masters and patriarchs. Hearing that the lineage of Zhaojue was exceptionally austere, he entered the mountains to pay his respects and inquire about the essentials of the Dharma.
Under the pine trees, they reached a spiritual accord. One day, he again ascended to Zhaojue and asked:
"Han Yu’s visit to Dadian was still but the second level of seeing; what is the first level of seeing? Zhaojue replied: "The highest capacity."
"The pivot does not require a cone. The scholar said, "Since the strings of the pivot are of one kind, why did you drive out the Head Seat?
Juexian said, "I, this mountain monk, do not know how to engage in such tangled talk. The scholar said, "Please verify the truth of these sincere words, Master.
Juexian said, "This is precisely where you must let go of your body and life. Thereupon, the scholar’s doubts were resolved. Juexian presented him with a Guanyin cap and spoke a verse: Juexian.

The Sound-Cap: as vast as a leaning parasol, it covers and shelters the corners of the earth; its resonance pervades the three realms. Thus has the Dharma-lineage been transmitted for a thousand ages;
before the assembly of humans and devas, it is freely displayed and sold.
The Regional Commander Kunyu, Layman Zhang, whose name was De-di, was a native of Beizhi, Jingzhao.

Having governed Sichuan for many years, he had long aspired toward the Way and his devotion to the scriptural teachings grew ever more earnest. Once, while reading the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, upon reaching the passage, "All that has marks is empty and false," his mind and境 (the objective realm) were suddenly enlightened.
At that time, Master Chang was expounding the Dharma in Hannan; Layman Zhang admired his reputation for the Way and could not help but long for him.
I saw that during the Renyin year of the Kangxi era, Master Chang [Zhaojue] returned to Sichuan with his staff and took up residence at Taiping Temple in Jingguan.

A scholar-official came first to pay his respects and inquire about the Way; only then did the Master’s long-held aspirations find fulfillment. He immediately requested that the master open the Zhaojue Monastery to propagate its fundamental tenets.
One day, as the official’s carriage entered the mountains, he asked why he had come to seek instruction. The Master replied, "I have not begrudged you the transmission of the Way. Zhaojue...
Xuefeng said, "I am glad that you, Minister, have brought up this matter once more. It is difficult to point directly to the matter of one's own self.
The Layman asked, "Does the Venerable Master have the transmission of the lamp? Xuefeng said, "Who does not have a share? The Layman asked, "If so, do I, your disciple, have a share?
Xuefeng suddenly picked up his whisk and showed it to him, saying, "Do you understand? The Layman made a gesture as if to snatch it away. Xuefeng said, "Remember this clearly."
Take this up.
The layman Hu Shanguan of Shangshu was a native of Tushan in Yue.

Having formerly served as a judicial official in Sichuan, one day he accompanied the provincial governor and various officials to Zhaojue Temple, where they set out tables of fruit offerings. The layman said, "I request that the Master provide a single word; only then shall I dare to eat."
Cha (Tea). Jue said, "The weather is cool today; do not trouble yourself to provide further commentary. The Layman said, "Please turn the phrase once more. Jue set down his chopsticks.
One day, while playing the *qin*, Jue said, "Layman, you can only play that which has strings. Please perform a piece for me on that which has no strings.
The Layman said, "I request a tune for the stringless. Jue snapped his fingers. The Layman said, "That still belongs to the realm of 'having'. Jue— [remained silent].
Xuedou said, "If you have doubts, seek instruction elsewhere. Because he had seen the *Sūtra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas*, [the scholar] asked, "The names are here;
I do not know where the Dharmakāya dwells. Xuedou called out, "Master Hu! The scholar responded, "Yes? Xuedou asked, "Do you understand?

After the scholar prostrated and returned to his place standing, Xuedou tested him with the kōan of the Three Sages Repeatedly Offending the Unforgivable. The scholar immediately offered this verse: "Kill!"
When the monkey is exhausted, there is no need to seek; a thousand-layered iron wall is but a waste of effort.

It is his own power that invites disaster and provokes calamity—why must you go to the monks' quarters to question that monk? Jue then raised the *Ancestral Mind Seal* (Zuoshi Xin Yin) kōan once more to test him.
Shi composed two verses in succession: "The spring arrives and the plum blossoms naturally emit their fragrance; In the river city, the iron flute blows through the waning year. Amidst the snow..."
Seeking the plum blossoms, the blossoms are not to be found; where can the spring light be depicted? Furthermore, the entire great earth is a treasury of radiance;

the wind-blown sails bring laughter unto death. My Master had not a single word; with hands cast loose, he passed through the river city. Thus, like a needle meeting its eye, we were matched; he bestowed his seal of certification upon me.
With a staff of rabbit horns, I carry the fragrant waters of the ocean; with a rope of tortoise hair, I bind Mount Emei. I am now old in years.

It is difficult to gather up; fortunately, you have come to take up one shoulder of this burden. Tomorrow, by imperial decree, you shall be specially promoted to the post of Minister of the Ministry of Justice.
Layman Zhao Hai'an, whose name is Liangbi, was entering the jurisdiction as the Judicial Commissioner of Sichuan.

Hearing that Master Zhang’s spiritual influence was solitary and lofty, he wished to pay his respects. Upon arriving at his post, Master Zhang was taking a summer retreat on Mount Wuzhong; the layman dispatched a messenger with a satchel for the monk.

The Master requested a silk cap and robe. After the formal opening address had fully expressed his sincerity, he concluded by saying, "One helmet and one suit of armor—please return quickly to gather the remaining troops.
Upon reading the letter, the Master returned to the monastery and prepared a vegetarian feast. When the officer arrived and saw him, the Master brandished his staff as if wielding a spear;
the officer made a gesture of fear. The Master said, "A surrendered general is not executed. The officer replied, "I have long admired the Master."
"Such a capacity exists; today I have seen it directly. The Master said, "I must not let this pass. The scholar leaped with joy and performed a prostration.

Beyond his official duties, he constantly sought to penetrate the barriers of Zen. On the winter solstice of the Guiyou year, he visited Zhaojue and, under the guidance of Master Changzhe, turned over a new leaf and received certification.
He spoke this verse: "The nine-thousand-li Peng bird has just spread its wings; The hundreds of thousands of Buddhas..."
Intoxicated by the elegance of Chan, he grandly opened the Vajra Terrace upon the seashore to remain as a guardian for the foremost island of Saha.
Transcending these characters, he soared southward; his dharma name was Zheguan (Gallinule Hermit), and he was a *dhūta* practitioner. His lineage originated from Jiyang;
his ancestors were originally of the Ding clan from Haoliang, but because his grandfather traveled for official service, they eventually settled at Shiqiao in the capital city of Yan. He was born...
There was a character, "Kai" (開), inscribed upon his hand. The occipital bone at the back of his head protruded like a crescent moon facing upward.
When he was in his swaddling clothes, he would sometimes weep bitterly; whenever a nurse pointed toward an image of Gautama that had been offered, his crying would immediately cease.

Upon reaching the age of five, when playing with other children, he would sit cross-legged with palms joined and chant the name of the Buddha in a murmuring voice, commanding the children to bow in prostration before him. Later...
A man wearing a yellow cap passed by his door and, seeing him, said in astonishment, "You have come from Mount Song, yet you reside here?
At the age of twenty, you were among the students, pursuing the studies for the civil service examinations. You lived in simplicity with few friends and did not harmonize with worldly customs.

In your leisure time, you extensively studied the Buddhist scriptures and thoroughly investigated the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*). As you grew older and entered the official registers, you further delved into the schools of *dharmatā* and *lakṣaṇa*."

He did not inquire after his family’s affairs or their childbirths. Wherever he went, he would always consult and question his spiritual mentors, offering his wholehearted sincerity to seek their instruction.

In his daily life, he would simply sweep and clean a single room, sitting upright in meditation facing a wall upon a rush-cushion and cotton robe, his side never touching the mat, regardless of cold or heat.
He appeared entirely like an old Chan monk. Previously, he had been investigating the *huatou* "The Cypress Tree in Front of Zhaozhou’s Courtyard.
For seven days and nights, he had neglected both sleep and food, yet remained utterly without attainment; he even regretted not being dead.

One day, while walking by the edge of a pond, he leaned against the railing and stood for a moment. Suddenly, a carp leaped with a sharp *pala-la* sound, and he felt that the object which had long obstructed his chest dissolve away.
However, his doubts were resolved like ice melting away. He composed a verse, saying: "The pond water glistens, clear to its very bottom; Leaning on the railing, standing alone, I see the fish swim.
Suddenly hearing the 'pat-lat' sound as they dash across the waves, It causes my mindless self to take a start.

When Master Ding of Pingyan saw this, he laughed and said, "I am glad that your great matter has been thoroughly resolved from this point forward. Later, he went to Yizhou to pay his respects to Zhaojue Changzong.
The Master Xuezui asked, "From where have you come? Xuetao replied, "From the Capital. The Master said, "The road to Shu is more difficult than ascending to the blue heavens;
how did you manage to reach here? Xuetao said, "I am well-acquainted with the hoofprints of donkeys by the roadside.
The Master said, "Do you recognize this old monk? Xuetao said, "Before even entering the Jianmen Pass, I had already met the Master."
The Master said, "Where did you learn that empty talk? Dato replied, "Cold flowers drift in six petals; they form ice across the ground. The Master let it be.
One day during tea, the Master split a yellow tangerine with his hand and held it out to him, saying, "What kind of flavor is this?
Dato replied, "Old and decrepit as I am, I do not even know what sweet or sour is. The Master said, "In recent years..."
"The old monk’s teeth are missing; he swallowed the entire offering of *tōna* whole. Zhaozhou said, "Do not show off so much.
One day, he went to the Xianjue Hall and beheld the portraits of the two elders, Yuanwu and Poshan, as well as the portrait of Master Zhaozhou himself. As he gazed upon them in reverence...
Without bowing, he stood upright and pointed with his fingers one by one, saying, "This is so-and-so;
this is so-and-so. Zhaozhou said from the side, "I am glad you did not mistake them. Nanquan said, "Why do the patriarchs, fathers, sons, and grandsons sit together?
Zhaozhou said, "A poor man dotes on his child. Nanquan said, "When everyone is gathered in a circle, what are they discussing? Zhaozhou said, [nothing].
"Do not spread this news recklessly. Da said, "Indeed, there is a final destination. Chang said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice. One day, Chang assembled the community and ascended the seat;
he unrolled his hand-scroll and handed the whisk to Da. Da declined repeatedly, but when he could no longer refuse, he finally bowed and accepted it.
He spoke a verse: "Before the hall of Zhaojue, I watch the bright moon; The great ocean dries up, leaving but a single drop."
The ladle. A bamboo staff soars ninety thousand miles; from the back of empty space, one plucks tortoise hair.

As for the heart-fast (xinzhai), it penetrates the Way of the people of Lu; though they dwell constantly in rooms of wealth and honor, they observe that the world and the body are impermanent, like dreams and illusions.
Their only regret is not having met an enlightened person to point the way and dispel their doubts. Fortunately, having moved to Chengdu, he went to...
Zhaojue paid his respects to Master Zhang, saying, "I am fortunate to have met you in three lifetimes; I hope that the Master will bring me to ultimate realization.
Master Zhang said, "I am not free today; come back on another day. The scholar said, "Is there no expedient means? Master Zhang said, "Layman, pay your respects."
The old monk raised his hand. "How could there be no expedient means? He then instructed him to investigate the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature.
Without allowing his mind to be divided by wealth, status, children, or wife, he investigated with vigor without ceasing. After a long time, he attained realization.

His karmic conditions harmonized with those of Zhaojue, who recognized and certified his attainment. He spoke this verse: "Investigating Chan, one investigates until there is no handle; In the place where there is no handle..."
Just so—participate! A bright mirror stands upon the dais as the weather grows still; the Vajra sword emerges, its cold radiance piercing the Ox and Cow constellations.
Mikhing Rinpa, successor to Zhongxing Siding Chanshi, was born into the Liu clan of Jinchuan. He received the tonsure under Master Yanju and relied upon him...
Zhishi Shuanggui was a senior disciple of Pó Lǎrén; he was the successor of Kāifēng Mìxíng.

While traveling through Jīnchuān, the fourfold assembly requested him to preach the Dharma at Xīngguó Temple. Dēngyú attained thorough penetration of the source of the Dharma beneath his words, whereupon Mìxíng bestowed a verse upon him as a seal of approval.
He resided at Zhōngxīng Chányuàn in Luòyuán and held a retreat. At the request of the lay practitioner Wáng Xuāngōng, he ascended the hall to address the assembly.
Question: "Was Bodhidharma’s facing the wall and the Master’s ascending the seat the same or different? The Master said: "If they were different, they would not be the same;
if they were the same, they would not be different. The questioner pressed further: "Emperor Wu was sagely and wise; why did he fail to accord with the essential meaning? The Master said:
"It is because you have heard things by hearsay from the roadside. Question: "Before one's parents were born, what is the student's original face? The Master struck him.
The Master said, "Blind fellow, why do you prattle in your sleep? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him repeatedly with his staff and drove him out, then said:
"The auspicious air urges on the yellow birds; the bright light turns the green duckweed. If you understand the matter of today, you will not be ignorant of your original person.
Since the assembly has understood the matter of today, who is your original person? Have you not heard it said: 'Above heaven and below heaven, only...'"
"Am I alone the Honored One? This refers to the Original Source of Life (benming yuanchen) of the Layman Xuangong today, prior to the birth of his parents.
If you can understand this, then you will understand the Original Source of Life within each person.
If you understand the Original Source of Life within each person, then you will understand Bodhidharma’s wall-gazing and today’s ascending of the seat by Zhongxing; otherwise, they are not the same.

Regarding the principle that "where there is sameness, there is no differentiation," [the Master] let out a sudden shout. At the sound of the shout, a monk fell over in shock. The Master said, "How excellent!
A patch-robed monk turns upon being given a single nudge. He then descended from his seat.
The Chan Master Hui-xian of Hua was a native of Hengzhou Prefecture. He received the Dharma lineage from Master Mi-xing Ren.

Later, observing that the world was in decline and the Way was becoming thin, he took no pleasure in those who produced such "insects" [of commentary]. He left behind only verses on ancient cases (*songgu*) for circulation in the world:

"Before descending from Tushita, he already entered the royal palace; Before emerging from his mother’s womb, his work of saving beings was complete. (Verse: "Originally, it was but one level and straight path."

To wander aimlessly through the world is but a steep and perilous path; how much better it is to retire in seclusion beyond the thousand peaks, lying down to watch the twin wheels of the sun and moon turn across the vast void.
The World-Honored One held up a flower. (Verse: Raising waves against the current, his spirit is far-reaching; He overturns the Milky Way, leaving no trace behind.
The Yellow River flows in nine bends toward the Eastern Sea; even now, its sands roll at the bottom. The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye is like a flake of snow in a red furnace;
the Separate Transmission outside the Teachings is like the *huqia* flute of the barbarians in an autumn frontier pass.

Mahākāśyapa is truly worthy of pity. The Goose King chooses his milk, knowing it is not duck’s; how could one who paints a foot know it does not look like a snake? “This very mind is Buddha. (Verse: Lips and mouth—two.
A single skin; a set of teeth and bones. Jiangxi’s Horse Winnowing Basket releases a falcon from the vast heavens.
Baizhang’s second visit to Mazu. (Verse: The thunder is great, yet there are no raindrops. Deaf ears and a protruding tongue; an old maid seeing her servant.
This refers to the school of the Jiangxi lineage. One does not realize that there are a thousand differences and ten thousand errors.

When Ling Xingpo visited Fubei, and when Nanquan and Zhaozhou engaged in their dialogues—(Verse): Grasping her hair and rushing to the yamen, she brings the enemy upon herself; Nanquan and Zhaozhou are laden with cangues and shackles.

Master Shiqin Wen, a successor of the Dharma lineage of Yanguan, was a native of a neighboring county in Sichuan. From birth he possessed exceptional intelligence; at the age of seven, when he began his formal education, he took leave of his parents to study Buddhism.
He received the tonsure under Master Zide on East Mountain in Tóngliáng. Subsequently, he traveled as a pilgrim to lecture halls and attended various Zen assemblies.
Master De-fa Yan-ju resided at the Yongmen [Monastery] in Guiyang. He presided over seven dharma centers in total, including Kaizhou Fude Monastery.
When Prefect Wen invited him to ascend the hall, he asked: "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master said:
"News from the Northern Sea has been cut off; on the Southern Mountain, spring rains bring forth the fragrance of flowers.

"How is it that the scene is taken away but not the person? The Master said: "The setting sun sinks in the west, the mountain light grows faint; the horse-head turns eastward, the spirit for wine runs deep.
"How is it that both person and scene are taken away? The Master said: "Spirits vanish as the solitary sail capsizes upon the cliffs and islands; the bowels break with grief at Juyong Pass."
The horse neighed. [The student asked: "How is it that both the person and the environment are not taken away? The Master said: "Guests have not yet dispersed within the towers of the singing halls;
the moon first rises upon the roads of Changgan. He then said: "To raise an eyebrow is already too late; to shake one's sleeves is still too slow. To walk while blinking the eyes—"
Both person and environment are stripped away. If one were within the domain of a patch-robed monk, there might be a slight margin for comparison;
but as for the matter that transcends the patch-robed monk, he looks to his left and right and says: "Investigate! (Chán).

Master Lin Yu, a Dharma heir of Master Wen of Lingyin, was a native of Shu. At the age of twenty, he shaved his head and received the tonsure; after completing his full ordination, he traveled extensively to visit various masters until he reached Huilong.
There, under the shout of Master Lingyun, he realized his true home and subsequently received certification of his enlightenment. He resided at Manao Mountain in Yuanzhou.
At Kuyan, he ascended the hall and said: "A man of the true lineage has no openings; he is a ready-made wooden puppet.

There is no need to question him further for what is essential. One must strictly avoid opening one's mouth. Before the gates of the mouth are even parted by the soul, the path through the weeds is cut off for all people.

Even before the pivot of action, empty space has already laughed. Why do you dally with such hollow pretenses? How many people with clear eyes have there been throughout antiquity? It is truly excessive."
Lan-dang. Fearing neither shame nor embarrassment, he utters only cries of despair. A single heart of crimson, two pieces of skin; with forced words, one phrase contains the Three Mysteries.
His beard and hair are entirely white, yet it is said that "one mystery possesses the three essentials. With beard and hair entirely white, the ancient public cases have long been established.
"Shang Da Ren" (The Great Person of Shang). Today, with sincere diligence, he adds fodder and feed. "Transforming the Three Thousand"—this is the first.
The first essential: Treading upon the two ends of a hempen rope, the Persian suspects it to be a red-spotted snake;
by day and under the blue sky he holds up a lamp to look—seeing the strange as not strange. The second essential: A toad leaps upon the Diamond Eye;
with one blow it is shattered and offered to the Empty King—it turns out to be a hawk from Silla after all; pressing the eyes, flowers bloom. The third essential: An iron brazier boils...
Tea is not the same as the kettle. Samantabhadra lost his white elephant king; the local deity comes before one to seek a prognostic stalk.

Seeking horns on a horse’s head—this saying is heard by all ears throughout the various quarters. When the water of the eastern ravine flows into the western ravine, everyone understands how to shift the register and turn the melody.

Chan Master Miyin was the son of the Li family in Xuzhou Prefecture, southern Sichuan. From childhood, he did not consume alcohol or meat.

Contemplating the world and the body as illusory transformations, he took the step of renouncing the mundane. Upon the passing of his two parents, he went to Guanyin Cave to shave his head and don the robes of a monk.
He received full ordination from Master Yushong and received the transmission of the Dharma from Chan Master Wen of Lingyin.

He resided at Huilong Chan Monastery in Huigong, Hubei. During the opening of the retreat, he ascended the hall and said: "Smoke hangs across the ferry crossing; it has its own origins. Snow covers the reeds..."
How could these flowers bear the omens? Like a clear thunderclap that shakes the earth, they overturn stagnation on the banks; like the pivot of a swift wind, they sweep away all dust and haze.
Brocade clouds disperse together as a single radiant orb emerges from the sky of nature (*dharmadhātu*);

embroidered vapors vanish simultaneously as the myriad dharmas are fully revealed within the ocean of wisdom (*prajñā*). Rice in the bowl, water in the bucket—everywhere light is emitted. The fence of outflows...
The stainless ladle manifests auspicious signs in every object. Only when one reaches such a state does one realize that the immovable site of enlightenment pervades the ten directions;

there, conditions do not cling and the essence merges with the great void. If the thousand Buddhas were to open their mouths, they would immediately err; if the myriad sages were to extend their hands, they would likewise be mistaken.

Chan Master Pofeng Chong of Longzou Temple in Jiading Prefecture, heir to the dharma robe and teachings of Huijue, was a native of the Yue clan of Nanchong. He was the son of Menglong, a jinshi degree holder.

A descendant of [his] lineage, he was grave and majestic in his demeanor. Having returned from traveling extensively to consult various masters, he sought certification from the Venerable Huìjué. Ascending the hall, he said:
"As for this single staff—throughout the three periods of time, even all the Buddhas can do nothing with it; through successive generations, even all the patriarchs can do nothing with it.
Today, as I hold it in my hand, I wish to gouge out sores upon healthy flesh. He struck it once and set it down.
[The Master] ascends the hall. Old Śākyamuni established the three periods [of retreat] to harmonize the mind and set up the red furnace to smelt the nature.
But tell me, how is the mind to be harmonized? How is the nature to be smelted? Examine this! Ascends the hall.
Śākyamuni spoke what was not spoken; the fierce winds of Vairambha blow over the seas and mountains. Kāśyapa heard what was not heard; the green mountains are reduced to mere dust. Leaving behind—
One turning word: "The tongue is inside the mouth. [He] ascends the hall and says: "The Great Way is level and plain; there is no arising and no falling.
When the true mechanism is proclaimed, what is there to untie or to knot? [He] ascends the hall and sits silently. Suddenly, he speaks out loud:
"Assembly, do not recklessly engage in forced interpretation! He slaps his own mouth and says: "The mouth is the gate of calamity. He descends from the seat.
Foyu Yuzhanshi of Yuzhou was the son of the Fan family of Jiazhou. At the age of ten, he paid homage to Master Huijiao and received the tonsure.

Upon observing a corpse, he attained a profound realization. In responding to others and engaging in debate, his wit was sharp and swift; he remained by the master’s side as his attendant, carrying the water pitcher and towel.
He never displayed an expression of indolence. Once he said to a Zen practitioner: "The clear and distinct phrase is not obscure; with nose straight and brows arched, how many have missed it?

It is only because this manifest reality is difficult to discern that Zen practitioners travel across thousands of mountains and ten thousand waters. He then composed a verse on the plum blossom: With its fragrance wafting through the cold, It stands alone amidst the frost. Though the branches are sparse and the petals few, Its spirit fills the world. Even if the moonlight is bright, It cannot compare to its brilliance. If you wish to know the mind of the ancient sages, Look at this flower blooming in the snow.
With ice-like skin and snow-like bones, he has long harbored the cinnabar heart. What he spits forth causes others to look with close attention.
His true color was not borrowed from peach or apricot blossoms; a single curtain of shimmering stars adorns the jade balustrade.

Taking it as his duty to support the monastic community and making filial service to his master his core concern, when Venerable Huijue passed away in the autumn of the Gui-chou year of the Kangxi era, he was so overcome by grief that he became skeletal, his very breath and rest [devoted to mourning].

As was suspected, on the anniversary of the Buddha’s attainment of enlightenment that year, he manifested a slight ailment. He refused to take medicine, and after seven days had passed, having finished bidding farewell to the assembly and entrusting them with his final instructions, he closed his eyes at midday and passed away.

Daohou, the Dharma heir of Chan Master Huoling Shun, was the son of the Li family of Luyang. He descended into the world in the Gengwu year of the Chongzhen era. As a child, he suffered from many illnesses;
whenever he saw a monk, he would rejoice. Upon reaching the age of six, because his maternal uncle had become a monk at Tongshan, he followed him there to take refuge.
He became a monk. Later, he went to the seat of Master Yunfeng Tizong on Mount Fangshan to receive full ordination.
There he heard that Master Dahou was opening the Dharma at Dingxing in Hongyang, so he set out directly for that place with his staff and alms bowl. Dahou said, "I have a junior second seat;

if you can utter a single word of the Way, I will invite you [to take his place]. Ling said, "Please let the Master try to pose a question. Dahou said, "In the past, the World-Honored One held up a flower."
Kāśyapa smiled. "What is the meaning of this? Lingyun said, "When the Way prevails, the Emperor’s edict is not transmitted; when the times are clear, one need not sing songs of great peace.

Xuanhou nodded in approval and was subsequently appointed to the position of West Hall Attendant. Upon the conclusion of the retreat, Master Xuanhou granted him formal certification (inka), saying in verse:
"When the Way prevails, the Emperor’s edict is not transmitted; In a state of carefree ease, there is no need to deliberate over right and wrong. The head of the rope has leaked through."
He withdrew from public view. Returning after subduing dragons at the Great Sea and wearing the crescent moon upon his brow, he subsequently resided at Jinchuan Lingying to rest in tranquility.
Because Master Yunfeng Xiaoxu was about to pass away, he issued a written testament to the officials and gentry;

together with the common people, they petitioned him to become the abbot of Yunfeng to succeed to the seat. Within a few years, he passed away peacefully. His stupa was erected on the western ridge of Yunfeng.

Chan Master Yuchun Zhi was the son of the Huang family of Yibin. At the age of sixteen, after both his parents had passed away, he went to Mount Emei to pay respects to Master Tirong and receive the tonsure.
He subsequently traveled south with companions to study the exegesis of the sutras and śāstras, before returning to Sichuan to propagate the teachings.
Later, while in the city of Yucheng, he encountered Master Dahou, who asked him, "What sutra do you lecture on, Preceptor? The Master replied:
Fahua and Lengyan Hou said, "The scriptures state: 'This Dharma cannot be shown; words and signs are quiescent. How do you explain this?
The Master replied, "At this point, I have no opening for speech. Hou said, "If that is so, you cannot even serve as a slave to a Dharma teacher.
He then abandoned his reliance on the teachings and scriptures. Later, he received the prediction of enlightenment and resided at Guiyuan in Jingzhou Prefecture.

At the Fragrant Pavilion, he ascended the hall. When there was questioning and answering, it was like gouging a sore on healthy flesh; when there was no questioning and no answering, it was like choking off the throat.

If one discusses speech and silence, movement and stillness, raising the eyebrows or blinking the eyes, clenching the fist or pointing a finger, or the mutual exchange of staff and shout—set all that aside to one side.
But what then? Striking the meditation desk with his whisk, he said: "On both banks is stillness; the mountain of benevolence is like a tiger."
A single stream stirs the water of wisdom like a dragon; the mud-bull at the bottom of the sea performs a somersault. Startling the Persian merchant, he breaks the bell.
The Chan Master Sanfeng Ban-shui was the son of the Yu family of Baxian. He received the *śīla* (precepts) from Chan Master Shigou.

I received the Seal Verse from Master Dahou in the winter of the Bingwu year of the Kangxi era. On the occasion of opening the furnace for the retreat, he ascended the hall and held up his staff, saying:
"A seven-foot black cane, a tortoise-nosed snake; it soars through the universe and brings auspiciousness to the Three Baha regions.

It wanders far through the marketplace, yet few people can see it; even upon close inspection, it has not yet reached home. He dropped the staff, let out a shout, and ascended the hall to expound the fundamental source.
Entering retreat, this mind is truly excellent; for twenty-one days in continuous succession, the incense of the ninefold concentration burns.
Sitting until the break of dawn and the dead of night, there is nothing ordinary or mundane to deliberate upon.
Chan Master Lin Wujian of Jingyang, the Dharma heir of Master Yian, initially used the three studies to guide the assembly. Later, he studied under Master Yian and began to succeed him on the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Churning the long river into butter and milk—what a pity to call a bell a jar! Transforming the great earth..."
To turn it into gold—what difference is there from proving a tortoise to be a turtle? A single phrase: eyes askance and nose straight; a horse’s face is not a bull’s head.
Should you hesitate or pause your activity, you cannot avoid being like one who guards the stump waiting for a hare.
Again, Master Guoqing Zhong of Nanyang ascended the hall and said: "Everyone carries the bright moon pearl; every person embraces the jade of Mount Jing. At times, the ten thousand virtues..."
Yan. At times he wore robes of grass and ate from the woods; sometimes he manifested his seclusion in the city of Vaiśālī, and at other times he displayed his birth in the kingdom of Krakucchanda.
He turned the wheel of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and held the scales of the patch-robed monks’ nostrils. [He] suddenly raised his whisk and said:
Setting aside for a moment the weighing of Buddhas and Patriarchs, what is the very core of a monk’s realization? [As he] descended from his seat, he struck them apart with his staff.
Shengke Yu was his dharma heir.

The Second Patriarch of Huayan at Chan Master Huanchu’s Monastery, with the protection of the Prince of Duchi from the Chongqing Prefecture, requested that he ascend the hall on the Buddha’s Birthday.
“The World-Honored One carved open the primordial chaos; Yunmen forged stones to mend the heavens.
Though there was not even a hair’s breadth of leakage, there still remained the constellations, the sun, and the moon. While it is true that their merit in battle was high, [the Master] returned.”
"Do you see the Great Peace? For now, let us rejoice that today is free from affairs. [The Master] struck his whisk and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Nan-zhi Jing was the son of the Deng family of Wan County. In his childhood, he paid respects to Master Heng-xiu and received the tonsure.
He received full ordination under Master Min-shu. Hearing that Master Sheng-ke was opening a dharma center at Fahua Rock, he stayed with him for twenty years.
In another year, Master Sheng entered the room and asked, "The boundless ocean of lands has neither self nor other separated by even the tip of a hair.
Why is it that the person inside the hermitage does not know what is outside the hermitage? The Master replied, "Publicly, a needle cannot pass; privately, a carriage and horse may go through.
Sheng said, "Ten generations of past and present, from beginning to end, do not depart from this very thought-moment. Why is it that one does not know tomorrow today?"
The Master said: "Where there is water, it contains the moon; where there is no mountain, it does not bear clouds. Saint (Xuedou) said: "This is the very bottom of Xuefeng’s teaching.
While serving as the Head Seat, Saint was commanded by the Abbot to preside over the *bǐngfú* (dharma-rod) small assembly. Upon the level ground of reality, he picked up a single thread.
Why is it that all the people of the great earth lose their wits and are rendered tongue-tied? Tell me, where does the point of benefit and harm lie? Do you understand this thoroughly?
It is as large as a mustard seed and yet as fine as Mount Sumeru; it is as soft as iron and as hard as mud. It is never apart from the four modes of deportment, yet alas, people do not recognize it.

The Master said, "I am no expert at being a guest; I trouble the host for nothing. The World-Honored One saw only the sharpness of the chisel's tip, but did not see the squareness of the chisel's head.
Although Kāśyapa’s correct command was being put into practice, in the end, a few could not withstand the many. At that time—
If the Elder Jing were present at that time, when the World-Honored One asks you, "Whom do you wish to expel, Mañjuśrī?

you should simply raise the mallet and say, "Which fellow is no man of spirit? and strike it. Not only would Mañjuśrī be left with nowhere to hide his shame, but even Śākyamuni would have no opening to speak. Do you understand this fully?

His transformation first startled the multitude.
At fifteen years of age, Master Hong of Zizhong at Longxing Temple in Hanzhou took the step of renouncing worldly dust.

He paid homage to Master Ziming to receive the tonsure and full ordination, and traveled extensively to consult with venerable elders. Upon hearing of the school of Venerable Shengke of Huayan, he [sought him out].

The wind blew fiercely, and he rushed down from the duster (the whisk) to clarify the mind-ground. Longxing ascended the hall: "The earth is cold, the sky is freezing, and the grasses and trees are withered;
heaps of yellow leaves fill the steps and courtyards. When the monks beneath the forest encounter this moment, they leap and dance, manifesting their majesty to realize the Patriarchal Chart.
Is there anyone who can do so? Is there anyone? He asked: "For what reason does a bhikṣu of pure conduct not take birth in the heavenly realms, while one who breaks the precepts [does]?"
The monk asked, "For what reason does one not enter hell? The Master said, "Willow trees by the waters north of Wei; evening clouds over the Yangtze east of Jiang.
The monk asked, "What is the seamless stupa? The Master remained silent. The monk pressed further, "Who is inside the stupa? The Master then gave a shout.
The monk continued, "A tree a thousand fathoms high—when its leaves fall, they return to the root. The Master said, "I shall give you a good kick beneath the heels!"

[The Master] said: "Thirty. Danxia burned the wooden Buddha simply because the cold had penetrated to his very bones; the head monk’s eyebrows and whiskers fell out because of a single thought of resentment.
This is precisely when the palace is moved and the throne changed, and the cold air mingles—how does this stand in the station of a patch-robed monk?
[He] struck his staff and said: 'Does the assembly understand? If you do not, I shall spin a web of complications for you.'"
Master Zhuhangjun entered the Nanji Hall. As he personally offered incense, he said, "The one who is direct—this one is direct!

At that moment, the *vinaya-dhara* (ritual master) asked, "What is this 'one who is direct'? Master Hangjun gave a shout. The ritual master said, "Master Hangjun is among those who follow the Buddha-dharma;
why do you vent such anger? Master Hangjun said, "Do you take my shouting to be venting anger? The ritual master also shouted. Master Hangjun shouted twice in succession.
[The Master] shouted, "The hook is in the ground of non-doubt. He called to those on his left and right, saying, "Recognize this monk!
The Master continued, "Great assembly, look at these two men! They raise both seizing and letting go simultaneously; killing and giving life are manifested together.

Even so, they cannot avoid falling into a trap of words. How can they compare to today’s Star and Dipper? Layman Yun, with your无缘慈 (unconditioned compassion), you have given rise to a vast and great mind."
I have come here to provide a meal for the Sangha and to gloriously propagate the Dharma transformation. At this very moment, how do you speak that single phrase of "killing or giving life"?
Holding the Mohe sword crosswise, one fully maintains the correct command; throughout the realm of Great Peace, the foolish and stubborn are executed.
Chan Master Fākōngzhèng succeeded Master Shèng of Huáyán. He resided at Lái Fèng Chan Monastery in Tōngshān, Lúzhōu. Upon ascending the hall for the formal discourse, a monk asked:
"The spring breeze pervades all realms and is difficult to gather; the myriad phenomena all return within a single mirror. What is the pure *dharmakāya*? The Master said:
"The earth is fertile, so the winter melon is large. The monk pressed further: "Purity and defilement together form the Land of Peace and Bliss."
"Sages and ordinary people are not separated by even a hair's breadth. What is the Perfect Reward Body? The Master said, "The belly of a hungry man is wide.
The student asked, "Wherever there are green willows, one can tether a horse; every household has a road leading to Chang'an. What is the thousand-billion Transformation Bodies?
The Master said, "A native watching a walking lantern. The student asked, "What is the meaning of this?"
The Master said, "Coming and going are distinct. He then planted his staff in the ground and said, "If it accords with the bright side, it must accord with the dark side;
in the four directions and eight points, one may act as one pleases. The Buddha of the Sun’s Face, the Buddha of the Moon’s Face—what thing is this joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure?
How many people in the world are like those who wait by the stump! They all retreat in the middle of the way. Little do they realize that one must lift up the tongs of the Ultimate."
Employing a hand and eye that transcend the mundane, all the sages alike stand in the shadow [of his influence]. The Three Worthies cannot even catch a glimpse of him. Thus it is said:
"The True Pure Dharma-realm is the foundation of spiritual intelligence and the root of cosmic transformation. It smelts and refines the two polarities of heaven and earth;

it acts as the crucible and hammer for the myriad existences. Vast, it has no exterior; minute, it has no interior. It is the reason why the ten thousand phenomena arise and the reason why the five musical notes are formed. Furthermore...
Zhuo leaned on his staff and said, "I venture to ask the assembly: ultimately, what kind of body is this? Divine heads and ghostly faces manifest themselves as they will;
whether in heaven or among men, let each be honored as you wish. He gave a shout.

Chan Master Yanchan of Longyan Fushí in Jiānwei received the seal of approval from Master Shèng of Huārán. Residing at Longyan, he ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the matter that transcends [the ordinary]?
The Master said, "Your heels must touch the ground. The monk stepped forward and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Digging a hole to search for a snake. The monk asked further, "What is the meaning of the single sandal returning to the West?"...
[The student] expressed his intent to leave. The Master said, "Run barefoot. He then said, "The meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Sages are precisely the meaning of ordinary people.

Between ordinary beings and sages, how could there be two different kinds? Simply exhaust the mind of the ordinary; apart from this, there is no separate 'sage-understanding. Follow conditions with ease and let go;
follow your nature in carefree wandering. You are liberated right now. Within these words, there is one principle and two meanings. If a person can discern them, it will not hinder [their progress].
Within the Buddha-dharma, there is a place for the person. If this is not yet so, do not say you have no doubts. (He strikes the meditation staff and descends from the seat.
Chan Master Jiannan Xian of Ciyun Monastery was the son of Liu of Puyang. His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations. Due to the events of the Jia-shen year...
During the period of upheaval, he was mixed among the warhorses for many years, yet he constantly harbored the aspiration to transcend the mundane world.

In the province of Dian, he received the tonsure and full ordination under Master Gūyuè. Following his preceptor back to Yucheng in Shu, he established the Baiyang Monastery to restore the ancestral temple.

Over twenty years had passed, and [the temple] was resplendently renewed. Because his own teacher had passed away early, in the winter of the Bingchen year of the Kangxi era, he heard that Master Shengke was founding Huayan Temple.
He traveled there on straw sandals to pay his respects and intended to take up residence at the mountain. He presented a record of his *songgu* (verses on ancient cases) for inspection;
Master Shengke tested him by raising a *gong'an* to see if his realization was genuine, and subsequently, on behalf of Master Gurye, he conferred upon him the seal of transmission.
There are ancient verses (gū) on mountain dwelling that have circulated in the world; I shall now select several of them to certify what I have attained.

When the World-Honored One was first born, [a verse says]: Pointing at heaven, pointing at earth—what does he intend to plot? He acts as if there were no one beside him, his courage and spirit coarse.

Master Shangsheng was the son of the Duan family of Zhugong. During the late Ming dynasty, he served as a lieutenant general before entering Mount Yanghuan to receive the tonsure and full ordination under the Vinaya Master Chongxu.
He traveled to Yuzhou to visit Master Sheng of Huayan, under whose whisk and fly-whisk he attained numerous insights into the fundamental principle.
As a token of his realization, Huayan presented him with a bamboo hat and a verse, which began: "The object upon this old monk’s head..."
This is the common way of human affairs. With the exception of one who is a son capable of supporting his family, [the dharma] must not be lightly bestowed upon others.
After receiving the seal of mind-transmission, he remained strict in regulating his own conduct. Later, he resided at Guiting and Jinao, and subsequently moved to Chongfu.
In the summer of the *renshen* year, he passed away without illness. His chief disciple, Nianshe Yue, who had attained the Dharma, erected a stupa for him on the eastern ridge of Huayan.
Buhui Xing was the son of the Wang family of Yingshan. Encountering the chaos of the Shu region, he fled to Chu, where he received the tonsure under Master Dangshan of Xiangyan.
After completing his full ordination, he traveled extensively with Master Shengke to visit various teachers. He attained realization upon hearing a single word from them;
from then on, his spontaneous responses were unyielding. One day, Shengke said: "Set aside all talk of barbarians and Han people. Before your parents..."
Before his death, Kewen said a single phrase; Huo immediately struck him with his palm. Kewen said, "Too coarse, sir.
Huo struck him again. Kewen then withdrew. Later, Yinyuan wrote a verse: "The osmanthus tree was poisoned by Yao, yet it still bears five scars upon its face today.
Though he has shaken it for ten years, his heart remains unyielding; resentment meets only with the person who seeks vengeance. He returned to Shu and resided at Xiaoshan in Hanzhou.
Master Quan ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Before one's parents were born, what is the student's original face?
The Master said, "The eyes are horizontal and the nose is straight. The monk pressed further, "Once dead and cremated, where is the face and body? The Master struck him. The monk continued:
"Does this allow you students to separately communicate the news? The Master struck again and said, "In the land of lush willows and fragrant grasses, stroll about as you please.
He looked at the assembly and asked, "Do you understand? If you do not, today I shall certainly communicate the news to you all separately.
He dragged his staff down from the seat and returned to the abbot's quarters. Sitting upright, he passed away. The assembly did not see him for the midday meal.

The Master emerged from his room; shaking him, he found him already still. Only then did the entire assembly realize that the words spoken today were intended as a definitive message to be conveyed elsewhere.
His stupa was erected at his home mountain.
Chan Master Zhiyun Xiao was the son of the Li family from Xintan. At the age of twenty, he received the tonsure under Master Sheng of Huayan, where he immediately completed his full ordination.
He studied under Master Tianyin of Chonghua for many years before returning to Huayan, where he served as a monastic administrator (*gangwei*) for several years.
He once composed a verse on Deshan’s bowl-carrying, which reads: "Pressing through empty space, the withered tree blossoms; The one who composed this is [Zhiyun]."
Meeting face-to-face at the two houses; though each possesses the eye atop the head, the jade is naturally flawless, yet it has a flaw.

naked and bare, she is like gold refined a hundred times. If a monk acts beyond his station, when will he emerge from the Iron Ring City? (Again: A priceless jewel.

His understanding is majestic and grand—this is the pure *dharmakāya*.
